JISHUMI:v1p537/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p537/r1.claim: من may be partitive or an emphatic extra particle; آية is genitive after it.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r1.anchor: (من) في قوله: من آية قيل: للتبعيض

JISHUMI:v1p537/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p537/r3.claim: Polytheists mocked Muhammad for changing commands and claimed his words contradicted each other; the verse was revealed in response.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r3.anchor: روي أن المشركين قالوا: ألا ترون إلى محمد يأمر أصحابه بأمر ثم ينهاهم عنه

JISHUMI:v1p537/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r4.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v1p537/r4.claim: ʿAli ibn ʿIsa links the verse with the preceding one: although Jews disliked revelation, God continues sending what is best for them.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r4.anchor: أبدا ينزل ما هو أصلح لهم [*]، عن علي بن عيسى

JISHUMI:v1p537/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p537/r5.claim: Abu Muslim says that after recounting Jewish objections to Muhammad, God explains the permissibility of abrogating a prescribed law.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r5.anchor: نسخ شريعة كانت مفروضة - بين الله تعالى جواز ذلك ردا عليهم، عن أبي مسلم

JISHUMI:v1p537/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p537/r6.claim: Since an ayah itself is not abrogated, the wording has an omitted object: its ruling, recitation, or preservation.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r6.anchor: قيل: في الكلام حذف؛ لأن الآية لا تنسخ، فإما أن تريد حكم آية أو تلاوة آية، أو حفظ آية

JISHUMI:v1p537/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r7.speaker: الحسن وأكثر أهل العلم
JISHUMI:v1p537/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and most scholars understand nasakh as removal or abrogation.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r7.anchor: النسخ الذي هو الرفع، عن الحسن وأكثر أهل العلم

JISHUMI:v1p537/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r8.speaker: عطاء وسعيد بن المسيب
JISHUMI:v1p537/r8.claim: ʿAtaʾ and Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab understand nasakh as copying or transcribing.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r8.anchor: النسخ الذي هو من نسخت الكتاب، عن عطاء وسعيد بن المسيب

JISHUMI:v1p537/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r9.speaker: الحسن وأبو علي والأصم
JISHUMI:v1p537/r9.claim: They say “abrogate” removes a ruling while retaining its recitation, whereas “cause to be forgotten” removes the recitation.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r9.anchor: فحملوا ننسخ على نسخ الحكم دون التلاوة، وننسها على نسخ التلاوة

JISHUMI:v1p537/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p537/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says abrogating an ayah replaces it, so the second ruling abrogates the first; leaving it unchanged means it remains binding.

JISHUMI:v1p537/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p537/r11.claim: Nisyan is the opposite of remembering: a meaning departs from the mind.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r11.anchor: والنسيان: نقيض الحفظ، وهو ذهاب المعنى عن النفس

JISHUMI:v1p537/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p537/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p537/r12.claim: Qadir and Qadir are synonymous, though one is more emphatic; God is powerful in Himself without limit and cannot be incapable.
JISHUMI:v1p537/r12.anchor: وقدير وقادر بمعنى، غير أن في قدير مبالغة للعدول، وهو تعالى قدير لذاته، يقدر من كل جنس، وفي كل وقت على ما لا يتناهى، ولا يجوز عليه العجز

ITQAN:v2p305#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r9.anchor:
﴿ قلوبنا غلف ﴾ في غطاء
1515 ﴿ ما ننسخ ﴾ نبدل

ITQAN:v2p305#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r10.claim: ننسها means leave it without replacing it.
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r10.anchor:
﴿ ما ننسخ ﴾ نبدل
1516 ﴿ أو ننسها ﴾ نتركها فلا نبدلها

BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r1.claim: The direct question to the Prophet affirms that God can abrogate a ruling and replace it with an equal or better one.
BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r1.anchor: الخطاب للنبي عليه السلام ومعنى الاستفهام تقرير أي : أنك تعلم

BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r2.claim: Although the address includes everyone, the Prophet is singled out because no human knows more of these realities; prophetic knowledge dwarfs that of saints and all creation.
BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r2.anchor: وخصه عليه السلام بالخطاب مع أن غيره داخل في الخطاب أيضا حقيقة بناء على أن المقصود من الخطاب تقرير علم المخاطب

BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r7.claim: Knowing God's power, sovereignty, and guardianship should yield certainty that He chooses what is best for believers, with trust, reliance, and surrender despite disbelievers' doubts about abrogation.
BURSEVI:v1p160#2/r7.anchor: هو الجزم والإيقان بأنه تعالى لا يفعل بهم في أمر من أمور دينهم أو دنياهم إلا ما هو خير لهم والعمل بموجبه

ASAD-NOTES:2:intro/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:intro/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:intro/r4.claim: The reference to earlier messages being superseded by the revelation to Muhammad is pivotal; Qur'anic law follows from it and continues God's ethical guidance in accord with human nature.
ASAD-NOTES:2:intro/r4.anchor: a direct consequence of that pivotal statement

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r1.claim: The apparent analysis makes conditional ما the fronted object of ننسخ, meaning whatever we abrogate, like أيا ما تدعوا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r1.anchor: أحدهما - وهو الظاهر - أنها مفعول مقدم لننسخ

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r2.claim: An alternative makes conditional ما a verbal noun, with من آية as object: whatever abrogation of an āya we make.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنها شرطية أيضا جازمة لننسخ، ولكنها واقعة موقع المصدر

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r3.claim: An anonymous poem beginning نعب الغراب supports the source-noun use of ما.

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r4.claim: Critics object that the analysis leaves the result without a resumptive pronoun returning to the conditional noun; they also object that من is not extra in affirmative conditions.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r4.anchor: وقد رد هذا القول بعضهم بشيئين، أحدهما: أنه يلزم خلو جملة الجزاء من ضمير يعود على اسم الشرط

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r5.speaker: ابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ننسخ with ḍamma on the prefix and kasra on sīn, from أنسخ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر: " ننسخ " بضم النون وكسر السين من أنسخ

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r6.speaker: أبو حاتم
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r6.claim: Abū Ḥātim calls Ibn ʿĀmir’s reading an error; al-Samīn rebukes his habitual audacity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r6.anchor: قال أبو حاتم: " هو غلط " وهذه جرأة منه على عادته

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r7.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī says this reading is neither a dialectal synonym of نسخ nor causative, but means ‘whatever we find abrogated’; this entails abrogation, so meanings agree.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r7.anchor: وقال أبو علي: ليست لغة لأنه لا يقال: نسخ وأنسخ بمعنى، ولا هي للتعدية

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the hamza as causative, with Gabriel omitted as first object; الإنساخ is commanding or informing him of abrogation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r8.anchor: فجعل الزمخشري المفعول المحذوف جبريل عليه السلام، والإنساخ هو الأمر بنسخها

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya also treats the hamza as causative but supplies the Prophet as omitted object and takes الإنساخ as permission to leave an abrogated āya.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r9.anchor: وجعل ابن عطية المفعول ضمير النبي عليه السلام، والإنساخ إباحة النسخ لنبيه

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya further derives the reading from copying a book without removing it, meaning write and send from the Preserved Tablet or delay and leave an āya from revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r10.anchor: وهو من نسخ الكتاب، وهو نقله من غير إزالة له

SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r11.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r11.claim: The Shaykh rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s alternative: the result must link to its conditional noun, but the first branch lacks that link because abrogated and delayed āyas differ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106/r11.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وذهل عن القاعدة وهي أنه لا بد من ضمير يعود من الجزاء على اسم الشرط

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r1.claim: من is partitive and modifies conditional ما through an omitted phrase; making it circumstantial is weaker. Singular آية stands for a plural.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r1.anchor: من " للتبعيض، فهي متعلقة بمحذوف لأنها صفة لاسم الشرط

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r2.claim: The genitive phrase specifies and clarifies the otherwise ambiguous conditional noun, as من الرجال narrows من to men.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r2.anchor: وهذا المجرور هو المخصص والمبين لاسم الشرط

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r3.claim: He compares this construction to ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة and وما بكم من نعمة فمن الله.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r3.anchor: وكذلك تخريج كل ما جاء من هذا التركيب

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ parses من آية as accusative specification for ما, meaning ‘what thing’; ‘which āya from an āya’ would be redundant.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r4.anchor: أنها في موضع نصب على التمييز، والمميز " ما "

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also makes من extra and آية circumstantial, meaning little or much; he cites its use as ‘sign’ in 7:73.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r5.anchor: والثاني: أنها زائدة وآية حال /، والمعنى: أي شيء ننسخ قليلا أو كثيرا

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r6.claim: Al-Samīn rejects this because a circumstantial accusative cannot be governed by من in the genitive.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r6.anchor: وهذا فاسد لأن الحال لا تجر ب " من "

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r7.claim: If ما is a source noun, من is extra and آية its object, completing four analyses of the phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#2/r7.anchor: " من " زائدة عل القول بجعل " ما " واقعة موقع المصدر

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r1.claim: أو divides the alternatives, and ننسها is jussive by coordination with the preceding conditional verb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r1.anchor: " أو " هنا للتقسيم، و " ننسها " مجزوم عطفا على فعل الشرط قبله

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r2.claim: Reading 1 of 13: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read ننسأها with open prefix, quiescent nūn, open sīn, and hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r2.anchor: بفتح حرف المضارعة وسكون النون وفتح السين مع الهمز

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r3.claim: Reading 2 removes hamza; Abū ʿUbayd al-Bakrī reports it from Saʿd, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya suspects a mistake.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r3.anchor: الثانية: كذلك إلا أنه بغير همز، ذكرها أبو عبيد البكري عن سعد بن أبي وقاص

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r4.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r4.claim: Reading 3: al-Ḥasan reads تنسها with open خطاب tāʾ, quiescent nūn, open sīn, and no hamza; also attributed to Ibn Abī Waqqāṣ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r4.anchor: الثالثة: " تنسها " بفتح التاء التي للخطاب، بعدها نون ساكنة

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r5.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r5.claim: Saʿd rejects attributing the initial-nūn, kasra-sīn form to Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib, saying Qurʾān was revealed neither to al-Musayyib nor his son; he cites verses about the Prophet’s forgetting.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r5.anchor: إن القرآن لم ينزل على المسيب ولا على ابن المسيب

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r6.claim: Reading 4 is the preceding خطاب form with hamza.

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r7.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r7.claim: Reading 5 is the preceding form with ḍamma on tāʾ, attributed to Abū Ḥaywa.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r7.anchor: الخامسة: كذلك إلا أنه بضم التاء وهي قراءة أبي حيوة

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r8.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r8.claim: Reading 6 is the preceding form without hamza, attributed to Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r8.anchor: السادسة: كذلك إلا أنه بغير همز وهي قراءة سعيد بن المسيب

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r9.speaker: باقي السبعة
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r9.claim: Reading 7 by the rest of the Seven is ننسها with ḍamma on prefix, quiescent nūn, kasra on sīn, and no hamza.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r9.anchor: السابعة: " ننسها " بضم حرف المضارعة وسكون النون وكسر السين من غير همز

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r10.claim: Reading 8 is the preceding form with hamza.

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r11.speaker: الضحاك وأبو رجاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r11.claim: Reading 9 has ḍamma on prefix, open second nūn, and doubled kasra sīn; al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū Rajāʾ read it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r11.anchor: التاسعة: ننسها بضم حرف المضارعة وفتح النون وكسر السين مشددة

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r12.claim: Reading 10 is ننسك with ḍamma on prefix, quiescent nūn, kasra on sīn, and خطاب kāf.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r12.anchor: العاشرة: " ننسك. بضم حرف المضارعة وسكون النون وكسر السين

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r13.speaker: الضحاك وأبو رجاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r13.claim: Reading 11 is the preceding خطاب form with open second nūn and doubled sīn; also transmitted from al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū Rajāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r13.anchor: الحادية عشرة: كذلك إلا أنه بفتح النون الثانية وتشديد السين مكسورة

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r14.speaker: حذيفة
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r14.claim: Reading 12 adds the feminine object pronoun after خطاب kāf: ننسكها; it is also in the muṣḥaf of freedman Sālim.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r14.anchor: الثانية عشرة: كذلك إلا أنه بزيادة ضمير الآية بعد الكاف: " ننسكها "

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r15.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r15.speaker: الأعمش
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r15.claim: Reading 13 is ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها نجىء بمثلها, also in ʿAbd Allāh’s muṣḥaf.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r15.anchor: الثالثة عشرة: " ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها نجىء بمثلها "

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r16.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r16.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r16.claim: Hamzated forms derive from نسء, ‘delay,’ also used in أنسأ الله في أجلك, credit sales, and postponing camels’ watering.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r16.anchor: فأما قراءة الهمز على اختلاف وجوهها فمعناها التأخير من قولهم: نسأ الله وأنسأ الله

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r17.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r17.speaker: عطاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r17.claim: ʿAṭāʾ interprets the hamzated reading as delaying an āya’s abrogation and revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r17.anchor: نؤخر نسخها ونزولها وهو قول عطاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r18.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r18.speaker: ابن زيد
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r18.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets it as erasing an āya in wording and ruling.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r18.anchor: الثاني: نمحها لفظا وحكما وهو قول ابن زيد

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r19.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r19.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r19.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says it means letting an āya stand without abrogation; al-Samīn rejects this because one would not bring better than what is retained.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#3/r19.anchor: الثالث: نمضها فلا ننسخها وهو قول أبي عبيد، وهو ضعيف لقوله: نأت بخير منها

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r1.claim: Unhamzated forms may derive from forgetting and mean not remembering or leaving; alternatively, they derive from نسء with hamza replaced by alif, uniting the readings.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r1.anchor: وأما قراءة غير الهمز على اختلاف وجوهها أيضا ففيها احتمالان: أظهرهما: أنها من النسيان

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r2.claim: For readers using simple ننساها, derivation from the triliteral verb is straightforward.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r2.anchor: ثم من قرأ من القراء: " ننساها " من الثلاثي فواضح

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r3.speaker: نافع وابن عامر والكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r3.claim: For Form IV readers including Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and the Kufans, the meaning is ‘make you forget it’ or ‘command its abandonment.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r3.anchor: وأما من قرأ منهم من أفعل، وهم نافع وابن عامر والكوفيون

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r4.claim: أنسيته الشيء may mean ‘I commanded him to leave it,’ while نسيته means ‘I left it’; a poem uses ناسيها and منسيها for the senses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r4.anchor: إن علي عقبة أقضيها لست بناسيها ولا منسيها

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r5.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects abandonment and forgetting because the Prophet did not forget Qurʾān; he cites the promise not to take away revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r5.anchor: هذه القراءة لا يتوجه فيها معنى الترك، لا يقال: أنسى بمعنى ترك

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r6.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r6.claim: Al-Fārisī and others defend ‘make you leave it’; they answer that 17:86 means God did not take away all revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r6.anchor: قال الفارسي وغيره: " ذلك متجه لأنه بمعنى نجعلك تتركها

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r7.claim: نأت is the conditional result; having both conditional and result verbs in the imperfect is most eloquent.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r7.anchor: قوله: " نأت " هو جواب الشرط، وجاء فعل الشرط والجزاء مضارعين

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r8.claim: خير is apparently comparative: a lighter replacement reduces burden, while a heavier one increases reward.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r8.anchor: الظاهر منهما: أنها على بابها من كونها للتفضيل

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r9.claim: On the comparative analysis, مثلها matches its predecessor in duty and reward.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r9.anchor: وقوله: " أو مثلها " أي في التكليف والثواب، وهذا واضح

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r10.claim: The alternative takes خير as a noun meaning good or blessing, not comparative; its full analysis continues in the next segment.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#4/r10.anchor: والثاني: أن " خيرا " هنا مصدر، وليس من التفضيل في شيء

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r1.claim: On the alternative, خير is a good or blessing, with من marking source and qualifying a good from the āya, as in the preceding verse.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r1.anchor: و " من " لابتداء الغاية، والجار والمجرور صفة لقوله " خير "

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r2.claim: Al-Samīn calls the alternative remote because مثلها does not naturally coordinate with بخير on that meaning; attachment to منها without repeating the preposition is Kufan-only.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r2.anchor: وهذا بعيد جدا لقوله بعد ذلك: " أو مثلها " فإنه لا يصح عطفه على " بخير "

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r3.claim: ما ننسخ shifts from third-person reference to first-person speech after والله يختص and والله ذو الفضل.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r3.anchor: وقوله " ما ننسخ " فيه التفات من غيبة إلى تكلم

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r4.claim: نسخ may mean removal without a succeeding replacement, as wind removes a trace, or transfer without removal, as copying a book.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r4.anchor: والنسخ لغة: الإزالة بغير بدل يعقبه، نسخت الريح الأثر

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r5.speaker: unspecified
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r5.claim: A further account divides removal into removal with replacement, like sun and shade, or without substitute, like wind and trace; it cites removing what Satan casts.
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r5.anchor: والنسخ: الإزالة، وهو في اللغة على ضربين

SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:106#5/r6.claim: النسيئة means postponement and can also mean carrying through or confirming; the poem uses نسأتها.

ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r2.speaker: قراء
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r2.claim: The text transmits three readings of the form: nunsihā, nansahā, and nunsāʾhā.
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r2.anchor: في (ننسها) غير وجه قد قرئ به: أو ننسها، وننسها، وننسؤها.

ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r3.claim: In Arabic, naskh means abolishing one thing and putting another in its place, as the sun removes shade and replaces it.
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r3.anchor: فأما النسخ في اللغة فإبطال شيء وإقامة آخر مقامه، العرب تقول نسخت الشمس الظل

ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r4.speaker: أهل اللغة
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r4.claim: Some lexicographers derive the phrase from forgetting, citing ‘You will recite, and you will not forget, except what God wills’; al-Zajjāj rejects this reading.

ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r5.claim: That derivation cannot mean God wills to remove revelation: 17:86 says He would not will to take away what He revealed to the Prophet.
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r5.anchor: لأن الله عز وجل: قد أنبأ النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في قوله (ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك)

ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r6.claim: The exception in ‘you will not forget except what God wills’ can mean leaving something aside by choice or ordinary human forgetting followed by later recollection, not stripping the Prophet of revealed wisdom.
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r6.anchor: أحدهما (فلا تنسى) أي لست تترك إلا ما شاء الله أن تترك، ويجوز أن يكون إلا ما شاء الله مما يلحق بالبشرية، ثم تذكر بعد

ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r7.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r7.claim: Another gloss takes it as ‘or leave it’; al-Zajjāj rejects أنسى for ‘leave’ and says it means God commands that the verse be left.
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r7.anchor: وقيل في (أو ننسها) قول آخر وهو خطأ أيضا، قالوا أو نتركها

ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r8.claim: Abrogation replaces a verse with another that cancels its ruling; leaving means believers stop a practice without a later abrogating verse, as with the test of emigrant women.
ZAJJAJ:v1p189/r8.anchor: أن النسخ يأتي في الكتاب في نسخ الآية بآية فتبطل الثانية العمل بالأولى. ومعنى الترك

ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r1.claim: The reading nunsāʾhā means ‘or defer it’; nasʾ in Arabic means delay, as in asking God to extend someone’s term.
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r1.anchor: ومن قرأ " أو ننسؤها " أراد نؤخرها. والنسء في اللغة التأخير

ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r2.claim: ‘Better than it’ means better for you; completing the fast replaced the earlier permission to abstain for those able to fast.
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r2.anchor: المعنى بخير منها لكم، (أو مثلها) فأما ما يؤتى فيه بخير من المنسوخ فتمام الصيام

ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r3.claim: ‘Or its like’ means a verse with equal reward; the replacement may be easier to follow and more readily accepted by people.
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r3.anchor: وأما قوله (أو مثلها) أي نأتي بآية ثوابها كثواب التي قبلها، والفائدة في ذلك

ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r4.claim: The change of qibla from Jerusalem to the Kaaba illustrates an equally rewarded act whose command at that time was more fitting and drew Arabs and others toward Islam.
ZAJJAJ:v1p190/r4.anchor: وعدل بها عن القصد لبيت المقدس، فهذا - وإن كان السجود إلى سائر النواحي متساويا

ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r1.claim: Asad reads the passage as establishing that the Qur’anic dispensation supersedes the earlier Biblical dispensation.
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r1.anchor: relating to the supersession of the Biblical dispensation by that of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r2.claim: In this context ayah means “message”; its use elsewhere for a Qur’anic verse led some theologians to an erroneous doctrine of internal Qur’anic abrogation, which Asad rejects.
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r2.anchor: by many Muslim theologians. The word ayah ("message") occurring in this, context is also used to denote a "verse;" of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r3.speaker: many Muslim theologians
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r3.claim: They take ayah to mean a Qur’anic verse and conclude that some verses were abrogated before revelation ended; Asad calls this assertion fanciful.
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r3.anchor: by many Muslim theologians. The word ayah ("message") occurring in this, context is also used to denote a "verse;" of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r4.claim: Asad likens the claim that Qur’anic verses were revised during revelation to imagining a human author editing manuscript proofs after the fact.
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r4.anchor: the image of a human author correcting, on second thought, the proofs of his manuscript - deleting one passage and replacing it with another

ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r5.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r5.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r5.claim: Asad says no reliable Tradition reports that the Prophet ever declared a Qur’anic verse abrogated, undermining the doctrine’s historical basis.
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r5.anchor: there does not exist a single reliable Tradition to the effect that the Prophet ever, declared a verse of the Qur'an to have been "abrogated"

ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r6.claim: Asad traces the doctrine to early commentators’ inability to reconcile Qur’anic passages, which they resolved by declaring one abrogated.
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r6.anchor: the inability of some of the early commentators to reconcile one Qur'anic passage with another

ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r7.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r7.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r7.claim: This arbitrary method explains the lack of agreement on which or how many verses were affected and whether abrogation removed a verse entirely or canceled only its ruling or statement.
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r7.anchor: why there is no unanimity whatsoever among the upholders of the "doctrine of abrogation" as to which, and how many, Qur'an verses have been affected by it

ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r8.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r8.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r8.claim: Read with 2:105, which says Jews and Christians reject revelation superseding the Bible, the verse concerns earlier divine messages, not parts of the Qur’an.
ASAD-NOTES:2:106#n87/r8.anchor: if read in this way, the abrogation relates to the earlier divine messages and not to any part of the Qur'an itself

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads ننسخ with first nūn ḍamma and sīn kasra; the other readers open both vowels.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن عامر وحده: (ما ننسخ) بضم النون الأولى وكسر السين

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r2.claim: In revelation, naskh means lifting or replacing a verse; lifting can affect recitation, legal force, or both.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r2.anchor: النسخ في التنزيل : رفع الآية وتبديلها

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r3.claim: Abū Bakr is reported to have said that Muslims once recited لا ترغبوا عن آبائكم إنه كفر, an example of wording and ruling both being lifted.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r3.anchor: كنحو ما روي عن أبي بكر الصديق أنه قال: كنا نقرأ: «لا ترغبوا عن آبائكم إنه كفر»

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r4.claim: Another form leaves the verse in the written text while removing its legal force, as with the rule about returning dowries when wives joined the disbelievers.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r4.anchor: فهذه ثابتة اللفظ في الخط مرتفعة الحكم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r5.claim: A ruling may be abrogated by Sunna or Qurʾān; Qurʾānic examples include the battle ratio reduced from one believer facing ten to one facing two, and the widow’s waiting period.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r5.anchor: وأما المنسوخ بقرآن مثله؛ فقوله في الأنفال: إن يكن منكم عشرون صابرون يغلبوا مائتين

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r6.speaker: عمر
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r6.claim: The wording of the stoning ruling is said to have been removed while the ruling remained; ʿUmar warned people not to abandon it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p180/r6.anchor: وما روي عن عمر من أنه قال: لا تهلكوا عن آية الرجم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r4.claim: For Ibn ʿĀmir’s ḍamma-nūn reading, al-Fārisī considers three analyses: an unattested lexical variant, a causative “make copy,” or “find it abrogated.”
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r4.anchor: فأما قراءة ابن عامر ما ننسخ من آية بضم النون، فالقول فيها: أنها لا تخلو من ثلاثة أوجه

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r5.claim: The lexical-variant analysis is rejected because no authority is known to have used or transmitted that form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r5.anchor: فلا يجوز أن يكون لغة على حد حل وأحل، وبدأ وأبدأ لأنا لم نعلم أحدا حكى ذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r6.claim: The causative analysis would make every revealed verse subject to replacement, although most verses are not abrogated; its implication conflicts with the verse’s intended meaning.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p184/r6.anchor: ولا تكون الهمزة لمعنى النقل، لأنك لو جعلته كذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p185/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p185/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p185/r1.claim: Al-Fārisī therefore takes Ibn ʿĀmir’s form to mean “we find it abrogated”; it agrees in meaning with the majority’s open-nūn reading despite different wording.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p185/r1.anchor: ننسخ : نجده منسوخا، وإنما نجده كذلك لنسخه إياه

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p185/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p185/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p185/r2.claim: The open-nūn reading is clearer and more explicit.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p185/r2.anchor: وقول من فتح النون فقرأ: ما ننسخ من آية أبين وأوضح

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read ننسأها with open nūn and hamza, meaning “we defer it”; the remaining readers use ḍamma nūn without hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ننسأها: بفتح النون الأولى مع الهمز

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r2.speaker: أبو علي
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r2.claim: The hamza reading is explained as postponing the verse; a critic’s claim that postponement makes no sense is answered with early recitation and Arabic usage.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r3.speaker: عمر وابن عباس وإبراهيم وعطاء وعبيد بن عمير
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r3.claim: The source supports the delay reading by citing reports that ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibrāhīm, ʿAṭāʾ, and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr recited it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r3.anchor: وقد قرأ بذلك من السلف فيما ذكر

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r4.speaker: مجاهد
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r4.claim: Mujāhid glosses the alternatives as erasing the verse or deferring it; deferral can preserve its written form while replacing its ruling.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r4.anchor: وروى ابن جريج عن مجاهد ما ننسخ من آية قال

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r5.speaker: ناس من أهل النظر
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r5.claim: One proposed deferral is to delay revelation altogether, so the verse is never sent down, known, practiced, or recited.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r5.anchor: أن يؤخر التنزيل فلا ينزل البتة، ولا يعلم ولا يعمل به، ولا يتلى

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r6.speaker: ناس من أهل النظر
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r6.claim: A second proposal is that a verse is revealed, recited, and practiced, then abrogated so its recitation is erased and it is no longer followed.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r6.anchor: أن ينزل القرآن فيعمل به ويتلى ثم يؤخر بعد ذلك بأن ينسخ فترفع تلاوته البتة

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r7.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق وأبي بن كعب
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r7.claim: Reports offered for erased recitation include Abū Bakr’s remembered wording and Ubayy’s claim that the Companions recited al-Aḥzāb as a longer sūra than al-Baqara.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p186/r7.anchor: مثل ما روى يونس عن الحسن أن أبا بكر الصديق قال

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r1.claim: In the fragmentary preceding discussion, he cites العيهل والكلكل and a poetic أضخما for الأضخم, calling the pronunciation doubly irregular: lengthening at pause and carrying pause treatment into connected speech.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r1.anchor: وفي هذا شذوذان؛ أحدهما: التثقيل في الوقف، والآخر: إجراء الوصل مجرى الوقف؛

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r2.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r2.claim: Ibn Abī Isḥāq reads المرء with ḍamma on mīm and hamza; another reads it with kasra on mīm, and a further dialect inflects mīm for case.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r2.anchor: وأما قراءة ابن أبي إسحاق: المرء بضم الميم والهمز فلغة فيه،

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r3.claim: The case vowel normally follows the hamza across rāʾ in امرؤ; when rāʾ is still, speakers shift the familiar inflectional alternation to the adjacent moving mīm, as in pausal بكر and صيم/قيم.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r3.anchor: فلما أن تحركت الميم وسكنت الراء لم يمكن الإتباع في الساكن فنقل الإتباع من الراء إلى الميم

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r6.speaker: أبو رجاء
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r6.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads ننسها with a doubled sīn; no further argument is given here.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p102/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة أبي رجاء5: "ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها"6 مشددة السين.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r1.claim: With ḍamma on nūn, the verb can mean that God causes an āya to be abrogated, as in the expression for causing someone to copy a book.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن ضم أن المعنى ما ننسخك يا محمد من آية كقولك أنسخت زيدا الكتاب

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r2.claim: The same ḍamma reading can mean making an āya subject to abrogation, just as a verb can mean making something a grave.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما ننسخ من آية أي نجعلها ذات نسخ كقوله تعالى ﴿ فأقبره ﴾

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r3.claim: With fatḥa on nūn, the verb is a transitive form taking one object.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r3.anchor: والحجة لمن فتح أنه جعله من الأفعال اللازمة لمفعول واحد

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r4.claim: Opening nūn and retaining hamza derives the reading from postponing or increasing; Arabic idiom uses the related form for extending a lifespan.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r4.anchor: فالحجة لمن فتح النون وهمز أنه جعله من التأخير أو من الزيادة ومنه قولهم نسأالله أجلك وأنسأفي أجلك

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r5.claim: Ḍamma on nūn without hamza means leaving an āya un-abrogated.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r5.anchor: والحجة لمن ضم وترك الهمز أنه أراد الترك يريد أو نتركها فلا ننسخها

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r6.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r6.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r6.claim: One reported explanation of bringing something better is that it requires less worship.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r7.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r7.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r7.claim: Another explanation is replacing a punishment verse with a verse of mercy.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r7.anchor: وقيل نبدل آية العذاب بآية رحمة فذلك خير

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r8.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r8.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r8.claim: A third explanation takes the replacement as stronger: divine warning and encouragement toward what God has prepared are better for people.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r8.anchor: وقيل بل بأشد منها لأنه تخويف من الله لعباده وترغيب فيما عنده فذلك خير

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r9.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r9.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r9.claim: Abrogation occurs in three forms: wording and ruling are removed, wording is removed while ruling remains, or ruling is removed while wording remains.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r9.anchor: والنسخ على وجوه نسخ اللفظ والحكم ونسخ اللفظ وابقاء الحكم ونسخ الحكم وابقاء اللفظ

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r10.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r10.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r10.claim: Likeness need only hold in one respect; total likeness would make the thing identical rather than its counterpart. Here both are Quran, but one conveys mercy and the other punishment.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p86/r10.anchor: المماثلة موافقة الشيء من وجه من الوجوه ولو ماثله من جميع وجوهه لكان هو ولم يكن له مثلا

NASHR:v1p257/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p257/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p257/r1.claim: The reader may stop after the istiʿādha and begin with the basmala or another passage, or connect them; both are sound. Al-Dānī’s wording appears to favor connection to the basmala.
NASHR:v1p257/r1.anchor: ويجوز الوقف على الاستعاذة والابتداء بما بعدها بسملة كان أو غيرها، ويجوز وصله بما بعدها، والوجهان صحيحان

NASHR:v1p257/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p257/r2.speaker: ابن الباذش
NASHR:v1p257/r2.claim: Ibn al-Bādhish says connecting istiʿādha and basmala in one breath is best, but pausing suits those who recite with tartīl; without a basmala he favors pausing, while allowing connection. The author endorses this as the best account.
NASHR:v1p257/r2.anchor: بالتسمية في نفس واحد، وهو أتم ولك أن تسكت عليها، ولا تصلها بالتسمية

NASHR:v1p257/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p257/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p257/r3.claim: When connected to the basmala and a following mīm, the mīm of الرحیم is assimilated for readers who use idghām; connecting also drops hamzat al-waṣl. A report says Abū ʿAmr concealed the mīm before the basmala’s bāʾ.
NASHR:v1p257/r3.anchor: نحو: (الرحيم ما ننسخ) - أدغم لمن مذهبه الإدغام

NASHR:v2p219/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p219/r5.speaker: ابن عامر
NASHR:v2p219/r5.claim: For ولكن الشياطين كفروا and related forms, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf lighten nūn and raise the following noun; the others geminate nūn and use accusative. Other listed verses have overlapping reader groups.
NASHR:v2p219/r5.anchor: فقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وخلف بتخفيف النون من ولكن ورفع الاسم بعدها

NASHR:v2p219/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p219/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p219/r6.claim: The passage points forward to an earlier-listed difference in gemination for أن ينزل عليكم.
NASHR:v2p219/r6.anchor: وتقدم اختلافهم في تشديد أن ينزل عليكم قريبا

NASHR:v2p220/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p220/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
NASHR:v2p220/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, except through al-Dājūnī from Hishām, reads ننسخ with initial nūn ḍamma and sīn kasra; the other readers open both vowels.
NASHR:v2p220/r1.anchor: النون والسين، وكذا رواه الداجوني عن أصحابه عن هشام

NASHR:v2p220/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p220/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p220/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read ننسأها with open nūn and sīn and a hamza before hāʾ; the rest read ننسها with nūn ḍamma, sīn kasra and no hamza.
NASHR:v2p220/r2.anchor: فقرأه ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بفتح النون والسين، وهمزة ساكنة بين السين والهاء

QIRAAT-ER:2:106:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:106:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:106:2#1/r1.claim: Form IV nunsikh means God causes abrogation or copying, introducing an intermediary, unlike Form I nansakh, we abrogate.
QIRAAT-ER:2:106:2#1/r1.anchor: Form IV introduces an intermediary: God causes someone else to perform the abrogation

QIRAAT-ER:2:106:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:106:6#1/r1.speaker: Ibn Kathīr
QIRAAT-ER:2:106:6#1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads from n-s-ʾ, we defer it, rather than n-s-y, we cause it to be forgotten; the variant implies postponement rather than cognitive erasure.
QIRAAT-ER:2:106:6#1/r1.anchor: Ibn Kathīr: root n-s-ʾ (to defer/delay) replaces n-s-y (to forget)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r1.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r1.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi say God caused His Prophet to forget what He willed and abrogated what He willed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r1.anchor: عن قتادة والكلبي في قوله ﴿ ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها ﴾ قال كان الله تعالى ذكره ينسي نبيه ما شاء وينسخ ما شاء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r2.claim: Qatada says a replacement can be better by easing a rule, granting a concession, or giving a command or prohibition.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r2.anchor: قال معمر وقال قتادة وأما قوله ﴿ نأت بخير منها أو مثلها ﴾ يقول آية فيها تخفيف فيها رخصة فيها أمر فيها نهي

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r3.claim: Saʿd rejects Ibn al-Musayyib’s reading “or cause it to be forgotten,” saying the Qurʾan was not revealed to Ibn al-Musayyib or his family; he cites 87:6 and 18:24.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p55/r3.anchor: فقلت إن سعيد بن المسيب يقرؤها أو ننسها قال فقال سعد إن القرآن لم ينزل على ابن المسيب ولا على آل المسيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r5.claim: Nasakha can mean removing something without a replacement, as the sun removes shade or wind erases a trace, or transferring something without removing it, as copying a book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r5.anchor: النسخ: إزالة الشيء بغير بدل يعقبه، نحو: نسخت الشمس الظل، ونسخت الريح الأثر. أو نقل الشيء من غير إزالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r6.claim: Nasiʾa means delay; the verb can also mean to advance or let something pass, as shown by the cited poem.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r6.anchor: النسيئة: التأخير، نسأ ينسأ، ويأتي نسأ: بمعنى أمضى الشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r7.claim: The poem uses نسأتها to witness the sense of making something pass or advance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p540/r7.anchor: قال الشاعر: لمؤن كألواح الأران نسأتها ... على لاحب كأنه ظهر برجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r5.speaker: اليهود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r5.claim: A reported occasion says Jews, jealous that Muslims faced the Kaʿba, objected that Muhammad changed his commands and contradicted himself; the verse was then revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r5.anchor: سبب نزولها، فيما ذكروا، أن اليهود لما حسدوا المسلمين في التوجه إلى الكعبة، وطعنوا في الإسلام قالوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r6.claim: Exegetes debate legal abrogation's definition, categories, agreement and disagreement, rational possibility, legal occurrence, and what can abrogate; Abū Ḥayyān leaves this to legal theory.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r6.anchor: وقد تكلم المفسرون هنا في حقيقة النسخ الشرعي وأقسامه، وما اتفق عليه منه، وما اختلف فيه، وفي جوازه عقلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r7.claim: He treats each discipline's principles as established from that discipline and avoids expanding tafsir with lengthy specialist debates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r7.anchor: وهكذا جرت عادتنا: أن كل قاعدة في علم من العلوم يرجع في تقريرها إلى ذلك العلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r8.claim: He criticizes al-Rāzī for lengthy material unrelated to tafsir and quotes a scholar's quip that the book contains everything except tafsir.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p546/r8.anchor: كما فعله أبو عبد الله محمد بن عمر الرازي، المعروف بابن خطيب الري، فإنه جمع في كتابه في التفسير أشياء كثيرة طويلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says he deliberately omits material outside tafsir and includes the methodological discussion to explain that choice, not because he overlooked other books.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r1.anchor: وإنما أمعنت الكلام في هذا الفصل لينتفع به من يقف عليه، ولئلا يعتقد أنا لم نطلع على ما أودعه الناس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r2.claim: The conditional ما is a fronted object of ننسخ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r2.anchor: وما من قوله: ما ننسخ، شرطية، وهي مفعول مقدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r3.claim: ننسخ shifts the discourse from third-person reference to first-person plural, following the preceding mention of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r3.anchor: وفي ننسخ التفات، إذ هو خروج من غائب إلى متكلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r4.claim: The majority read nansakh from nasakha, meaning removal; the reading covers removal of both wording and ruling, wording alone, or ruling alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ننسخ من نسخ، بمعنى أزال، فهو عام في إزالة اللفظ والحكم معا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r5.speaker: ابن عامر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r5.claim: A group and Ibn ʿĀmir read from the form inʾāsā/insākh rather than the majority's nasakha reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r5.anchor: وقرأت طائفة وابن عامر من السبعة: ما ننسخ من الإنساخ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r6.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī objects that this is not an Arabic usage because nasakha and ansakha are not synonymous; as a causative it would make every revealed verse written or abrogated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r6.anchor: وقد استشكل هذه القراءة أبو علي الفارسي فقال: ليست لغة، لأنه لا يقال نسخ وأنسخ بمعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r7.claim: Al-Fārisī therefore explains the form as finding a verse already abrogated, like saying one found a man praiseworthy or miserly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p547/r7.anchor: كما يقال: أحمدت الرجل إذا وجدته محمودا، وأبخلته إذا وجدته بخيلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r1.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r1.claim: Al-Fārisī says something is found abrogated only because it has been abrogated, so the readings agree in meaning despite their different wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r1.anchor: قال أبو علي: وليس نجده منسوخا إلا بأن ينسخه، فتتفق القراءات في المعنى، وإن اختلفا في اللفظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r2.claim: On al-Fārisī's account the hamza is not causative: the form means finding an item in the state named by its root, one of the meanings of afʿala.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r2.anchor: فجعل الهمزة في النسخ ليست للتعدية، وإنما أفعل لوجود الشيء بمعنى ما صيغ منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the hamza as causative: God commands Gabriel to make the verse abrogated by informing him of its abrogation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r3.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري الهزة فيه للتعدية قال: وإنساخها الأمر بنسخها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls al-Zamakhsharī's phrasing obscure, then explains that adding the causative hamza makes the one-object verb نسخ take two objects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r4.anchor: وهذا تثبيج في العبارة عن معنى كون الهمزة للتعدية. وإيضاحه أن نسخ يتعدى لواحد، فلما دخلت همزة النقل تعدى لاثنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya parses the reading as ما ننسخك: what God permits the Prophet to abrogate or leave by God's own abrogation; here the first omitted object is the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: التقدير ما ننسخك من آية، أي ما نبيح لك نسخه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya also derives the causative from copying a book: it means what God writes and sends from the Preserved Tablet, or defers and does not send.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r6.anchor: وخرج ابن عطية هذه القراءة على تخريج آخر وهو: أن تكون الهمزة فيه للتعدية أيضا، وهو من نسخ الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r7.claim: In that second parse, منها and بمثلها refer back to the verse deferred and not sent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r7.anchor: فتجيء الضميرات في منها وبمثلها عائدين على الضمير في ننسأها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says this parse violates the rule that a conditional's answer must link back to it: copying and deferring differ, leaving the first condition without a valid answer-link.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p548/r8.anchor: وذهل عن القاعدة النحوية، وهي أن اسم الشرط لا بد في جوابه من عائد عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r1.claim: من is partitive, while singular آية can stand for a plural; the phrase means any of the verses, as in Arabic expressions using a singular after من.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r1.anchor: هنا للتبعيض، وآية مفرد وقع موقع الجمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r2.claim: The genitive phrase specifies the otherwise general conditional object; some parse من آية as accusative specification, meaning what thing of an ayah is abrogated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r2.anchor: ويتضح بهذا المجرور ما كان معمولا لفعل الشرط، لأنه مخصص له، إذ في اسم الشرط عموم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r3.claim: He rejects estimating أي آية ننسخ, since it would combine أي آية with a second specification by من آية, an unacceptable duplication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r3.anchor: ولا يحسن أن يقدر أي آية ننسخ، لأنك لا تجمع بين آية وبين المميز بآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r4.claim: Some treat من as extra and آية as a circumstantial accusative, meaning any amount of abrogation; Abū Ḥayyān rejects it because a circumstantial cannot be introduced by من.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r4.anchor: وجوزوا أيضا أن تكون من زائدة، وآية حالا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r5.claim: Some make ما a verbal noun and آية its object, citing poetry for مصدرية ما; he rejects this because the conditional answer lacks a pronoun resuming it, and conditional clauses do not license extra من on an object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p549/r5.anchor: وجوزوا أيضا أن تكون ما مصدرا، وآية مفعولا به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r1.speaker: عمر، وابن عباس، والنخعي، وعطاء، ومجاهد، وعبيد بن عمير، وابن كثير، وأبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r1.claim: These readers read ننسأها with hamza, opening the initial nūn and sīn and making the hamza still.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r1.anchor: قرأ عمر، وابن عباس، والنخعي، وعطاء، ومجاهد، وعبيد بن عمير، ومن السبعة ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد البكري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r2.claim: Al-Bakri's book attributes the hamzated reading to Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, but Abū Ḥayyān and Ibn ʿAṭiyya regard that attribution as a mistake.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r2.anchor: وذكر أبو عبيد البكري في (كتاب اللآلئ) ذلك عن سعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص، والحسن، وابن يعمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reports that Saʿd, al-Ḥasan, and Ibn Yaʿmar read تنساها with open tāʾ, still nūn, and no hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r3.anchor: وقرأ سعد بن أبي وقاص تنساها بالتاء المفتوحة وسكون النون وفتح السين من غير همز، وهي قراءة الحسن وابن يعمر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r4.speaker: فرقة، وأبو حيوة، وسعيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r4.claim: A group reads the same form with hamza; Abū Ḥaywa uses a damma on tāʾ, while Saʿīd reads it without hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r4.anchor: وقرأت فرقة كذلك، إلا أنهم همزوا: وقرأ أبو حيوة كذلك، إلا أنه ضم التاء. وقرأ سعيد كذلك، إلا أنه بغير همز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r5.speaker: باقي السبعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r5.claim: The remaining Seven read ننسها with a damma on the first nūn and kasra on sīn, without hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r5.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة، ننسها، بضم النون وكسر السين من غير همز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r6.speaker: فرقة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r6.claim: Another group reads the form without hamza except that they place hamza after sīn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r6.anchor: وقرأت فرقة كذلك، إلا أنها همزت بعد السين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r7.speaker: الضحاك، وأبو رجاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Abū Rajāʾ read with damma on the first nūn, fatḥa on the second, doubled sīn, and no hamza.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r7.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك وأبو رجاء: بضم النون الأولى وفتح الثانية وتشديد السين وبلا همز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r8.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r8.claim: Ubayy reads ننسك, with the second nūn still, kasra on sīn, no hamza, and a second-person kāf instead of the third-person pronoun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبي: أو ننسك، بضم النون الأولى وسكون الثانية وكسر السين من غير همز، وبكاف للخطاب بدل ضمير الغيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r9.speaker: سالم مولى أبي حذيفة، وأبو حذيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r9.claim: Salim's codex has Ubayy's form; Abū Ḥudhayfa's reading combines the two pronouns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r9.anchor: وفي مصحف سالم مولى أبي حذيفة كذلك، إلا أنه جمع بين الضميرين، وهي قراءة أبي حذيفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r10.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r10.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها نجيء بمثلها; this wording is also fixed in ʿAbd Allāh's codex.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r10.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها نجيء بمثلها. وهكذا ثبت في مصحف عبد الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r11.claim: Excluding al-Aʿmash's reading, the word has eleven recorded readings, including the hamzated and unhamzated forms he enumerates.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r11.anchor: فتحصل في هذه اللفظة، دون قراءة الأعمش، إحدى عشرة قراءة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r12.speaker: ابن عباس، والزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r12.claim: They explain نسخ here as replacement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r12.anchor: وفسر النسخ هنا بالتبديل، قاله ابن عباس والزجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r13.speaker: عبد الله، وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r13.claim: They also explain abrogation as changing the ruling while leaving the written wording in place.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r13.anchor: أو تبديل الحكم مع ثبوت الخط، قاله عبد الله وابن عباس أيضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r14.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r14.claim: Al-Suddī explains نسخ as lifting or removing the verse.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r15.speaker: مجاهد، وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r15.claim: If read without hamza from the root meaning forget, the phrase means God causes the verse to be forgotten or forgets it, depending on the verb form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r15.anchor: فإن كان من النسيان ضد الذكر، فالمعنى: ننسكها إذا كان من أفعل، أو ننسها إذا كان من فعل، قاله مجاهد، وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r16.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r16.claim: If the unhamzated form means leave, it means leaving the verse's revelation unsent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r16.anchor: وإن كان من الترك، فالمعنى: أو نترك إنزالها، قاله الضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r17.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd says it means erasing the verse so that neither its wording remains recited nor its ruling remains binding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r17.anchor: أو نمحها، فلا نترك لها لفظا يتلى ولا حكما يلزم، قاله ابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r18.claim: Another usage is to order something abandoned: أنسيته means I ordered its abandonment, and نسيته means I left it; an anonymous poem illustrates the usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p550/r18.anchor: أو نأمر بتركها، يقال: أنسيته الشيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r1.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the unhamzated reading with the stated vowels cannot mean leave, since أنسي does not mean leave.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r1.anchor: وقال الزجاج: قراءة ننسها، بضم النون وسكون النون الثانية وكسر السين، لا يتوجه فيها معنى الترك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r2.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī and others say that reading can mean making the addressee leave the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r2.anchor: ذلك متجه، لأنه بمعنى نجعلك تتركها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r3.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects forgetfulness as the meaning because the Prophet did not forget Qurʾān; he cites 17:86 as evidence that God did not remove what He revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r3.anchor: إن هذا لم يكن للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows that the Prophet did forget a verse and answers that 17:86 means God did not remove all of the revelation; al-Ṭabarī traces al-Zajjāj's view to an earlier authority.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي: معناه لم نذهب بالجميع، وحكى الطبري قول الزجاج عن أقدم منه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's preferred distinction allows God to make the Prophet forget what He does not intend to preserve as Qurʾān; ordinary human lapses are barred before conveying and until companions have memorized, but possible afterward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r5.anchor: والصحيح في هذا أن نسيان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، لما أراد الله أن ينساه، ولم يرد أن يثبته قرآنا جائزا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r6.speaker: النبي، وأبي بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r6.claim: A report says the Prophet omitted a verse in prayer; when he asked why Ubayy did not remind him, Ubayy said he feared it had been removed, and the Prophet replied that he had forgotten it. No grading is given.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r6.anchor: ومنه الحديث، حين أسقط آية، فلما فرغ من الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r7.claim: With hamza, the word comes from delaying; Arab usage includes delaying camels' watering by a day or more.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r7.anchor: وأما من قرأ بالهمز فهو من التأخير، تقول العرب: نسأت الإبل عن الحوض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r8.speaker: عطاء، وابن أبي نجيح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r8.claim: They take the hamzated reading to mean delaying the verse's abrogation or its revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r8.anchor: فالمعنى: نؤخر نسخها أو نزولها، قاله عطاء وابن أبي نجيح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says the hamzated form means erasing both the verse's wording and its ruling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r9.anchor: أو نمحها لفظا وحكما، قاله ابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the hamzated form means carrying the verse forward without abrogating it; the author objects that this cannot fit the promise to bring something better.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551/r10.anchor: أو نمضها فلا ننسخها، قاله أبو عبيدة، وهذا يضعفه قوله: نأت بخير منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r1.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās rearranges the verse to mean replacing a ruling with one more beneficial, or an equivalent, then deferring another verse; Abū Ḥayyān rejects it as disrupting Qurʾānic order.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r1.anchor: وهذه الحكاية لا تصح عن ذلك الحبر ابن عباس، إذ هي محيلة لنظم القرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r2.claim: نأت is the conditional answer; having both the condition and answer in the imperfect is the best construction for conditional verbs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r2.anchor: نأت: هو جواب الشرط، واسم الشرط هنا جاء بعده الشرط والجزاء مضارعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r3.claim: خير is apparently comparative: a lighter replacement is better by relieving obligations, while a heavier one is better through increased reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r3.anchor: الظاهر أن خيرا هنا أفعل التفضيل، والخيرية ظاهرة، لأن المأتى به، إن كان أخف من المنسوخ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r4.claim: A replacement like the original is equal in obligation and reward; he illustrates it with changing the direction of prayer from Jerusalem to the Kaaba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r4.anchor: أو مساو لها في التكليف والثواب، وذلك كنسخ التوجه إلى بيت المقدس بالتوجه إلى الكعبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r5.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r5.claim: Some read خير as a kind of good, with من marking origin, like 2:105; the author says coordination with أو مثلها fails unless good means relief from obligation, yielding no replacement or an equivalent one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r5.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن خيرا هنا ليس بأفعل التفضيل، وإنما هو خير من الخيور، كخير في قوله: أن ينزل عليكم من خير من ربكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r6.claim: He considers coordination of مثلها with the pronoun in منها weak because the preposition is not repeated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r6.anchor: وأما عطف مثلها على الضمير المجرور في منها فيضعف لعدم إعادة الجار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the phrase is a plain question: some supply أم تريدون as its counterpart, while others take أم as disconnected and supply أم علمتم; both assume the Prophet is addressed for his community, whereas direct address to him requires an omitted counterpart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ظاهره الاستفهام المحض، فالمعادل هنا على قول جماعة: أم تريدون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r8.claim: He rejects the proposed counterpart: this is a confirmatory question, normally especially after negation, and the hearer is the addressee; examples include 95:8, 26:18, 93:6, and 94:1.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p551#2/r8.anchor: وما قالوه ليس بجيد، بل هذا استفهام معناه التقرير، فلا يحتاج إلى معادل ألبتة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p554/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p554/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p554/r6.claim: Repeating the name Allah in three clauses marks each as independent rather than grammatically dependent on the others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p554/r6.anchor: وتكرر اسم الله ظاهرا في هذه الجمل الثلاث، ولم يضمر للدلالة على استقلال كل جملة منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p554/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p554/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p554/r7.claim: The first two clauses are confirmatory and affirmative in sense; the final denial of any protector or helper fits because nothing can obstruct God's will over all things under His power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p554/r7.anchor: ولما كانت الجملتان الأوليان للتقرير، وهو إيجاب من حيث المعنى، ناسب أن تكون الجملة الثالثة نفيا للولي والناصر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p567/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p567/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p567/r1.claim: The verse ends by affirming God's power because it has just promised a change in circumstances, and such a promise suits mention of divine power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p567/r1.anchor: ثم اختتم الآية بذكر قدرة الله تعالى على كل شيء، لأن قبله وعدا بتغيير حال، فناسب ذلك ذكر القدرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r1.speaker: المشركون أو اليهود
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r1.claim: The occasion is the polytheists' or Jews' complaint that Muhammad orders something, then forbids it or says its opposite, so the Qur'an is his own inconsistent speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r1.anchor: نزلت لما قال المشركون أو اليهود : ألأ ترون إلى محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يأمر أصحابه بأمر ثم ينهاهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r2.claim: In Arabic, naskh is removing a form or its equivalent from one thing and establishing its like elsewhere, whether the things are attributes or entities; using the term for the whole process is metonymic.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r2.anchor: والنسخفي اللغة إزالة الصورة أو ما في حكمهاعن الشيء وإثبات مثل ذلك في غيره سواء كان في الإعراض أو في الأعيان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r3.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r3.claim: Al-Raghib favors treating the two uses of naskh as figurative extensions of one meaning rather than as homonyms; wind erasing a trace and copying a book illustrate them.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r3.anchor: ومن إستعماله في المجموع التناسخ وقد أستعمل لكل واحد منهما مجازا وهو أولى من الإشتراك ولذا رغب فيه الراغب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r4.speaker: بعض الأصوليين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r4.claim: Some legal theorists define abrogating a verse as declaring that the duty to recite it has ended, as in the reported stoning wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r4.anchor: ونسخ الآية على ما أرتضاه بعض الأصوليين بيان إنتهاء التعبد بقراءتها كآية ( الشيخ والشيخة إذا زنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r5.speaker: بعض الأصوليين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r5.claim: The same definition covers ending the ruling derived from a verse, exemplified by the widow's one-year provision and maintenance wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r5.anchor: أو الحكم المستفاد منها كآية ( والذين يتوفون منكم ويذرون أزواجا وصية لأزواجهم متاعا إل الحول غير إخراج

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r6.speaker: بعض الأصوليين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r6.claim: Abrogation may end both recitation and ruling, as in the report of ten known sucklings making marriage unlawful.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r6.anchor: أو بهما جميعا كآية 0 عشر رضعات معلومات يحرمن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r7.claim: This definition removes the perpetual force inferred from an unrestricted expression; another definition accordingly calls abrogation the removal of a legal ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r7.anchor: وفيه رفع التأييد المستفاد من إطلاقها ولذا عرفه بعضهم برفع الحكم الشرعي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r8.claim: The term taʿabbud excludes an endpoint specified in the ruling: that states when the ruling itself ends, rather than when the duty to comply ends.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r8.anchor: وخرج بقيد التعبد الغاية فإنها بيان لإنتهاء مدة نفس الحكملا للتعبد به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r9.claim: This definition concerns rulings, since reports themselves do not involve a duty of devotional compliance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r9.anchor: وأختص التعريف بالأحكام إذ لا تعبد في الأخبار أنفسها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r10.claim: To make a verse forgotten is to remove it from hearts so it is no longer retained in memory.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r10.anchor: وإنساؤها إذهابها عن القلوب بأن لا تبقى في الحفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r11.speaker: بعض الصحابة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r11.claim: A Companion once tried to recite something he had memorized, could not find it in his memory, and asked the Prophet, who said it had been erased from people's chests the previous night.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r11.anchor: فإن بعض الصحابة أراد قراءة بعض ما حفظه فلم يجده في صدره فسأل النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فقال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r12.speaker: أبو موسى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r12.claim: Muslim transmits Abu Musa's report that they forgot a sura resembling Bara'a in length and intensity but remembered its saying that Adam's son would seek a third valley of wealth and that only earth fills his mouth; no grading is given.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r12.anchor: وروى مسلم عنن أبي موسى سنا كنا نقرأ سورة نشبهها في الطول والشدة ببراءة فأنسيتها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r13.speaker: أبو موسى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r13.claim: Abu Musa also reports that they forgot a sura resembling one of the musabbihat but remembered its address to believers about saying what they do not do and answering for written testimony on Judgment Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r13.anchor: وكنا نقرأ بسورة نشبهها بإحدى المسبحات فأنسيتها غير أني حفظت منها ( يا أيها الدين آمنوا لم تقولون

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r14.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r14.claim: Hasan holds that the Prophet too could be made to forget, citing God's promise to make him recite without forgetting except what God wills.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r14.anchor: والذاهبون إلى الأول أستدلوا بقوله تعالى : ( سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله ) وهو مذهب الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r15.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r15.claim: Al-Zajjaj holds that this kind of forgetting does not happen to the Prophet, citing the promise that God would not remove what He revealed to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r15.anchor: وهذا قول الزجاج وليس بالقوي لجواز حمل الذي على ما لا يجوز عليه ذلك من أنواع الوحي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r16.speaker: أبو علي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r16.claim: Abu Ali interprets the promise as meaning that God would not remove all revelation; either interpretation remains compatible with the exception in the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r16.anchor: وقال أبو علي : المراد لم نذهب بالجميع وعلى التقديرين لا ينافي الإستثناء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r17.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r17.claim: One explanation distinguishes abrogation as removing a ruling regardless of whether its wording remains, and forgetting as removing wording regardless of whether its ruling remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r17.anchor: وفسر بعضهم النسخ بإزالة الحكم سواء ثبت اللفظ أو لاو الإنساءبإز الة اللفظ ثبت حمه أو لا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r18.speaker: بعض آخر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r18.claim: Another explanation defines abrogation as removing a ruling in favor of a replacement, and forgetting as removing it without a replacement.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r18.anchor: وفسر بعض آخر الأول بالإذهاب إلى بدل للحكم السابق والثاني بالإذهاب لا إلى بدل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r19.claim: Al-Alusi objects to both definitions as contrary to Arabic and technical usage; nisyān means removal from memory, and figurative meanings should not be preferred when the literal sense works. He doubts the supporting reports from early authorities.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r19.anchor: وأورد على كلا الوجهين أن تخصيص النسخ بهذا المعنى مخالف للغة والإصطلاح وأن النساء حقيقة في الإذهاب عن القلوب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r20.claim: ما is a conditional particle governing ننسخ and is also its object; it can do both in different grammatical capacities, with the jussive force supplied to the verb separately.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r20.anchor: و ( ما ) شرطية جازمة ل ( ننسخ ) منتصبة به على المفعولية ولا تنافي بين كونها عاملة ومعمولة لإختلاف الجهة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r21.claim: The conditional ما indicates that what follows is possible, since such particles ordinarily introduce matters open to occurrence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r21.anchor: وتدل على جواز وقوع ما بعدها إذ الأصل فيها أن تدخل على الأمور المحتملة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r22.claim: All religious communities agree that abrogation is possible and has occurred; Jews other than the ʿĪsawiyya disagree about its permissibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p351/r22.anchor: وأتفقت أهل الشرائع على جواز النسخ ووقعه وخالفت اليهود غير العيسوية في جوازه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r1.speaker: اليهود
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r1.claim: The Jews argue that abrogation is rationally impossible; Abu Muslim al-Isfahani accepts its rational possibility but says it never occurred.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r1.anchor: وقالوا : يمتنع عقلا وأبو مسلم الأصفهاني في وقوعه فقال : إنه وإن جاز عقلا لكنه لم يقع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r2.claim: من آية is an accusative specification (tamyiz) whose specified term is ما, meaning “whatever thing”; making من extra and آية circumstantial is untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r2.anchor: و ( من آية ) في موضع النصب على التمييز والمميز ( ما ) أي أي شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r3.claim: Treating ما as a conditional verbal noun and آية as its object is even less acceptable than the alternative parse.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r3.anchor: كإحتمال كون ( ما ) مصدرية شرطية و ( آية ) مفعولا به أي نسخ ( ننسخ آية ) بل هدا الإحتمال أدهى وأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r4.claim: The pronoun in ننسها refers back to آية, like a construction meaning “I have a dirham and half of it”; abrogating and forgetting are distinct, and “verse” is named as the common case although rulings beyond verses are included.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r4.anchor: والضمير المنصوب عائد إلى ( آية ) على حدعندي درهم ونصفهلأن المنسوخ غير المنسي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r5.speaker: طائفة وابن عامر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r5.claim: A group and Ibn Amir read ننسخ with the hamza of the ifʿāl form; Abu Ali explains it as finding something in the state of being abrogated, which in meaning agrees with the unhamzated reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r5.anchor: وقرأ طائفة وإبن عامر من السبعة ( ننسخ ) من باب الأفع الوالهمزة كما قال أبو علي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
