ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows the hamza to be causative: “whatever verse We cause you to abrogate,” with the Prophet as recipient of permission to leave it after God's abrogation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r6.anchor: وجوز إبن عطية كون الهمزة للتعدية فالفعل حينئذ متعد إلى مفعولين والتقدير ( ما ) ننسخك ( من آية )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r7.claim: Some take the causative reading to mean an order to abrogate, addressed either to the Prophet or to Gabriel.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r7.anchor: وجعل بعضهم الإنساخ عبارة عن الأمر بالنسخ والمأمور هو النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم أو جبرائيل عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r8.claim: The suggestion that naskh means writing from the Preserved Tablet, or delaying and withholding a revelation, fails because the following pronouns must have an antecedent in the conditional answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r8.anchor: وإحتمال أن يكون من نسخ الكتاب أي ما نكتب وننزل من اللوح المحفوظ أو ما نؤخر فيه ونترك فلا ننزله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r9.speaker: عمر وابن عباس والنخعي وأبو عمرو وابن كثير وكثير
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r9.claim: These readers recite ننسأها with open nūn and sīn and a quiescent hamza; another group has the same form with alif but no hamza. The root means to delay, and the reading can mean delaying in the Preserved Tablet or removing it from memory, matching ننسها.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352/r9.anchor: وقرأ عمر وإبن عباس والنخعي وأبو عمرو وإبن كثير وكثير ( ننسأها ) بفتح نون المضارعة والسين وسكون الهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.claim: Al-Alusi calls it subtler to understand ننسأها as delaying the later abrogating verse until the abrogated verse has remained in force; the verse coming later then refers to the abrogated one, and either timing serves the timely benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.anchor: ولعله ألطف : إن المعنى نؤخر إنزالها وهو في شأن الناسخة حيث أخر ذلك مدة بقاء المنسوخة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك وأبو الرجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak and Abu Rajaʾ read ننسها as an active causative form, with the first object omitted: God causes someone to forget it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك وأبو الرجاء ( ننسها ) على صيغة المعلوم للمتكلم مع الغير من التنسية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.speaker: الحسن وابن يعمر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Yuʿmar read تنسها with an open tāʾ, from the verb “to forget.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وإبن يعمرتنسهابفتح التاء من النسيان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وفرقة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.claim: This reading is also attributed to Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and a group, who pronounce it with hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.anchor: ونسيت إلى سعد بن أبي وقاص وفرقة كذلك إلا أنهم همزوا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.speaker: أبو حيوة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.claim: Abu Haywa reads the form with a ḍamma on the tāʾ, deriving it from the causative of forgetting.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.anchor: وأبو حيوة كذلك إلا أنه ضم التاء على أنه من الإنساء

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.speaker: معبد
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.claim: Maʿbad reads the same form without hamza.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.claim: Ubayy reads ننسك with a ḍamma on the first nūn, a kasra on the sīn, no hamza, and a second-person kāf; Salim's codex makes both objects explicit as ننسكها.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبين نسك بضم النون الأولى وكسر السين من غير همز وبكاف الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r8.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r8.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها تجيء بمثلها.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها تجيء بمثلها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r9.claim: The verse may connect to the preceding ban on saying راعنا: its earlier toleration resembles the complaint prompting the verse, then the phrase was forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r9.anchor: أن فيه ما هو من قبيل النسخ حيث أقر الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم مدة على قول ( راعنا )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r10.claim: Alternatively, after calling God the possessor of great bounty, the passage counters the claim that avoiding abrogation would be more generous because people find familiar practice easier.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r10.anchor: أو لأنه تعالى لما ذكر أنه ( ذو الفضل العظيم ) كاد ترفع الطغام رؤوسها وتقول : إن من الفضل عدم النسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r11.claim: A third link is that after affirming revelation and refuting its opponents, the verse explains abrogation as one form of revelation and rebuts its critics.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r11.anchor: أو لأنه تعالى لما أشار إلى حقية الوحي ورد كلام الكارهين له رأسا عقبه بما يبين سر النسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r12.claim: God brings something better for people, or something equal; the replacement may be a ruling or no ruling, and recited revelation or non-recited revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r12.anchor: أي بشيء هو خير للعباد منها ( أؤ مثلها ) حكما كان ذلك أو عدمه وحيا متلوا أو غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r13.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r13.claim: “Better” can mean better in benefit, reward, or both; “equal” applies specifically to reward, according to some scholars.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r13.anchor: والخيرية أعم من أن تكون في النفع فقط أو في الثواب فقط أو في كليهما والمثلية خاصة بالثواب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r14.claim: When the abrogated material carries a ruling, a replacement ruling necessarily serves a benefit absent from the former ruling; benefits change with time, while the replacement may be better, equal, or without reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r14.anchor: إذا كان ناسخا للحكم سواء كان ناسخا للتلاوة أو لا لابد أن يكون مشتملا على مصلحة خلا عنها الحكم السابق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r15.claim: If only recitation is abrogated, the ruling and its benefit remain unchanged, so the new material can only be better or equal in reward, not in benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r15.anchor: وإذا كان ناسخا للتلاوة فقط لا يتصور الخيرية في النفع لعدم تبدل الحكم السابق والمصلحة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r16.claim: The same benefit and reward analysis applies when a verse is made forgotten: if it carried a ruling, what follows can be better in benefit; if it did not, the replacement is better or equal in reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r16.anchor: وكذا الحال في الإنساء فإن المنسي إذا كان مشتملا على حكم يكون المأتي به خيرا في النفع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r17.claim: Equal benefit is not possible: changing a ruling changes the benefit, while leaving the ruling intact preserves the original benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p352#2/r17.anchor: أن المماثلة في النفع لا تتصور لأنه على تقدير تبدل الحكم تتبدل المصلحة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r1.claim: Al-Alusi's preferred position permits abrogation without a replacement ruling and permits the Qur'an to be abrogated by the Sunna.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r1.anchor: جواز النسخ بلا بدل وجواز نسخ الكتاب بالسنة وهو المذهب المنصورومن الناس

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r2.claim: Opponents forbid abrogation without a replacement, abrogation by a heavier substitute, and abrogation of Qur'an by Sunna, arguing from the verse's wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r2.anchor: ومن الناس من منع ذلك ومنع النسخ ببدل أثقل أيضا وأحتج بظاهر الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r3.claim: Al-Alusi replies that neither a replacement nor a lighter substitute is required: absence of a ruling, or a heavier ruling, can better serve people's interests and spiritual improvement as circumstances vary.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r3.anchor: فلأنا لا نسلم أن كون المأتي به خيرا أو مثلا لا يتصور إلا في بدل وأن الأثقل لا يكون خيرا من الأخف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r4.claim: Laws resemble medicines: what benefits one era or person may harm another, so a heavier ruling or no ruling can better organize life and reform the afterlife through God's wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r4.anchor: كالدواء الذي تعالج به الأدواء فإن النافع في عصر قد يضر في غيره والمزيل علة شخص قد يزيل علة سواه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r5.claim: The objection that the verse requires another verse mistakes the debate: the issue is whether a ruling needs a replacement, not whether the first verse's wording must be replaced.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r5.anchor: لما أن الخلاف في جواز النسخ بلا بدل ليس في إتيان اللفظ بدل الآية الأولى بل في الحكم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r6.claim: The verse does not require the thing brought to be the abrogator: it says abrogation entails bringing something better or equal, so the abrogator may be another matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r6.anchor: إذ يجوز أن يعرف النسخ بغير المأتي به فإن مضمون الآية ليس إلا أن نسخ الآية يستلزم الإتيان بما هو خير منها أو مثل لها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r7.claim: Accordingly, the Sunna may abrogate while another Qur'anic verse supplies what is better or equal; the Sunna itself is also from God, as revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r7.anchor: وأيضا السنة مماأتى به الله سبحانه لقوله تعالى : ( وما ينطق عن الهوى إن هو إلا وحي يوحى )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r8.claim: Better or equal refers to benefit and reward, not wording, so the Sunna can be better or equal in those respects.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r8.anchor: وليس المراد بالخيرية والمماثلة في الفظ حتى لا تكون السنة كذلك بل في النفع والثواب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r9.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r9.claim: The Muʿtazila use change through abrogation and differences in merit over time to argue that the Qur'an is created.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r9.anchor: وأحتجت المعتزلة بالآية على حدوث القرآن فإن التغير المستفاد من النسخ والتفاوت المستفاد من الخيرية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r10.claim: Al-Alusi replies that change and difference characterize the relations of eternal inner speech to acts, commands, and reported propositions, not the essence of divine speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r10.anchor: وأجيب بأن التغير والتفاوت من عوارض ما يتعلق به الكلام النفسي القديم وهي الأفعال في الأمر والنهي والنسب الخبرية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r11.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r11.claim: Al-Razi answers that the two properties describe verbal speech, whereas the eternal speech affirmed by the Ashʿarites is inner speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r11.anchor: وأجاب الإمام الرازي بأن الموصوف بهما الكلام اللفظي والقديم عندنا الكلام النفسي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r12.claim: Al-Alusi objects that al-Razi's answer conflicts with the Ashʿarite consensus that the ruling is eternal and that abrogation applies only to rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r12.anchor: وأعترض بأنه مخالف لما أتفقت عليه آراء الأشاعرة من أن الحكم قديم والنسخ لا يجري إلا في الأحكام

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r13.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r13.claim: Abu Amr reads ناتب with the hamza changed to an alif.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r14.claim: The opening question may be for affirmation or for rebuke.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r15.claim: The address is to the Prophet, implicitly including his Muslim community because he teaches them and is the source of their knowledge; the singular also intensifies the meaning concisely.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r15.anchor: والخطاب للرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وأريد بطريق الكناية هو وأمته المسلمون وإنما أفرده لأنه صلى الله

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r16.claim: Other proposed addressees are anyone who encounters the verse, or specifically those who deny abrogation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r16.anchor: وقيل : لكل واقف عليه على حد بشر المشائين وقيل لمنكري النسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r17.claim: Knowledge that God's power encompasses everything proves His ability to abrogate and bring what is better or equal, since these matters too are under His power.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r17.anchor: والمراد الإستشهاد بعلم المخاطب بما ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r18.claim: The verse switches from a pronoun to God's majestic proper name to inspire awe; the name gathers the divine attributes, including power, and makes the attribution stronger.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p353/r18.anchor: والإلتفات بوضع الأسم الجليل موضع الضمير لتربية المهابة ولأنه الأسم العلم الجامع لسائر الصفات ففي ضمنه صفة القدرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r1.claim: Polytheists accused Muhammad of inventing commands because he would replace one instruction with another; this verse explains the wisdom of abrogation and answers their charge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن المشركين قالوا: إن محمدا ما يأمر أصحابه بأمر ثم ينهاهم عنه ويأمرهم بخلاف ما يقوله إلا من تلقاء نفسه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r2.claim: Naskh can mean transfer or copying, as when writing is copied from one book to another; in that sense all the Quran is copied from the Preserved Tablet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما: بمعنى التحويل والنقل ومنه نسخ الكتاب وهو أن يحول من كتاب إلى كتاب فعلى هذا الوجه كل القرآن منسوخ لأنه نسخ من اللوح المحفوظ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r3.claim: Naskh can also mean removal or cancellation, as when the sun removes the shade; this is the sense in which some Quranic rulings abrogate others.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r3.anchor: والثاني: يكون بمعنى الرفع يقال: نسخت الشمس الظل أي ذهبت به وأبطلته. فعلى هذا يكون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas defines one kind of abrogation as retaining the written wording while replacing its ruling.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله تعالى {ما ننسخ من آية} ما نثبت خطها ونبدل حكمها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r5.claim: Other kinds remove recitation while leaving the ruling, as with the stoning verse, or remove both recitation and ruling.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r5.anchor: ومنها أن ترفع تلاوتها ويبقى حكمها مثل آية الرجم، ومنها أن ترفع تلاوته أصلا عن المصحف وعن القلوب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r6.speaker: أبو أمامة بن سهل بن حنيف
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r6.claim: Abu Umama reports that Companions could recall only the basmala of a surah; the Prophet told them its recitation and rulings had been removed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r6.anchor: كما روي عن أبي أمامة بن سهل بن حنيف: أن قوما من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم قاموا ليلة ليقرءوا سورة فلم يذكروا منها إلا بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r7.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r7.claim: One report says Surat al-Ahzab was once as long as al-Baqara, then most of its recitation and rulings were removed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: كانت سورة الأحزاب مثل سورة البقرة، فرفع أكثرها تلاوة وحكما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r8.claim: Abrogation may remove a ruling and install another, as with the qibla, inheritance, the waiting period, and the battle ratio.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r8.anchor: ثم من نسخ الحكم ما يرفع ويقام غيره مقامه، كما أن القبلة نسخت من بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة، والوصية للأقارب نسخت بالميراث

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r9.claim: Abrogation may also remove a ruling without installing a replacement, as in the examination of women.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r9.anchor: ومنها ما يرفع ولا يقام غيره مقامه، كامتحان النساء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r10.claim: Abrogation applies to commands and prohibitions, not to reports.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p133#2/r10.anchor: والنسخ إنما يعترض على الأوامر والنواهي دون الأخبار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r1.speaker: قراءة العامة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r1.claim: The general reading has fatḥa on the n and kasra on the s in nansakh, meaning to remove or abrogate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة بفتح النون وكسر السين من النسخ، أي: نرفعها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r2.speaker: ابن عامر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r2.claim: Ibn Amir reads with ḍamma on the n as insakh; it can mean make it abrogated or make it a copy.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بضم النون وكسر السين من الإنساخ وله وجهان: أحدهما: أن نجعله كالمنسوخ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r3.claim: The second explanation of Ibn Amir's form is to make it a copy for another; nasakhtu al-kitab means I copied the book, and ansakhtuhu means I made it a copy.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r4.claim: Nunsiha can mean that God makes the verse forgotten in the Prophet's heart.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains it as leaving the verse without abrogating it, with 9:67 using forgetting in the sense of leaving.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، نتركها لا ننسخها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r6.claim: Another explanation is that God commands the verse to be left; on this account abrogation removes a ruling and replaces it, while making it forgotten does not.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r6.anchor: وقيل {ننسها} أي: نأمر بتركها، يقال: أنسيت الشيء إذا أمرت بتركه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r7.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read nansa'ha with hamza, meaning to defer the verse rather than replace it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو أو ننسأها بفتح النون الأول والسين مهموزا أي نؤخرها فلا نبدلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r8.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وعطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Ata say an abrogated verse is revealed Quran, while a deferred verse remains in the Preserved Tablet and is not sent down.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p134/r8.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب وعطاء: أما ما نسخ من آية فهو ما قد نزل من القرآن جعلاه من النسخة أو ننسأها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r1.claim: A replacement is better in benefit, ease, and reward for people, not because one verse is superior to another; all God's speech is good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r1.anchor: أي بما هو أنفع لكم وأسهل عليكم وأكثر لأجركم، لا أن آية خير من آية، لأن كلام الله واحد وكله خير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r2.claim: An equal replacement matches in benefit and reward; an easier ruling is easier to practice, while a harder one brings greater reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r2.anchor: في المنفعة والثواب فكل ما نسخ إلى الأيسر فهو أسهل في العمل وما نسخ إلى الأشق فهو في الثواب أكثر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r3.claim: The question is grammatically interrogative but functions as an affirmation: the addressee knows God can abrogate and change rulings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p135/r3.anchor: لفظه استفهام، ومعناه تقرير، أي: إنك تعلم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r1.speaker: الأعرج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r1.claim: Al-Aʿraj reports reading to Abū Hurayra, who read to Ubayy ibn Kaʿb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r1.anchor: وقال الأعرج قرأت على أبي هريرة، وقرأ أبو هريرة على أبي بن كعب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr's reading chain runs through Mujāhid, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb to the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r2.anchor: وأما عبد الله بن كثير فإنه قرأ على مجاهد بن جبر وقرأ مجاهد على ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr read to Mujāhid and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who read through Ibn ʿAbbās and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb to the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r3.anchor: وأما أبو عمرو فإنه قرأ على مجاهد وسعيد بن جبير، وهما قرآ على ابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r4.speaker: ابن عامر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r4.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir read to al-Mughīra ibn Shihāb, who read to ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r4.anchor: وأما عبد الله بن عامر فإنه قرأ على المغيرة بن شهاب المخزومي، وقرأ المغيرة على عثمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r5.speaker: عاصم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r5.claim: ʿĀṣim read to Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and also to Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, whose reading went back to Ibn Masʿūd.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r5.anchor: وأما عاصم فإنه قرأ على أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي وقرأ أبو عبد الرحمن على علي بن أبي طالب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r6.speaker: حمزة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r6.claim: Ḥamza read to ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā, al-Aʿmash, and Ḥumrān; their chains ran through early authorities among ʿAlī's and Ibn Masʿūd's companions, ʿUthmān, and ʿAlī.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r6.anchor: وأما حمزة فإنه قرأ على عبد الرحمن بن أبي ليلى، وسليمان الأعمش، وحمران بن أعين وغيرهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r7.speaker: الكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r7.anchor: وأما الكسائي فإنه قرأ على حمزة، وأما يعقوب فإنه قرأ على أبي المنذر سلام بن سليمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r8.speaker: يعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r8.claim: Yaʿqūb read to Abū al-Mundhir Salām ibn Sulaymān, who read to ʿĀṣim.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r8.anchor: وأما يعقوب فإنه قرأ على أبي المنذر سلام بن سليمان الخراساني، وقرأ سلام على عاصم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r9.claim: The listed readings are permissible because of agreement upon their acceptability.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r9.anchor: فذكرت قراءات هؤلاء للاتفاق على جواز القراءة بها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r10.claim: The Qur'an needs the Sunnah to clarify it, and religious law rests on both; the author relies on sound hadith collections and omits objectionable reports.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p38/r10.anchor: فإن الكتاب يطلب بيانه من السنة، وعليهما مدار الشرع وأمور الدين - فهي من الكتب المسموعة للحفاظ

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r1.claim: The verse was revealed after polytheists or Jews said Muhammad orders his companions to do something, then forbids it and orders its opposite.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r1.anchor: نزلت لما قال المشركون أو اليهود: ألا ترون إلى محمد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r2.claim: In language, abrogation is removing a form from one thing and establishing it elsewhere, as a shadow replaces the sun or as copying transfers text; usage then covers either removal, as wind erasing traces, or copying a book.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r2.anchor: والنسخ في اللغة: إزالة الصورة عن الشيء وإثباتها في غيره

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r3.claim: Abrogating a verse means ending the ritual obligation of its recitation, its ruling, or both.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r3.anchor: ونسخ الآية بيان انتهاء التعبد بقراءتها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r4.claim: Causing a verse to be forgotten means removing it from people’s memories.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r4.anchor: أو بهما جميعا. وإنساؤها إذهابها عن القلوب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r5.claim: ما is a conditional particle that makes ننسخ jussive and is itself its object.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r5.anchor: وما شرطية جازمة لننسخ منتصبة به على المفعولية

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ما ننسخ from أنسخ: ‘We command you or Gabriel to abrogate it,’ or ‘We find it abrogated.’
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ما ننسخ من أنسخ

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r7.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read ننسأها, meaning ‘We defer it,’ from النسء.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r7.anchor: وابن كثير وأبو عمرو «ننسأها» أي نؤخرها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r8.claim: Other readings mean ‘We cause someone to forget it,’ ‘We cause you to forget it,’ passive ‘you are made to forget it,’ or ‘We cause you to forget it’ with two implied objects.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r9.claim: A replacement is better for servants in benefit or reward, or equal in reward.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r9.anchor: أي بما هو خير للعباد في النفع والثواب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r10.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the hamza as an alif.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو بقلب الهمزة ألفا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r11.claim: God’s power encompasses abrogating a verse and bringing a replacement equal to or better than the abrogated one.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r11.anchor: فيقدر على النسخ والإتيان بمثل المنسوخ

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r12.claim: The verse establishes the permissibility of abrogation and delaying revelation: rulings and verses serve people’s welfare and moral completion, which vary with times and persons, as livelihoods do.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r12.anchor: والآية دلت على جواز النسخ وتأخير الإنزال إذ الأصل اختصاص أن وما يتضمنها بالأمور المحتملة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r13.claim: Some use the verse to prohibit abrogation without a substitute, with a heavier substitute, or of the Qur’an by Sunna, since Sunna is not the replacement; al-Bayḍāwī calls all these arguments weak.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r13.anchor: واحتج بها من منع النسخ بلا بدل، أو ببدل أثقل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r14.claim: A missing ruling or a heavier one can be more beneficial; an abrogation can be known by something other than scripture, and Sunna too is brought by God. ‘Better or equal’ concerns benefit or reward, not wording.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r14.anchor: إذ قد يكون عدم الحكم، أو الأثقل أصلح

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r15.speaker: المعتزلة
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r15.claim: The Muʿtazilites argue that the Qur’an is originated because change and variation are among its properties.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r15.anchor: والمعتزلة على حدوث القرآن فإن التغير والتفاوت من لوازمه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r16.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r16.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī answers that change and variation affect things related to the eternal divine essence’s meaning, not that essential meaning itself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:106/r16.anchor: وأجيب: بأنهما من عوارض الأمور المتعلقة بالمعنى القائم بالذات القديم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r1.claim: Biqāʿī treats God’s prohibition of “raʿinā” after previously allowing it as an instance of abrogation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r1.anchor: ولما حرم سبحانه قوله { راعنا } بعد حله وكان ذلك من باب النسخ

BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r2.claim: Abrogation transfers a benefit, such as property, religion, power, or knowledge, from one people to another after God’s favor selects them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r2.anchor: بعد التخصيص الذي من مقتضاه نقل ما يكون من المنافع من ملك أو دين أو قوة أو علم من ناس إلى ناس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r3.speaker: اليهود
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r3.claim: The Jews claim their religion cannot be abrogated, arguing that abrogation would imply badāʾ, or God’s learning something only after it appears.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r3.anchor: وكان اليهود يرون أن دينهم لا ينسخ , فكان النسخ لذلك من مطاعنهم في هذا الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r4.claim: Biqāʿī answers that the Torah itself contains abrogation: after Israel refused to fight the giants and enter Jerusalem, God forbade their entry and fighting.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r4.anchor: فإن فيه أنه تعالى أمرهم بالدخول إلى بيت المقدس بعد مقاتلة الجبارين , فلما أبوا حرم عليهم دخولها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r5.claim: The Prophet says the Jews were commanded to observe Friday but disputed about it and chose Saturday, after which the Sabbath was imposed strictly; the Qur’an also states this.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r5.anchor: وأمرهم بالجمعة فاختلفوا فيه , كما قاله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r6.claim: Another Torah example is that all meats and fats were initially permitted, then fats were forbidden to Israel after they worshipped the calf.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r6.anchor: واختاروا السبت , ففرض عليهم وشدد عليهم فيه وأحل لهم جميع اللحوم والشحوم , لما اتخذوا العجل حرم عليهم الشحوم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r7.claim: Biqāʿī calls the greater unauthorized alteration a false form of abrogation: religious scholars distort scripture and forbid or permit whatever rulings they wish.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p212/r7.anchor: وأعظم من ذلك تعاطيهم من النسخ ما لم يأذن به الله في تحريفهم الكلم عن مواضعه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r2.claim: The verse answers the People of the Book, whose envy led them to alter scripture, replace stoning with humiliating punishment, follow Satanic material, and reject parts of their book.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r2.anchor: وكما فعلوا في إبدال الرجم في الزنا بالتحميم والجلد ؛ وفي اتباع ما تتلو الشياطين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines naskh as moving a trace or book from its place by a successor that removes it, or by a substitute that makes its absence unnecessary.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r3.anchor: نقل باد من أثر أو كتاب ونحوه من محله بمعاقب يذهبه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r4.claim: The verse is joined without a conjunction because it is tightly connected to what precedes it: God grants this community favor and mercy by changing rulings with circumstances.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r4.anchor: وساقها بغير عطف لشدة التباسها بما قبلها لاختصاصنا لأجل التمشية على حسب المصالح بالفضل والرحمة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r5.claim: One reading is that the Qurʾān abrogates all earlier religious laws, honoring Muslims with an independent scripture and easing former burdens.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r5.anchor: إن كان المراد نسخ جميع الشرائع الماضية بكتابنا فلما فيه من التشريف بالانفراد بالذكر وعدم التبعية والتخفيف للأحمال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r6.claim: Alternatively, the verse concerns abrogation within the Muslim law, as changing worldly and afterlife interests and causes require.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r6.anchor: وإن كان المراد نسخ ما شرع لنا فللنظر في المصالح الدنيوية والأخروية بحسب ما حدث من الأسباب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r7.claim: An āya may be abrogated by removing its ruling or its recitation after revelation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r7.anchor: أي فنرفع حكمها , أو تلاوتها بعد إنزالها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r8.claim: On Ibn ʿĀmir’s reading, the phrase can mean that God commands the abrogating act; the āya may belong to an earlier law, such as the former qibla, or not.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r8.anchor: أو نأمر بذلك على أنها من النسخ على قراءة ابن عامر , سواء كانت في شرع من قبل كاستقبال بيت المقدس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r9.claim: The form suggests that earlier communities sometimes lost a ruling without an equal or better substitute; Muslims should welcome replacement with joy or gratitude for what is better.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r9.anchor: وفي صيغة نفعل إشعار بأن من تقدم ربما نسخ عنهم ما لم يعوضوا به مثلا ولا خيرا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r10.claim: The alternative nunsihā, from ansā and read by readers other than Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr, means that God commands leaving the āya unrevealed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r10.anchor: من أنسى في قراءة غير ابن كثير وأبي عمرو , أي نأمر بترك إنزالها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r11.claim: Another parsing takes immediate abrogation as removal of a ruling or wording, while postponement delays repeal for a time, as with the qibla, before a better or equal replacement comes.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p213/r11.anchor: بأن نؤخر نسخها أو نتركه - على قراءة { ننسها } زمنا ثم ننسخها كالقبلة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r1.claim: Biqāʿī endorses al-Ḥarālī’s distinction: naskh succeeds and ends an earlier ruling, while nasʾ delays it and can let it return.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r1.anchor: وقال الحرالي : وهو الحق إن شاء الله تعالى . والنسء تأخير عن وقت إلى وقت

BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r2.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says this subtle distinction escaped most scholars, except the imams from the Prophet’s family, because succession and postponement are easily confused.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r2.anchor: لم يكد يتضح معناه لأكثر العلماء إلا للأئمة من آل محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لخفاء الفرقان بين ما شأنه المعاقبة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r3.claim: The Prophet temporarily forbade eating sacrificial meat after three days because visitors had arrived from the desert; believers mistook the delay for abrogation until he explained its cause.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r3.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى فسره فقال : ( إنما نهيتكم من أجل الدافة )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r4.claim: A ruling withheld for a cause and restored when that cause disappears is nasʾ; fighting when strong and making truce when weak are examples.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r4.anchor: ومنه المقاتلة للعدو عند وجدان المنة والقوة والمهادنة عند الضعف عن المقاومة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r5.claim: Al-Ḥarālī calls this verse one of the Qurʾān’s comprehensive passages and compares its alternating and recurring rulings to the succession and cycles of seasons.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r5.anchor: فبحق أن هذه الآية من جوامع آي الفرقان , فهذا حكم النسء والإنساء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r6.claim: Biqāʿī summarizes nasʾ as delaying a permission or prohibition until another time, following Arab usage, and directs readers to the discussion of 9:37.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p214/r6.anchor: وحاصله تأخير الحل كما ذكر أو الحرمة كما في المتعة ونحو ذلك إلى وقت آخر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r1.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r1.claim: Al-Ḥarālī distinguishes divinely caused forgetting from postponement: God may make a prophet forget what is not normally subject to delay, then reveal its instruction as Sunna.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r1.anchor: وأما النسيان والتنسية فمعناه أخفى من النسيء وهو ما يظهره الله من البيانات على سبيل إدخال النسيان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r2.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that he forgets in order to establish a Sunna.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r2.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن تنسيته كما ورد من قوله : إني لأنسى لأسن

BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r3.claim: The Prophet instructs people to say that they were made to forget, rather than saying simply that they forgot.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r3.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام في إفصاح القول فيه : ( بئسما لأحدكم أن يقول : نسيت , بل هو نسي )

BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r4.claim: Al-Ḥarālī cites the Prophet’s standing after two rakʿas and ending prayer after two as divinely disclosed Sunnas arising through forgetfulness; such prayer is no less than prayer without that lapse.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r4.anchor: ومنه قيامه من اثنتين وسلامه من اثنتين حتى أظهر الله سنة ذلك لأمته

BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r5.claim: The Prophet’s sleep through a prayer occasioned a second way to determine its time: by remembering it, alongside its ordinary time marked by the sun.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r5.anchor: منامه عن الصلاة حتى أظهر الله توقيت الصلاة بالذكر كما كان قد أظهرها بالوقت الزماني

BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r6.claim: A prayer performed when remembered counts as performance by that measure, while it counts as make-up because its ordinary solar time has passed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r6.anchor: ولصحة وقوعها للوقتين كانت الموقتة بالذكر أداء بحسبه , قضاء بحسب فوت الوقت الزماني

BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r7.claim: The community benefits from repeal, postponement, and divinely caused forgetting; the later instruction is better in its effect, and the process serves the community through its changing conditions.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r7.anchor: وفي كل ذلك إنباء بأن ما وقع من الأمر بعد هذا النسيان خير من موقع ذلك الأمر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r8.claim: God’s ability to provide the promised replacement proves his complete power, which entails knowledge; unlike human rulers, he need not fear subjects’ reaction to changing a command.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r8.anchor: والقدرة الشاملة التامة مستلزمة للعلم أي وليس هو كغيره من الملوك إذا أمر بشيء خاف غائلة أتباعه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r9.claim: Biqāʿī frames rejection of divine abrogation as a major error of the People of the Book, despite the burdens removed by the new scripture and their own alteration of earlier law.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p215/r9.anchor: ولا سيما ما فيها من الآصار والأغلال أشار سبحانه إلى أن من أعظم ضلالهم وغيهم ومحالهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r1.claim: The People of the Book object that God cannot abrogate, although they themselves permit scriptural distortion; this inconsistency leads them to reject any messenger whose teaching they dislike.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r1.anchor: مما هو موجود في كتابهم كما أمر آنفا , ومما سوغوه لأنفسهم بالتحريف والتبديل , ولزم من ذلك تكذيب كل رسول

BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r2.claim: Their objection says an omniscient God would not command something and later forbid it, since he would already know whether it was beneficial or harmful.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r2.anchor: وأنه لو كان من عند الله لما تغير لأنه عالم بالعواقب , ولا يخلو إما أن يعلم أن الأمر بذلك الشيء مصلحة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r3.claim: Biqāʿī answers that God creates circumstances that make a ruling beneficial at one time and harmful at another, according to wisdom and purposes governing the world’s finite course.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r3.anchor: فيخلق بقدرته من الأسباب ما يصير الشيء في وقت مصلحة وفي وقت آخر مفسدة لحكم ومصالح دبرها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r4.claim: The cited scripture says that God is not questioned about what he does, supporting his freedom to legislate as he wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r4.anchor: مما هو موجود في كتابهم كما أمر آنفا , ومما سوغوه لأنفسهم بالتحريف والتبديل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r10.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sees this address as a comprehensive frame for the later changes in detailed rulings and conditions, like the earlier address introducing parables at the sūra’s opening.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p216/r10.anchor: وهو في الحقيقة خطاب جامع لتفصيل ما يرد من النسخ في تفاصيل الأحكام والأحوال

DURR-FULL:v1p254/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says revelation used to come to the Prophet at night and be forgotten by day, so this verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان مما ينزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي بالليل وينساه بالنهار فأنزل الله

DURR-FULL:v1p254/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r4.claim: Ibn Umar reports that two Anṣār who learned a sūra from the Prophet could not recite any of it one night; he told them it had been abrogated or forgotten and to leave it aside.
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قرأ رجلان من الأنصار سورة أقرأها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وكانا يقرآن بها فقاما يقرآن ذات ليلة

DURR-FULL:v1p254/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r5.speaker: الزهري
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r5.claim: Al-Zuhri read the form with a damma on the nūn and a light sīn, indicating the passive “be forgotten.”
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r5.anchor: فكان الزهري يقرؤها {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} بضم النون خفيفة

DURR-FULL:v1p254/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r6.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r6.claim: Umar says Ubayy was the best reciter and Ali the best judge, but they set aside some of Ubayy's recitation because he retained everything heard from the Prophet, citing this verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال عمر: أقرؤنا أبي وأقضانا علي وإنا لندع شيئا من قراءة أبي

DURR-FULL:v1p254/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r7.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r7.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas read the form “nun-sā-hā,” rejected Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib's “nun-sihā,” and cited 87:6 in support.
DURR-FULL:v1p254/r7.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص أنه قرأ (ما ننسخ من آية أو ننساها) فقيل له: إن سعيد بن المسيب يقرأ {ننسها}

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as beginning or leaving a verse without replacing it.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله (ما ننسخ من آية أو ننساها) يقول: ما نبدا من آية أو نتركها لا نبدلها

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says what replaces a verse is better for people in benefit and more accommodating to them.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله (ما ننسخ من آية أو ننساها) يقول: ما نبدا من آية أو نتركها لا نبدلها {نأت بخير منها أو مثلها} يقول: خير لكم في المنفعة وأرفق بكم

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r3.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r3.claim: Umar explains nun'siha as delaying a verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: خطبنا عمر فقال: يقول الله تعالى (ماننسخ من آية أو ننساها) أي نؤخرها

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r4.claim: Mujahid is reported to have read the phrase as ننساها.

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r5.claim: Mujahid reports Ubayy's reading as ننسك.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال في قراءة أبي ((ماننسخ من آية أو ننسك))

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r6.speaker: مجاهد عن أصحاب ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r6.claim: Mujahid reports Ibn Masud's associates explaining abrogation as retaining a verse's written form while changing its ruling, and explaining nun'siha as postponing it with God.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد عن أصحاب ابن مسعود في قوله {ما ننسخ من آية} قال: نثبت خطها ونبدل حكمها (أو ننساها) قال: نؤخرها عندنا

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r7.speaker: عبيد بن عمير الليثي
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r7.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr explains it as leaving a verse and raising it from people's possession.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r7.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير الليثي في قوله {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} يقول: أو نتركها نرفعها من عندهم

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Masud's reading as ننسك من آية أو ننسخها.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: في قراءة ابن مسعود ((ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها))

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r9.claim: Qatada says God could abrogate a verse after the Prophet recited it, raise it and cause him to forget it, and bring a replacement with easing, concession, command, or prohibition.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r9.anchor: عن قتادة قال: كانت الآية تنسخ الآية وكان نبي الله يقرأ الآية والسورة وما شاء الله من السورة ثم ترفع فينسيها الله نبيه

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas connects the verse with God replacing one verse by another and erasing and confirming what He wills.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله (ما ننسخ من آية

DURR-FULL:v1p255/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r11.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r11.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God revealed matters from the Quran and later raised them.
DURR-FULL:v1p255/r11.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال: يقولون (ماننسخ من آية أو ننساها) كان الله أنزل أمورا من القرآن ثم رفعها

DURR-FULL:v1p256/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet was taught Quran and then made to forget some of it; some abrogated Quran remained recited.
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {أو ننسها} قال: إن نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرىء قرآنا ثم أنسيه فلم يكن شيئا

DURR-FULL:v1p256/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة بن سهل بن حنيف
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r2.claim: Men who knew a sura found themselves unable to recite it at night; the Prophet said it had been abrogated the previous night.
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة بن سهل بن حنيف إن رجلا كانت معه سورة فقام من الليل فقام بها فلم يقدر عليها وقام آخر بها فلم يقدر عليها

DURR-FULL:v1p256/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r3.speaker: أبو أمامة
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r3.claim: A group of Ansar could recall only the basmala of a sura; the Prophet said it had been abrogated overnight and removed from memory and every written copy.
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r3.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أن رهطا من الأنصار من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أخبروه أن رجلا قام من جوف الليل يريد أن يفتتح سورة

DURR-FULL:v1p256/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r4.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r4.claim: Anas says Quran about those killed at Bi'r Ma'una was recited until it was abrogated after its message had been conveyed.
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r4.anchor: عن أنس قال: أنزل الله في الذين قتلوا ببئر معونة قرآنا قرأناه حتى نسخ بعد أن بلغوا قومنا

DURR-FULL:v1p256/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r5.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r5.claim: Abu Musa recalls two forgotten suras: one comparable to Bara'a, except a saying about Adam's two valleys of wealth, and one like a glorification chapter, except an address about saying what one does not do.
DURR-FULL:v1p256/r5.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: كنا نقرأ سورة نشبهها في الطول والشدة ببراءة فأنسيتها غير أني حفظت منها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد : ماننسخ من آية اي نمحو من آية

IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reads the verb in the sense of causing something to be forgotten.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك ، قال : ما ننسخ : ما ننسك

IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says the verse's wording remains written while its ruling is replaced; this is also reported from Ibn Masud's associates, Abu al-Aliya, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قوله : ماننسخ من آية نثبت خطها ونبدل حكمها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r4.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r4.claim: Ata says this concerns what was left out of the Qur'an; Abu Muhammad explains it as material not sent down to Muhammad.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج عن عطاء : ماننسخ من آية اما مانسخ فيما ترك من القران

IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r5.claim: Abu Muhammad clarifies Ata's phrase as material left out because it was not revealed to Muhammad.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r5.anchor: قال أبو محمد : يعني ترك لم ينزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says naskh here means seizure or taking away.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r6.anchor: عن السدى : ماننسخ من آية . نسخها : قبضها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r7.claim: Abu Muhammad explains this as taking away or raising the text, citing the stoning formula and a report about Adam's two valleys of wealth.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو محمد : يعني قبضها . رفعها مثل : الشيخ والشيخة اذا زنيا فارجموها البتة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that revelation would come to the Prophet at night and be forgotten by day, after which this verse was revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان مما ينزل على النبي

IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r9.speaker: سعد بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r9.claim: In a report, Sa'd ibn Malik rebukes Said ibn al-Musayyib's claim to authority, then recites the verse; the same report explains the phrase as God causing Muhammad to forget and cites 87:6 and 18:24.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p199#2/r9.anchor: فقال سعد : ان الله لم ينزل القران على سعيد ولا على أبيه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r1.speaker: محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Qatadah, and Ikrimah are reported to hold a view like Said ibn al-Musayyib's.

IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r2.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the phrase as distinguishing the abrogating verse from the abrogated one.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله : ماننسخ من آية اوننسها قال : الناسخ من المنسوخ

IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r3.claim: Mujahid says the wording remains while its ruling is replaced, also reported from Ibn Masud's associates.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد : أو ننساها قال : نثبت خطها , ونبدل حكمها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r4.claim: In Umar's sermon, Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as postponing or deferring the verse; Abu al-Aliya and Ata are also reported to gloss it as deferral.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس , قال : خطبنا عمر , فقال : يقول الله ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها اي نؤخرها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r5.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r5.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr says it means leaving or removing a verse from among people, then bringing one similar or better; al-Rabi and al-Suddi are also reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r5.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير في قول الله : ماننسخ من آية أو ننسها يقول : أو نتركها نرفعها من عندكم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the alternatives as replacing a verse or leaving it without replacing it.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها يقول : ما نبدل من آية أو نتركها لا نبدلها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r7.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says it means leaving the verse without abrogating it.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r7.anchor: عن السدى أو ننساها فنتركها لا ننسخها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the better verse is more beneficial and gentler for people.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r8.anchor: عن علي ابن عباس قوله : نات بخير منها أو مثلها

IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r9.claim: Abu al-Aliya says an abrogated verse is no longer acted upon, while one deferred is kept with God until it is brought back or replaced.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p200/r9.anchor: عن الربيع عن أبي العالية : ما ننسخ من آية اي فلا يعمل بها : أو ننسها اي نرجيها عندنا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says God brings something better than the verse abrogated or something like the verse left in place.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r1.anchor: عن السدى : نات بخير منها أو مثلها يقول : نات بخير من التي نسخناها ، أو مثل الذي تركناه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r2.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r2.claim: Qatadah says the better or equivalent verse may contain ease, a concession, a command, or a prohibition.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r2.anchor: عن قتادة قول : نات بخير منها أو مثلها فيقول : آية فيها تخفيف ، فيها رخصة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says only God can bring this about, by His authority and power.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p201/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق قوله : على كل شئ قدير اي لا يقدر على هذا غيرك بسلطانك وقدرتك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r1.claim: The Jews defended exclusive belief in Mosaic revelation by claiming their law could not be abrogated; they accused Muhammad's law of invalidating Torah and invoked badāʾ, as if God learned belatedly what to legislate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r1.anchor: وهم في عذرهم ذلك يدعون أن شريعتهم لا تنسخ ويقولون إن محمدا وصف التوراة بأنها حق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r2.claim: God had already exposed their lack of fidelity to their own law and their envy of the Qur'an; the present passage now dismantles their argument against abrogation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r2.anchor: وقد قدمنا أن الله تعالى رد عليهم عذرهم وفضحهم بأنهم ليسوا متمسكين بشرعهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r3.claim: The primary purpose is to teach Muslims that a later law may replace an earlier law and that a ruling within one law may replace an earlier ruling; the direct address to Muslims also refutes the Jews implicitly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p654#2/r3.anchor: والمقصد الأصلي من هذا هو تعليم المسلمين أصلا من أصول الشرائع وهو أصل النسخ الذي يطرأ على شريعة بشريعة بعدها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r1.claim: The word āya can conventionally denote a message, naming something by its customary associate; the cited verse uses āya in that sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r1.anchor: ألكني إليها عمرك الله يا فتى بآية ما جاءت إلينا تهاديا ولذا أيضا سموا الرسالة آية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r2.claim: Here āya means its legal ruling, whether the wording is removed or retained, because the verse explains why rulings are repealed rather than why Qur'anic wording disappears.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r2.anchor: والمراد بالآية هنا حكم الآية سواء أزيل لفظها أم أبقى لفظها لأن المقصود بيان حكمة إبطال الأحكام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r3.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib defines naskh as removing one thing by another thing that takes its place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r3.anchor: والنسخ إزالة الشي بشيء آخر قاله الراغب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r4.claim: The Arabic verb can depict removal and replacement, as sunlight removes shade or shade displaces sunlight, and as bees move wax and honey to another cell.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r4.anchor: تقول نسخت الشمس الظل لأن شعاعها أزال الظل وخلفه في موضعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r5.claim: Naskh may mean removal alone, as when wind erases a trace, or the special establishing of a remover; Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects a sense of mere establishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r5.anchor: وقد يطلق على الإزالة فقط دون تعويض كقولهم نسخت الريح الأثر وعلى الإثبات لكن على إثبات خاص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r6.claim: Calling the transcription of a book naskh is figurative imitation of moving its letters to a new page, not proof that naskh means mere establishment; calling a child his father's copy is metaphor upon metaphor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r6.anchor: لكن هذا توهم لأن إطلاق النسخ على محاكاة حروف الكتاب إطلاق مجازي بالصورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r7.claim: Naskh does not mean simple disappearance without removal: night does not abrogate day, since night is original darkness from the absence of an illuminating body.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r7.anchor: ولا يطلق النسخ على الزوال بدون إزالة فلا تقول نسخ الليل النهار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r8.claim: In this verse naskh is removal with a replacement, as shown by the following promise; legal theorists define it as lifting a legal ruling by a later revealed address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r8.anchor: والمراد من النسخ هنا الإزالة وإثبات العوض بدليل قوله : { نأت بخير منها أو مثلها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r9.claim: The definition excludes newly introduced legislation, which lifts nothing, and the end of original permissibility, since that is absence of obligation before revelation rather than a legal ruling; scripture specifies permissions only in special contexts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p656/r9.anchor: فخرج التشريع المستأنف إذ ليس برفع ، وخرج بقولنا الحكم الشرعي رفع البراءة الأصلية بالشرع المستأنف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r1.claim: The promise is the conditional's answer; its form pairs each kind of abrogation, forgetfulness, or deferral with a suitable replacement or provision at the corresponding time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r1.anchor: وقوله : { نأت بخير منها أو مثلها } جواب الشرط وجعله جوابا مشعر بأن هذين الحالين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r2.claim: With abrogation, what comes is the superseding law or ruling; with causing forgetfulness, it may be a superseding rule or a later contrary rule; with deferral, other rules sustain people during the delay.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r2.anchor: فالمأتي به مع النسخ هو الناسخ من شريعة أو حكم والمأتي به مع الإنساء من النسيان هو الناسخ أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r3.claim: Goodness may mean serving human interests, averting harm, bringing good outcomes or reward, or easing hardship; a stricter rule can still better serve the interest. Each case has either benefit or equivalence, and aw allows either and possibly both.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r3.anchor: وقد أجملت جهة الخيرية والمثلية لتذهب نفس السامع كل مذهب ممكن فتجده مرادا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r4.claim: Examples include Islam replacing Torah and Gospel with a better law, and the law of Ṣāliḥ replacing Hūd's with an equivalent one, since each benefits its community in a comparable way.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r4.anchor: نسخ شريعة مع الإتيان بخير منها كنسخ التوراة والإنجيل بالإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r5.claim: A better ruling example is the initial censure or disfavor of wine in 2:219, later replaced by its categorical prohibition: better for public interest though less lenient.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r5.anchor: مثل نسخ كراهة الخمر الثابتة بقوله : { قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r6.claim: A rule can also be better through greater leniency: permission for food, drink, and marital relations at night in Ramadan replaced the earlier restriction after sleep.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r6.anchor: كنسخ تحريم الأكل والشرب وقربان النساء في ليل رمضان بعد وقت الإفطار عند الغروب إذا نام الصائم قبل أن يتعشى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r7.speaker: صحيح البخاري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r7.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī says Muslims rejoiced when the nighttime Ramadan permission was revealed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p659/r7.anchor: قال في الحديث في ( صحيح البخاري ) ففرح المسلمون بنزولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r1.claim: An example of a law fading away is the law of Adam and Noah giving way to Moses's better, broader law; Idrīs's law is offered as equivalent to Noah's.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r1.anchor: نسيان شريعة بمعنى اضمحلالها كشريعة آدم ونوح مع مجيء شريعة موسى وهي أفضل وأوسع وشريعة إدريس مثلا وهي مثل شريعة نوح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r2.claim: A ruling example is ten known sucklings being replaced by five, then both forgotten, with 4:23 retaining the general rule of milk kinship; the outcomes are equivalent and the small difference poses no hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r2.anchor: كان فيما نزل عشر رضعات معلومات يحرمن فنسخن بخمس معلومات ثم نسيا معا وجاءت آية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r3.claim: Another view takes nisyān to mean abandoning a ruling; on that reading its meaning and cases collapse into those of deferral or causing forgetfulness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r3.anchor: وقيل : المراد من النسيان الترك وهو حينئذ يرجع معناه وصوره إلى معنى وصور الإنساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r4.claim: The promise shows that changing or delaying laws does not compromise God's knowledge, wisdom, or lordship: each change suits people's conditions, advances their interests mercifully, and preserves worldly order until the final law.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r4.anchor: والمقصد من قوله تعالى : { نأت بخير منها أو مثلها } إظهار منتهى الحكمة والرد عليهم بأنهم لا يهمهم أن تنسخ شريعة بشريعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r5.claim: The same divine purpose culminates in Islam as the final religion and in the religion prescribed to Muhammad as the one previously enjoined on Noah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r5.anchor: ولذلك قال : { إن الدين عند الله الإسلام } ( آل عمران : 19 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r6.claim: Better or equivalent applies to both abrogation and forgetfulness or deferral, not as a fold-and-unfold distribution; each case is compensation or reinforcement, so people are never left without provision and no divine change of mind is implied.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p661/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن الإتيان بخير أو بمثل راجع إلى كل من النسخ والإنساء فيكون الإتيان بخير من المنسوخة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r1.claim: Some exegetes understand nunsihā as God making Muslims forget a verse or surah, or making the Prophet forget it, so that collective loss would indicate abrogation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r1.anchor: ما قاله بعض المفسرين في قوله تعالى : { ننسها } أنه إنساء الله تعالى المسلمين للآية أو للسورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r2.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports through al-Ṭabarānī that two men forgot a surah the Prophet had taught them; he told them it was among what had been abrogated and forgotten and to leave it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r2.anchor: بسنده إلى ابن عمر قال ( قرأ رجلان سورة أقرأهما إياها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr grades the Ibn ʿUmar report weak because its chain includes Sulaymān ibn Arqam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r3.anchor: قال ابن كثير هذا الحديث في سنده سليمان بن أرقم وهو ضعيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls the report munkar and questions how a report so unusual could have escaped the leading hadith scholars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية هذا حديث منكر أغرب به الطبراني وكيف خفي مثله على أئمة الحديث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the claim that mass forgetfulness proves abrogation; a Prophet's forgetting a passage God intended to remove rather than preserve as Qur'an is possible in principle, but did not occur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r5.anchor: والصحيح أن نسيان النبيء ما أراد الله نسخه ولم يرد أن يثبته قرآنا جائز ، أي لكنه لم يقع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r6.claim: The Prophet is protected from ordinary forgetfulness before delivering revelation; after delivery and its preservation by Muslims, such a lapse is possible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r6.anchor: فأما النسيان الذي هو آفة في البشر فالنبيء معصوم عنه قبل التبليغ ، وأما بعد التبليغ وحفظ المسلمين له فجائز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet omitted a verse during prayer; after prayer Ubayy asked why he had not reminded him, thinking it had been lifted, and the Prophet replied that he had forgotten it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r7.anchor: وقد روي أنه أسقط آية من سورة في الصلاة فلما فرغ قال لأبي لم لم تذكرني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r8.claim: Temporary forgetfulness followed by recollection is possible but is not the verse's meaning, since that conflicts with its promise of a replacement; permanent loss of Qur'an is likely impermissible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r8.anchor: والحق عندي أن النسيان العارض الذي يتذكر بعده جائز ولا تحمل عليه الآية لمنافاته لظاهر قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r9.claim: The promise in 87:6 that the Prophet will not forget supports the impossibility of permanent Qur'anic loss; 87:7's exception is an accommodation in the promise, to be explained in Sūrat al-Aʿlā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r9.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { سنقرئك فلا تنسى } ( الأعلى : 6 ) دليل عليه وقوله : { إلا ما شاء الله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r10.speaker: أنس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r10.claim: Anas reports in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim that Muslims once recited a surah nearly as long as Barāʾa, then forgot it except for a saying about Adam's desire for more wealth and God's acceptance of repentance; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls the report strange.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r10.anchor: وأما ما ورد في ( صحيح مسلم ) عن أنس قال : كنا نقرأ سورة نشبهها في الطول ببراءة فانسيتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r11.claim: He interprets Anas's report as a surah whose recitation and rulings had both been abrogated; Muslims' forgetting wording removed from Qur'an is unsurprising.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p662/r11.anchor: وتأويله أن هنالك سورة نسخت قراءتها وأحكامها ، ونسيان المسلمين لما نسخ لفظه من القرآن غير عجيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r11.claim: In Arabic, naskh can mean transfer or removal; transfer is not the sense here, while removal is the verse’s sense.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r11.anchor: النسخ في كلام العرب على وجهين: أحدهما النقل كنقل كتاب من آخر، والثاني الإزالة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r12.claim: The transfer sense is absent here but occurs in 45:29, ‘We had been copying down what you did.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r12.anchor: قوله تعالى: إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r13.claim: Removal may leave the abrogated thing’s successor in place, like the sun removing shade, or leave nothing, like wind erasing a trace; legal abrogation has both forms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r13.anchor: وهو منقسم في اللغة على ضربين: أحدهما يثبت الناسخ بعد المنسوخ كقولهم نسخت الشمس الظل، والآخر لا يثبت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r14.claim: God is the true abrogator, though the legal address is called abrogating; Sunni experts define it as a later discourse lifting a ruling that otherwise would have continued.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190/r14.anchor: والناسخ حقيقة هو الله تعالى، ويسمى الخطاب الشرعي ناسخا إذ به يقع النسخ، وحد الناسخ عند حذاق أهل السنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r1.claim: Abrogation is rationally possible for God because it entails neither impossibility nor change in His attributes; commands are not tied to will, and God knows each ruling’s endpoint in advance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r1.anchor: والنسخ جائز على الله تعالى عقلا لأنه ليس يلزم عنه محال ولا تغيير صفة من صفاته تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r2.claim: Abrogation does not arise from newly acquired knowledge or a changed divine will; those would imply change that is impossible for God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r2.anchor: وليست الأوامر متعلقة بالإرادة فيلزم من النسخ أن الإرادة تغيرت، ولا النسخ لطرو علم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r3.claim: Badaʾ is impossible for God because it requires new knowledge or changed will; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Jews wrongly equated it with abrogation and thereby erred.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r3.anchor: والبداء لا يجوز على الله تعالى لأنه لا يكون إلا لطرو علم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r4.speaker: اليهود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r4.claim: The Jews treated abrogation and badaʾ as one thing and rejected both; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this was a mistake.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r4.anchor: وجعلت اليهود النسخ والبداء واحدا، ولذلك لم يجوزوه فضلوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r5.speaker: أئمتنا
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s Sunni imams say the abrogated object is the very established ruling itself.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r5.anchor: والمنسوخ عند أئمتنا: الحكم الثابت نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r6.claim: The Muʿtazilites say abrogation removes the equivalent ruling for future cases, based on their doctrines that commands are intended and goodness is intrinsic; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects those premises.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r6.anchor: لا ما ذهبت إليه المعتزلة، من أنه مثل الحكم الثابت فيما يستقبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r7.claim: Specification can resemble abrogation but is not: the specified item was never included in the general wording; removing something certainly included would be abrogation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r7.anchor: والتخصيص من العموم يوهم أنه نسخ وليس به، لأن المخصص لم يتناوله العموم قط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r8.claim: Abrogation applies only to commands and prohibitions, not reports; an apparent command-as-report objection is answered by its implicit proviso that God may lift it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r8.anchor: والنسخ لا يجوز في الإخبار، وإنما هو مختص بالأوامر والنواهي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r9.speaker: بعض المعترضين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r9.claim: A critic begins an objection by treating an order as a report and asking whether it means an obligation to do something.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p190#2/r9.anchor: ورد بعض المعترضين الأمر خبرا بأن قال:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r1.claim: The objection says a command means ‘it is obligatory that you do this’; Ibn ʿAṭiyya replies that it implicitly includes ‘unless I abrogate and lift it.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r1.anchor: «واجب عليكم أن تفعلوا كذا» ؟ فهذا خبر، والجواب أن يقال: إن في ضمن المعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r2.claim: Abrogation may move from a heavier rule to a lighter one, from lighter to heavier, between equal burdens, or remove a rule without replacement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r2.anchor: فقد ينسخ الأثقل إلى الأخف كنسخ الثبوت لعشرة بالثبوت لاثنين، وقد ينسخ الأخف إلى الأثقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r3.claim: As an example of abrogating both recitation and ruling, Ibn ʿAṭiyya cites Abu Bakr’s report of a former recitation declaring disavowal of fathers to be unbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r3.anchor: قول أبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه: «كنا نقرأ لا ترغبوا عن آبائكم فإنه كفر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r4.claim: Recitation can be lifted while the rule remains, as with the stoning verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r4.anchor: وقد تنسخ التلاوة دون الحكم كآية الرجم،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r5.claim: A ruling can be lifted while recitation remains, as with the alms before private consultation and 60:11 concerning emigrant wives.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r5.anchor: وقد ينسخ الحكم دون التلاوة كصدقة النجوى،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r6.claim: Recitation and ruling are each rulings, so either may be abrogated without the other.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r6.anchor: والتلاوة والحكم حكمان، فجائز نسخ أحدهما دون الآخر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r7.claim: Qur’an may abrogate Qur’an and Sunna Sunna by definitive mass-transmitted reports; abrogation by one-person reports is also agreed when the report abrogates another such report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r7.anchor: وينسخ القرآن بالقرآن، والسنة بالسنة، وهذه العبارة يراد بها الخبر المتواتر القطعي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r8.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r8.claim: Leading scholars allow Sunna to abrogate Qur’an, citing ‘no bequest to an heir’; this is apparent in Malik, while al-Shafiʿi denies it, though the stoning rule’s exemption from flogging rests on Sunna.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r8.anchor: وأبى ذلك الشافعي رحمه الله، والحجة عليه من قوله إسقاطه الجلد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r9.claim: Qur’an may abrogate Sunna: the Jerusalem direction was not in the Qur’an, and 60:10 bars returning emigrant women after their return had been allowed under the Prophet’s pact with Quraysh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r9.anchor: وكذلك حذاق الأئمة على أن السنة تنسخ بالقرآن، وذلك موجود في القبلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r10.speaker: أبو المعالي وغيره
