IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r10.claim: Experts allow Qur’an to be abrogated by a solitary report in principle; Abu al-Maʿali and others say it occurred when a report at Quba announced the change of qibla, while others deny occurrence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r10.anchor: فذهب أبو المعالي وغيره إلى وقوعه في نازلة مسجد قباء في التحول إلى القبلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r11.claim: Analogy cannot abrogate an explicit text because a valid analogy must not contradict a text.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r11.anchor: ولا يصح نسخ نص بقياس إذ من شروط القياس أن لا يخالف نصا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r12.claim: Abrogation occurred only during the Prophet’s lifetime; after his death and the law’s stabilization, consensus says it ceased, and a consensus apparently contrary to text must rest on an unknown abrogating text.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191/r12.anchor: وأما بعد موته واستقرار الشرع فأجمعت الأمة أنه لا نسخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r1.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r1.claim: Some theologians say an abrogating rule takes effect for everyone whether or not they know of it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعض المتكلمين: «النسخ الثابت متقرر في جهة كل أحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r2.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r2.claim: Experts say someone who has not received the abrogating text remains bound by the first ruling until it reaches them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r2.anchor: والذي عليه الحذاق أنه من لم يبلغه الناسخ فهو متعبد بالحكم الأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r3.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r3.claim: Experts permit abrogating a ruling before it is acted upon, as in the story of the intended sacrifice.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r3.anchor: والحذاق على جواز نسخ الحكم قبل فعله، وهو موجود في كتاب الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r4.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r4.claim: Most readers pronounce ننسخ with an open initial ن, from نسخ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «ما ننسخ» بفتح النون، من نسخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r5.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAmir alone among the seven readers uses a damma on the initial ن; Abu ʿAli al-Farisi rejects treating أنسخ as a synonym or causative form, and understands it as ‘find it abrogated.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r5.anchor: وبها قرأ ابن عامر وحده من السبعة، قال أبو علي الفارسي: ليست لغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r6.claim: For the damma reading, Ibn ʿAṭiyya offers either ‘write/reveal from the Preserved Tablet’ or ‘postpone and leave unrevealed’; alternatively it means God permits the Prophet to leave an abrogated verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r6.anchor: ما نكتب وننزل من اللوح المحفوظ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r7.speaker: نافع وحمزة والكسائي وعاصم وابن عامر وجمهور من الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r7.claim: These readers pronounce ننسها with a damma on the first ن, a silent second ن, and kasra on س, without hamza; it is from the causative of ‘forget.’

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r8.claim: Another group adds a hamza after س, yielding the sense ‘postpone’; the verb ansaʾa is used for delaying a debt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r8.anchor: وقرأت ذلك فرقة كما تقدم إلا أنها همزت بعد السين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r9.claim: An unassigned group reads with an open first ن and open س, meaning ‘leave’; Makki cites it without attribution, and Abu ʿUbayd al-Bakri reports it from Saʿd, which Ibn ʿAṭiyya thinks may be mistaken.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r9.anchor: وقرأت طائفة «أو ننسها» بفتح النون الأولى وسكون الثانية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r10.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r10.claim: Saʿd is reported to read تنسها addressing the Prophet; when told Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib read it differently, he retorted that the Qur’an was not revealed to al-Musayyib or his family.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ سعد بن أبي وقاص «أو تنسها» على مخاطبة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r11.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r11.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib is said to read ننسها with the initial ن damma-marked and س bearing kasra.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r11.anchor: إن سعيد بن المسيب يقرؤها بنون أولى مضمومة وسين مكسورة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r12.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r12.claim: A separate report says Saʿid reads تنسها with an initial damma on ت and an open س, deriving it from forgetting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r12.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن المسيب فيما ذكر عنه أيضا «أو تنسها» بضم التاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r13.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم وأبو رجاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak and Abu Rajaʾ read ننسها with the second ن open and a doubled, kasra-marked س, also deriving it from forgetting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p191#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن مزاحم وأبو رجاء «ننسها» بضم النون الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس وإبراهيم النخعي وعطاء ومجاهد وعبيد بن عمير وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r1.claim: These authorities read ننسأها with an open ن followed by a silent ن and a hamzated alif, giving the meaning ‘postpone.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r1.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وابن عباس وإبراهيم النخعي وعطاء بن أبي رباح ومجاهد وعبيد ابن عمير وابن كثير وأبو عمرو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r2.claim: The delay reading is illustrated by Arab usage for delaying camels’ watering and lengthening their thirst by a day or more.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r2.anchor: نسأت الإبل عن الحوض أنسؤها نسأ أي أخرتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r3.claim: A group reads the delay form with an open ت to address the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r3.anchor: وقرأت فرقة مثل هذه القراءة إلا أنها بتاء مفتوحة أولا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r4.claim: Abu Haywa reads the same form with ت damma-marked.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة مثل ذلك إلا أنه ضم التاء أولا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r5.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reads ننسك, addressing the Prophet.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب «أو ننسك» بضم النون الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r6.speaker: سالم مولى أبي حذيفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r6.claim: Salim’s codex has Ubayy’s reading with the added pronoun for the verse: ننسكها.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r6.anchor: وفي مصحف سالم مولى أبي حذيفة «أو ننسكها» مثل قراءة أبي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r7.speaker: الأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r7.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads ‘what We cause you to forget of a verse or abrogate’ and bring its equivalent; Ibn Masʿud’s codex records this wording.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r7.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش «ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها نجىء بمثلها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya groups the readings under three senses: postponement, causing forgetfulness, or leaving/abandoning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r8.anchor: وهذه القراءات لا تخلو كل واحدة منها أن تكون من النسء أو الإنساء بمعنى التأخير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r9.claim: Arabic nisyān usually means the opposite of remembering but can also mean leaving something.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r9.anchor: والنسيان في كلام العرب يجيء في الأغلب ضد الذكر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r10.claim: On the forgetfulness sense, God may cause the Prophet to forget a verse so it is removed entirely, then provide something better or equal in benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r10.anchor: ما ننسخ من آية أو نقدر نسيانك لها فتنساها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r11.claim: On the leaving sense, God may abrogate a verse or leave it unrevealed, while providing a better or equivalent replacement so the religion remains complete.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r11.anchor: ما ننسخ على وجوه النسخ أو نترك غير منزل عليك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r12.claim: A second leaving interpretation is to leave its recitation while lifting its ruling; abrogation then removes both recitation and ruling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r12.anchor: والمعنى الثاني أو نترك تلاوته وإن رفعنا حكمه فيجيء النسخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r13.claim: A third leaving interpretation is to leave its ruling while lifting its recitation, again making abrogation a removal of both.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p192/r13.anchor: والمعنى الثالث أو نترك حكمه وإن رفعنا تلاوته فالنسخ أيضا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r1.claim: A fourth interpretation is to leave the verse intact in both recitation and ruling; the pronouns in ‘better/equal than it’ then refer only to what was abrogated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r1.anchor: نتركها غير منسوخة الحكم ولا التلاوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r2.claim: The postponement reading likewise allows four parallels: delay revelation, ruling, or recitation while retaining the other, or defer a verse without abrogating it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r2.anchor: يحمل على معنى التأخير فإن الآية معه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r3.claim: Some interpretations are stronger than others, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya records all because scholars stated or indicated each possibility.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r3.anchor: وبعض هذه المعاني أقوى من بعض، لكن ذكرنا جميعها لأنها تحتمل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the kasra reading ننسها cannot mean ‘leave,’ since أنسأ does not mean to leave.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج: إن القراءة «أو ننسها» بضم النون وسكون الثانية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r5.speaker: أبو علي وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r5.claim: Abu ʿAli and others accept the ‘leave’ sense by construing it as ‘make you leave it.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r5.anchor: وقال أبو علي وغيره: ذلك متجه لأنه بمعنى نجعلك تتركها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects interpreting the verse as the Prophet forgetting, arguing that he never forgot Qur’an; he cites 17:86 as proof that God did not take away what He revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r6.anchor: وكذلك ضعف الزجاج أن تحمل الآية على النسيان الذي هو ضد الذكر، وقال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r7.speaker: أبو علي وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r7.claim: Abu ʿAli and others say intended forgetting is possible and occurred, with no essential difference from lifting a verse by abrogation; they read 17:86 as threatening removal of all revelation, not a part.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r7.anchor: وقال أبو علي وغيره: ذلك جائز وقد وقع ولا فرق بين أن ترفع الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s preferred position is that God may cause the Prophet to forget what He intends not to preserve as Qur’an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r8.anchor: والصحيح في هذا أن نسيان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما أراد الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r9.claim: The Prophet is protected from human lapses before conveying revelation and after conveyance until a Companion has memorized it; once it is preserved by a Companion, ordinary forgetfulness is possible because the trust has been delivered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r9.anchor: فالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معصوم منه قبل التبليغ وبعد التبليغ ما لم يحفظه أحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r10.claim: A report says the Prophet omitted a verse in prayer, asked whether Ubayy was present, and explained that he had forgotten it rather than it being abrogated; no grading is stated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p193/r10.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: لم ترفع ولكني نسيتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r1.claim: Khayr is comparative: more beneficial now if the replacement is lighter, in the afterlife if heavier, or equally beneficial if the replacement is equivalent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r1.anchor: ولفظة خير في الآية صفة تفضيل، والمعنى بأنفع لكم أيها الناس في عاجل إن كانت الناسخة أخف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r2.claim: Some take خير as a verbal noun and من as marking origin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r2.anchor: وقال قوم «خير» في الآية مصدر و «من» لابتداء الغاية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds the verbal-noun analysis strained because ‘or like it’ would need to coordinate with the pronoun in منها without repeating من.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r3.anchor: ويقلق هذا القول لقوله تعالى أو مثلها إلا أن يعطف المثل على الضمير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r4.claim: Although phrased as a question, ألم تعلم functions as confirmation, which like a direct question needs an alternative clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ألم تعلم أن ظاهره الاستفهام ومعناه التقرير

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r5.claim: Some identify the alternative with أم تريدون in 2:18; others treat أم as disconnected and supply ‘or did you know?’; if the Prophet alone is addressed, the alternative is omitted. Both analyses are transmitted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r5.anchor: فالمعادل هنا على قول جماعة أم تريدون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r6.claim: God abrogates or confirms what He wills and acts freely in His rulings; this answers the Jews’ denial of abrogation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r6.anchor: ومعنى الآية أن الله تعالى ينسخ ما يشاء ويثبت ما يشاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r7.claim: ‘Everything’ is general in wording but particular in scope: reason excludes God’s eternal attributes and impossibilities, which are not things.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r7.anchor: على كل شيء لفظ عموم معناه الخصوص، إذ لم تدخل فيه الصفات القديمة بدلالة العقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r8.claim: In Arabic, a thing means an existent.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r9.claim: Qadīr is an intensive active participle from qadara–yaqdiru; some Arabs instead say qadara–yaqdiru with the opposite vowel pattern.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p194/r9.anchor: وقدير اسم فاعل على المبالغة من «قدر» بفتح العين «يقدر»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r1.speaker: اليهود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r1.claim: After the change of qibla, the Jews objected that Muhammad made things lawful or forbidden whenever he wished; this verse was revealed in response.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r1.anchor: سبب نزولها ان اليهود قالت لما نسخت القبلة إن محمدا يحل لأصحابه إذا شاء ويحرم عليهم إذا شاء فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says naskh linguistically means abolishing one thing and installing another in its place, like the sun removing shade and taking its place.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج النسخ في اللغة إبطال شئ وإقامة آخر مقامه تقول العرب نسخت الشمس الظل إذا أذهبته وحلت محله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r3.speaker: السدي وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r3.claim: One account of naskh is the lifting of both wording and ruling; it is attributed to al-Suddī and also reported among Ibn ʿAbbās’s views.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r3.anchor: أحدها رفع اللفظ والحكم والثاني تبديل الآية بغيرها رويا عن ابن عباس والأول قول السدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r4.speaker: مقاتل وابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r4.claim: Another account defines naskh as replacing one verse with another; it is attributed to Muqātil and also reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r4.anchor: والثاني تبديل الآية بغيرها رويا عن ابن عباس والأول قول السدي والثاني قول مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r5.speaker: مجاهد عن أصحاب ابن مسعود وأبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r5.claim: A third account is that the ruling is lifted while the wording remains; Mujāhid reports it from Ibn Masʿūd’s companions, and Abū al-ʿĀliya also holds it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r5.anchor: والثالث رفع الحكم مع بقاء اللفظ رواه مجاهد عن أصحاب ابن مسعود وبه قال أبوالعالية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads nunsikh with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the sīn; Abū ʿAlī explains it as ‘whatever We find abrogated.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r6.anchor: بضم النون وكسر السيد قال أبو علي أي ما نجده منسوخا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r7.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī explains this reading as God finding the verse abrogated through His act of abrogating it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read nunsāʾhā with hamza, meaning ‘We delay it’; Abū Zayd illustrates delay with camels held back from a watering place and relates nasīʾa to postponement in sale.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r1.anchor: بفتح النون مع الهمزة والمعنى نؤخرها قال أبو زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r2.claim: One meaning of delaying a verse is to leave it unabrogated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r2.anchor: نؤخرها عن النسخ فلا ننسخها قاله الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r3.claim: Another proposed meaning is delaying its revelation so it is never sent down.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r3.anchor: نؤخر إنزالها فلا ننزلها البتة والثالث نؤخرها عن العمل بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r4.claim: A further meaning is delaying its application by abrogating it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r4.anchor: الثالث نؤخرها عن العمل بها بنسخنا إياها حكاهما أبو علي الفارسي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r5.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r5.claim: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ reads tansahā with an open tāʾ and a nūn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ سعد بن أبي وقاص تنسها بتاء مفتوحة ونون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and al-Ḍaḥḥāk read tansahā with ḍamma on the tāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن المسيب والضحاك تنسها بضم التاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r7.speaker: نافع
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r7.claim: Nāfiʿ reads aw nun­sihā with two nūns, the first with ḍamma and second quiescent, meaning ‘or cause you to forget it.’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع أوننسها بنونين الأولى مضمومة والثاينة ساكنة أراد أو ننسكها من النسيان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains ‘better than it’ as gentler and easier for people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p127#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس بألين منها وأيسر على الناس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p128/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p128/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p128/r1.claim: ‘Or its like’ means equal in reward and benefit; replacing a verse with its equivalent serves as a test.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p128/r1.anchor: أي في الثواب والمنفعة فتكون الحكمة في تبديلها بمثلها الاختبار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains naskh as replacing one verse with another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {ما ننسخ من آية} ما نبدل من آية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r2.claim: Mujahid explains naskh as erasing a verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن جريج، عن مجاهد: {ما ننسخ من آية} أي: ما نمح من آية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد عن ابن أبي نجيح
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says the verse’s wording remains while its ruling is changed; this was transmitted from the companions of Ibn Masud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {ما ننسخ من آية} قال: نثبت خطها ونبدل حكمها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r4.speaker: أبو العالية ومحمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliyya and Muhammad ibn Ka‘b al-Qurazi are also reported to hold the interpretation that wording remains while the ruling changes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r4.anchor: وروي عن أبي العالية، ومحمد بن كعب القرظي، نحو ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r5.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the expression as God causing a verse to be forgotten.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {ما ننسخ من آية} ما ننسك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r6.speaker: عطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r6.claim: Ata interprets naskh here as what God leaves from the Quran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء: أما {ما ننسخ} فما نترك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r7.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim glosses what is left as material that was not sent down to Muhammad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن أبي حاتم: يعني: ترك فلم ينزل على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says naskh is a verse’s seizure or withdrawal; Ibn Abi Hatim explains it as being lifted, citing the stoning wording and the saying that Adam’s child would seek a third valley of wealth after two.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: {ما ننسخ من آية} نسخها: قبضها. وقال ابن أبي حاتم: يعني: قبضها: رفعها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r9.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jarir defines naskh as transferring a verse’s ruling to another ruling, changing and replacing it; the term derives from copying a book from one copy to another, like transferring worship from one ruling to another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: {ما ننسخ من آية} ما ينقل من حكم آية إلى غيره فنبدله ونغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r10.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r10.claim: For Ibn Jarir, abrogation applies to commands, prohibitions, restrictions, permissions and legal rulings, not to reports; changing either a verse’s ruling or its wording is called abrogation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r10.anchor: ولا يكون ذلك إلا في الأمر والنهي والحظر والإطلاق والمنع والإباحة. فأما الأخبار فلا يكون فيها ناسخ ولا منسوخ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r11.speaker: علماء الأصول
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r11.claim: Legal theorists phrase the definition differently, but the matter is close; a common summary is lifting a ruling through later legal evidence, including replacement by a lighter or heavier ruling or no replacement, while detailed types and conditions belong to legal theory.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r11.anchor: بعضهم أنه رفع الحكم بدليل شرعي متأخر. فاندرج في ذلك نسخ الأخف بالأثقل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r12.claim: A report transmitted from Salim from his father says two men who had learned a surah from the Prophet could no longer recall a letter; the Prophet said it was among what had been abrogated and forgotten and told them to leave it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r12.anchor: عن سالم، عن أبيه، قال: قرأ رجلان سورة أقرأهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فكانا يقرآن بها، فقاما ذات ليلة يصليان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r13.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r13.claim: Ibn Kathir grades the report about the two men as weak because Sulayman ibn Arqam is weak.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r14.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r14.speaker: الزهري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r14.claim: Al-Zuhri reads nunsiha with a damma on the initial nun and without doubling it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p375#2/r14.anchor: فكان الزهري يقرؤها: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} (3) بضم النون خفيفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r1.claim: The phrase has two readings: nunsāʾihā, with hamza, and nunsihā.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {أو ننسها} (7) فقرئ على وجهين: "ننسأها وننسها".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the hamzated reading as replacing a verse or leaving it unreplaced.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r2.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسئها} يقول: ما نبدل من آية، أو نتركها لا نبدلها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r3.speaker: مجاهد عن أصحاب ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r3.claim: Mujahid, reporting Ibn Masud's companions, says the written text remains while its ruling is changed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد عن أصحاب ابن مسعود: {أو ننسئها} نثبت خطها ونبدل حكمها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r4.speaker: عبيد بن عمير ومجاهد وعطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r4.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr, Mujahid, and Ata interpret the hamzated reading as delaying and postponing a verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r4.anchor: وقال (8) عبيد بن عمير، ومجاهد، وعطاء: {أو ننسئها} نؤخرها ونرجئها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r5.speaker: عطية العوفي والسدي والربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r5.claim: Atiyya al-Awfi, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi say it means delaying a verse without abrogating it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r5.anchor: وقال عطية العوفي: {أو ننسئها} نؤخرها فلا ننسخها. وقال السدي مثله أيضا، وكذا [قال] (9) الربيع بن أنس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the phrase as referring to the abrogating verse in relation to the abrogated one.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r6.anchor: وقال الضحاك: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسئها} يعني: الناسخ من المنسوخ.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r7.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r7.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the verse is deferred with God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r7.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسئها} أي: نؤخرها عندنا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r8.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Umar explaining the phrase in his sermon as meaning that God defers the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: خطبنا عمر، رضي الله عنه، فقال: يقول الله عز وجل: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} أي: نؤخرها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r9.claim: Qatada says God causes His Prophet to forget what He wills and abrogates what He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} قال: كان الله تعالى ينسي نبيه ما يشاء وينسخ ما يشاء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r10.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r10.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet was recited Quran and then forgot it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r10.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قال في قوله: {أو ننسها} (2) قال: إن نبيكم صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرئ قرآنا ثم نسيه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas reports through Ikrima that revelation came to the Prophet at night, which he forgot by day, prompting this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p376/r11.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان مما ينزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي بالليل وينساه بالنهار، فأنزل الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r1.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr interprets nunsihā as God removing the verse from the people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r1.anchor: وقال عبيد بن عمير: {أو ننسها} نرفعها من عندكم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r2.claim: Saʿd reads tun-sihā and rejects Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib's tun-sāʾihā reading, arguing the Quran was not revealed to al-Musayyib's family; he invokes 87:6 and 18:24. Al-Hakim grades the report sound on the two Shaykhs' criteria, though they did not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r2.anchor: سمعت سعد بن أبي وقاص يقرأ: " ما ننسخ من آية أو تنسها" قال: قلت له: فإن سعيد بن المسيب يقرأ: "أو تنسأها".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r3.speaker: محمد بن كعب وقتادة وعكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim reports that Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, Qatada, and Ikrima held a view like Saʿid's reading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r3.anchor: وروي عن محمد بن كعب، وقتادة وعكرمة، نحو قول سعيد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r4.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r4.claim: Umar says Ubay is the community's best reciter, yet they leave some of his recitation because he will not abandon anything heard from the Prophet; Umar cites the verse's authorization of abrogation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p377/r4.anchor: قال عمر: علي أقضانا، وأبي أقرؤنا، وإنا لندع بعض ما يقول أبي، وأبي يقول: سمعت رسول الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r1.claim: A replacement is better or equivalent in its ruling relative to the interests of those accountable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r1.anchor: أي: في الحكم بالنسبة إلى مصلحة المكلفين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the replacement is more beneficial and easier for people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r2.anchor: كما قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {نأت بخير منها} يقول: خير لكم في المنفعة، وأرفق بكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains abrogation as no longer acting on a verse and postponement as leaving it with God until He brings it or its like.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r3.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: {ما ننسخ من آية} فلا نعمل بها، {أو ننسئها} أي: نرجئها (2) عندنا، نأت بها أو نظيرها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says God brings something better than what He abrogated, or something like what He left.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: {نأت بخير منها أو مثلها} يقول: نأت بخير من الذي نسخناه، أو مثل الذي تركناه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r5.claim: Qatada describes such a verse as containing alleviation, a concession, a command, or a prohibition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: {نأت بخير منها أو مثلها} يقول: آية فيها تخفيف، فيها رخصة، فيها أمر، فيها نهي.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r6.claim: God alone controls creation and legislation, testing obedience through abrogation: He commands for a known benefit, then forbids with wisdom; complete obedience follows His commands and messengers. This rebuts Jewish denials of abrogation as impossible by reason or revelation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r6.anchor: فيحل ما يشاء، ويحرم ما يشاء، ويبيح ما يشاء، ويحظر ما يشاء، وهو الذي يحكم ما يريد لا معقب لحكمه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r7.claim: Ibn Jarir paraphrases God as owning the heavens and earth, commanding, forbidding, abrogating, replacing, and altering rulings as He wills while retaining what He wills.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378/r7.anchor: أحكم فيهما وفيما فيهما بما أشاء، وآمر فيهما وفيما فيهما بما أشاء، وأنهى عما أشاء، وأنسخ وأبدل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir says the address about God's sovereignty also refutes Jews who denied Torah abrogation and rejected Jesus and Muhammad because they changed Torah rulings; God's subjects owe obedience to His commands and prohibitions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r1.anchor: تكذيب لليهود الذين أنكروا نسخ أحكام التوراة، وجحدوا نبوة عيسى ومحمد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r2.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r2.claim: As examples of abrogation, God ordered Abraham to sacrifice his son and lifted the command before the act, and commanded Israelites to kill calf worshippers before lifting it to prevent their annihilation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r2.anchor: وأمر إبراهيم، عليه السلام، بذبح ولده، ثم نسخه قبل الفعل، وأمر جمهور بنى إسرائيل بقتل من عبد العجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r3.claim: The author says Jews contest abrogation from unbelief and stubbornness: reason does not preclude God changing rulings, and earlier laws did so, including marriage rules for Adam's children, Noah's food laws, and Jacob's descendants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r3.anchor: ليس في العقل ما يدل على امتناع النسخ في أحكام الله تعالى؛ لأنه يحكم ما يشاء كما أنه يفعل ما يريد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r4.claim: The author says Jews acknowledge earlier changes—Adam's children could marry each other, Noah was allowed all animals then some were prohibited, and Jacob's descendants could marry two sisters before Torah law forbade it—but evade their force.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r4.anchor: وكان نكاح الأختين مباح لإسرائيل وبنيه، وقد حرم ذلك في شريعة التوراة وما بعدها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r5.claim: Verbal replies do not defeat the substance of these proofs; Jewish books prophesy Muhammad and command following him, which makes his law binding and no deed accepted except under it. Whether earlier laws expired at his mission or were abrogated by his law, following him is obligatory as God's most recent scripture was given to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p378#2/r5.anchor: وكما في كتبهم مشهورا من البشارة بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والأمر باتباعه، فإنه يفيد وجوب متابعته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p379/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p379/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p379/r1.claim: God's sole dominion entails His authority to legislate; the author cites 7:54 and 3:93, and says Muslims unanimously allow and affirm the occurrence of abrogation in divine rulings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p379/r1.anchor: فكما أن له الملك بلا منازع، فكذلك له الحكم بما يشاء، {ألا له الخلق والأمر} [الأعراف: 54]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p379/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p379/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصبهاني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p379/r2.claim: Abu Muslim al-Asfahani claims no Quranic abrogation occurred; Ibn Kathir calls this weak and rejected, and says his evasions fail to explain the waiting-period change, qibla change, reduced combat ratio, and charity before private consultation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p379/r2.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم الأصبهاني المفسر: لم يقع شيء من ذلك في القرآن، وقوله هذا ضعيف مردود مرذول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r1.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r1.claim: Umar says Ali was the community’s best judge and Ubay its finest reciter; Ubay said he learned the disputed recitation from the Prophet and would not abandon it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال عمر: علي أقضانا، وأبي أقرأنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r2.claim: The episode shows that even an elder may believe a statement correct when it is actually mistaken.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r2.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن الرجل الكبير قد يقول الشيء يظنه صوابا وهو خطأ في نفس الأمر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r3.claim: Malik says every person’s opinion may be accepted or rejected except the Prophet’s, whose word is wholly accepted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p54/r3.anchor: ولهذا قال الإمام مالك: ما من أحد إلا يؤخذ من قوله ويرد إلا قول صاحب هذا القبر

JISHUMI:v1p536/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
JISHUMI:v1p536/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads with ḍamma on nūn and kasra on sīn; other readers use fatḥa, from copying a book.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر ما ننسخ بضم النون وكسر السين، والباقون بفتحها،

JISHUMI:v1p536/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد
JISHUMI:v1p536/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayd analyzes it as 'we cause you, Muḥammad, to copy,' as when one copies a book for another.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r2.anchor: ما قاله أبو عبيد: ما ننسخك يا محمد، كما قال: نسخت الكتاب، وأنسخته غيري،

JISHUMI:v1p536/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p536/r3.claim: Another analysis means making something have a copy, like giving a person a grave; the Qurʾān uses it in ثم أماته فأقبره.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنسخته جعلته ذا نسخ، كما قال قوم للحجاج وقد صلب رجلا: أقبرنا فلانا،

JISHUMI:v1p536/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v1p536/r4.claim: They read nansaʾhā with fatḥa and hamza as a conditional jussive meaning defer; Abū ʿAmr keeps the hamza because sukun marks the jussive.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ننسأها بفتح النون والهمزة، وهو جزم بالشرط،

JISHUMI:v1p536/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r5.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v1p536/r5.claim: The other readers use ḍamma on nūn and kasra on sīn, from forgetting or leaving aside.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r5.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بضم النون وكسر السين من النسيان أو من الترك.

JISHUMI:v1p536/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p536/r6.claim: Naskh can mean copying a book or removing a rule; ʿAlī b. ʿĪsā derives it from replacement and Abū Hāshim from removal, as sun erases shade and wind traces.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r6.anchor: النسخ: نسخك كتابا عن كتاب، والنسخ: أن تزيل أمرا كان يعمل به، واختلفوا في أصله

JISHUMI:v1p536/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r7.speaker: أبو هاشم
JISHUMI:v1p536/r7.claim: Abū Hāshim says legal naskh is used by analogy to its lexical sense; another view makes it a transferred legal term.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r7.anchor: فقيل: إنه يستعمل في الشرع تشبيها باللغة، عن أبي هاشم، وقيل: هي لفظة شرعية منقولة

JISHUMI:v1p536/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r8.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p536/r8.claim: The Qāḍī defines abrogation as a later text showing a binding ruling will not continue, though absent that text it would remain.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r8.anchor: هو ما دل على أن مثل الحكم الثابت بالشرع غير ثابت في المستقبل على وجه لولاه لكان ثابتا بالنص الأول

JISHUMI:v1p536/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r9.speaker: علي بن عيسى
JISHUMI:v1p536/r9.claim: ʿAlī b. ʿĪsā defines abrogation as lifting a binding rule and replacing it with another.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r9.anchor: وقيل: رفع كل شيء قد كان يلزم العمل به إلى بدل منه، عن علي بن عيسى - رحمه الله -.

JISHUMI:v1p536/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p536/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p536/r10.claim: Nasāʾ means delay, as with camels kept from water; related forms include deferred sale and postponement of a sacred month.
JISHUMI:v1p536/r10.anchor: والنسا: التأخير، يقال: نسأت الإبل عن الحوض أي أخرتها، ومنه سمي النسأ، والنسيئة في البيع،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r1.speaker: رُوي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed after critics objected that Muhammad gave an instruction, withdrew it, and contradicted himself the next day.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r1.anchor: روى انهم طعنوا في النسخ فقالوا ألا ترون إلى محمد يامر أصحابه بأمر ثم ينهاهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r2.claim: Reported forms include ما ننسخ, a form with ḍamma from أنسخ, and ننسأها.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r2.anchor: بضم النون من انسخ أو ننسأها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r3.claim: Other readings include forms with and without tashdīd, and forms addressed to the Messenger.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r3.anchor: بالتشديد و ( تنسها ) و ( تنسها ) على خطاب رسول الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r4.anchor: عبد الله ( ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r5.speaker: حذيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r5.claim: Ḥudhayfa reads ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسكها.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r5.anchor: حذيفة ( ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسكها )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r6.claim: Naskh removes a verse by replacing it; insākh is the command to abrogate it, nasyʾ delays or removes it without replacement, and insāʾ removes it from memory.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r6.anchor: ونسخ الآية إزالتها بإبدال أخرى مكانها وإنساخها الأمر بنسخها وهو ان يأمر جبريل عليه السلام بأن يجعلها منسوخة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r7.claim: The alternatives cover removing wording and ruling together or either one, with or without a replacement, according to what serves the interest.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#2/r7.anchor: والمعنى أن كل آية يذهب بها على ما توجبه المصلحة من أزالة لفظها وحكمها معا أو من إزالة أحدهما إلى بدل أو غير بدل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r1.claim: A better verse is better for servants because acting on it brings more reward; or it may be equal in reward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r1.anchor: بآية خير منها للعباد أي بآية العمل بها اكثر للثواب أو مثلها في ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r2.claim: God can provide something better or equal in goodness because He has power over everything.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r2.anchor: فهو يقدر على الخير وما هو خير منه وعلى مثله في الخير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r3.claim: The statement that God owns heaven and earth means He owns and administers people’s affairs for their interests and knows which abrogating or abrogated rules benefit them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r3.anchor: فهو يملك اموركم يدبرها ويجريها على حسب ما يصلحكم وهو اعلم بما يتعبدكم به من ناسخ ومنسوخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r4.claim: The reminder of God’s ownership and wise management urges trust in what He prescribes rather than proposing demands to the Messenger.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r4.anchor: أراد ان يوصيهم بالثقة به فيما هو أصلح لهم مما يتعبدهم به وينزل عليهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r5.claim: He warns against repeating the Israelites’ demand to Moses to make them a god, whose outcome was ruinous.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p201#3/r5.anchor: وان لا يقترحوا على رسولهم ما اقترحه آباء اليهود على موسى عليه السلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p202/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p202/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p202/r1.claim: The demand to see God openly is another example of the Israelites’ harmful proposals to Moses.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r1.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r1.claim: Al-Suddī interprets naskh as taking an āya away.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r1.anchor: أحدها : أنه قبضها , وهو قول السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets naskh as replacement.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r2.anchor: والثاني : أنه تبديلها , وهو قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the text remains written while its ruling is changed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r3.anchor: والثالث : أنه إثبات خطها وتبديل حكمها , وهو قول ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r4.claim: Al-Māwardī records two readings here: nunsihā and nansāʾhā.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r4.anchor: فيه قراءتان : أحدهما : هذه , والثانية : { أو ننسأها }

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r5.claim: One reading takes nunsihā to mean “retain it”; Ibn Masʿūd’s codex wording says “retain an āya or replace it.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r5.anchor: في مصحف عبد الله ابن مسعود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r6.claim: The explanation adds that the Prophet would recite an āya, then forget it and have it withdrawn.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r6.anchor: وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , كان يقرأ الآية , ثم ينسى وترفع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r7.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r7.claim: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ reads the verb as direct address to Muhammad: “or you forget”; Mujāhid and Qatāda give that sense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r7.anchor: وكان سعد بن أبي وقاص يقرأ :

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r8.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r8.claim: When Qāsim ibn Rabīʿa cites Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab’s reading, Saʿd rejects its authority and invokes 87:6 and 18:24.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r8.anchor: فقال سعد : إن القرآن لم ينزل على ابن المسيب , ولا على آل المسيب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Suddī understand it as leaving an āya unaltered: it is neither replaced nor abrogated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r9.anchor: أن ذلك بمعنى الترك , من قوله تعالى : { نسوا الله فنسيهم } , أي تركوه فتركهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r10.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r10.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk takes the phrase to refer to the abrogating and abrogated passages.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r10.anchor: قال : الناسخ والمنسوخ , وهذا قول الضحاك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets nunsihā as erasing an āya.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r11.anchor: والرابع : أن معنى ننسها أي نمحها , وهذا قول ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r12.speaker: عطاء وابن أبي نجيح
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r12.claim: The alternate reading nansāʾhā means “defer it,” from the verb nasaʾa, to delay.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r12.anchor: وهذا قول عطاء وابن أبي نجيح

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes “better” as more beneficial and gentler for believers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r13.anchor: أحدهما : أي خير لكم في المنفعة , وأرفق بكم , وهذا قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r14.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r14.claim: Qatāda takes “better” to mean lighter, through a concession in the ruling.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r14.anchor: والثاني : أن معنى خير منها , أي أخف منها , بالترخيص فيها , وهذا معنى قول قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r15.claim: Māwardī summarizes: when God changes a ruling He replaces it, or leaves it unchanged; the replacement is better for believers through ease now or greater reward later.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r15.anchor: فيكون تأويل الآية , ما نغير من حكم آية فنبدله , أو نتركه فلا نبدله , نأت بخير لكم أيها المؤمنون حكما منها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r16.claim: Night prayer was eased by abrogation, illustrating greater ease in the present life.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r16.anchor: كالذي كان من نسخ قيام الليل تخفيفا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r17.claim: Replacing the fast of a few set days with Ramadan fasting illustrates greater reward in the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r17.anchor: كالذي كان من نسخ صيام أيام معدودات بشهر رمضان

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r18.claim: “Or like it” means a ruling with comparable ease or burden and reward; changing the qibla from Jerusalem to the Kaʿba is the example.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r18.anchor: من نسخ استقبال بيت المقدس , باستقبال الكعبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r19.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r19.claim: One explanation takes alam taʿlam as “Have I informed you?”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r19.anchor: أن قوله ألم تعلم بمعنى أعلمت

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r20.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r20.claim: Another reads it as rhetorical confirmation, not a real question; the address to Jesus in 5:116 is a parallel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r20.anchor: أنه خارج مخرج التقرير , لا مخرج الاستفهام . كما قال الله تعالى :

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r21.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r21.claim: The address is to the Prophet while the intended audience is his community, as the following plural “you” shows.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p170/r21.anchor: للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , والمراد به أمته

MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r1.speaker: عبيد بن عمير المبثي
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r1.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr glosses causing a verse to be forgotten as leaving it, then removing it from the people.
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r1.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير المبثي في قوله ﴿ ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها ﴾ يقول أو نتركها

MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير المبثي
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r2.claim: In Ubayd ibn Umayr's explanation, God replaces what He removes with something equal or better.
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r2.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير المبثي في قوله ﴿ ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها ﴾ يقول أو نتركها نرفعها من عندكم فنأتي بمثلها

MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r3.speaker: أصحاب ابن مسعود
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud's companions say abrogation preserves a verse's written wording while changing its ruling.
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r3.anchor: عن أصحاب ابن مسعود في قوله ﴿ ما ننسخ من آية ﴾ أي نثبت خطها ونبدل حكمها

MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r4.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r4.speaker: أصحاب ابن مسعود
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r4.claim: They also explain it as deferring the verse with God, who then brings it or another verse.
MUJAHID:v1p85#2/r4.anchor: عن أصحاب ابن مسعود في قوله ﴿ ما ننسخ من آية ﴾ أي نثبت خطها ونبدل حكمها أي نرجئها عندنا نأت بها

MUQATIL:2:106/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:106/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:106/r1.claim: Naskh means replacing an ayah; God brings a better and more beneficial revelation in its place.
MUQATIL:2:106/r1.anchor: { ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها } ، يعني نبدل من آية فنحولها فيها تقديم، يقول: { نأت بخير منها }

MUQATIL:2:106/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:106/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:106/r2.claim: Muqatil explains the alternative as bringing something equal to what was abrogated, or leaving an ayah as it is without abrogating it.
MUQATIL:2:106/r2.anchor: ثم قال: { أو مثلها } ، يقول: أو نأت بمثل ما نسخنا أو ننسها، يقول: أو نتركها كما هى، فلا ننسخها،

MUQATIL:2:106/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:106/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:106/r3.claim: Meccan disbelievers accused Muhammad of inventing the Quran; the verse was revealed to magnify God's power, including His power over abrogation and what replaces it.
MUQATIL:2:106/r3.anchor: وذلك أن كفار مكة قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنما تقولت أنت يا محمد هذا القرآن من تلقاء نفسك،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r1.claim: Naskh linguistically means replacement; legally it declares the end of a ruling understood by us as continuing, so it replaces for us but clarifies for the Lawgiver.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r1.anchor: تفسير النسخ لغة التبديل وشريعة بيان انتهاء الحكم الشرعى المطلق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r2.claim: This account answers the charge of badaʾ made by Jews who deny abrogation: God clarifies a ruling’s end rather than changing His knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r2.anchor: وفيه جواب عن البداء الذى يدعيه منكروه أعنى اليهود

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r3.claim: Abrogation applies to a ruling possible in itself and lacking an explicit or implied time limit or declaration of permanence.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r3.anchor: ومحله حكم يحتمل الوجود والعدم فى نفسه لم يلحق به ما ينافى النسخ

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r4.claim: Valid abrogation requires ability to form inward commitment, not ability to act; the author rejects the Muʿtazila’s added condition.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r4.anchor: وشرطه التمكن من عقد القلب عندنا دون التمكن من الفعل خلافا للمعتزلة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r5.claim: Abrogation may occur through Qur’an or Sunna, whether the sources agree or differ.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r6.claim: The author permits abrogating recitation and ruling together, the ruling alone, or the recitation alone.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز نسخ التلاوة والحكم والحكم دون التلاوة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r7.claim: Abrogating a description through a ruling, such as adding to a text, counts as abrogation for the author, contrary to al-Shafiʿi.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r7.anchor: ونسخ وصف بالحكم مثل الزيادة على النص فإنه نسخ عندنا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r8.claim: Making a verse forgotten means removing it from people’s memory.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r8.anchor: والانساء أن يذهب بحفظها عن القلوب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r9.speaker: مكي وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r9.claim: Makki and Abu ʿAmr read ننسأها, from نسأت, meaning to defer it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r9.anchor: مكى و أبو عمرو أى نؤخرها من نسأت

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r10.claim: A better replacement benefits people because acting on it earns greater reward.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r10.anchor: نأت بآية خير منها للعباد أى بآية العمل بها أكثر للثواب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r11.claim: A replacement may instead be equal in this respect, since no Qur’anic verse is superior to another.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p63#2/r11.anchor: فى ذلك إذ لا فضيلة لبعض الآيات على البعض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r1.claim: ننسها is coordinated with ننسخ, with its final yāʾ omitted because the verb is jussive; in the hamza reading ننسأها, the hamza’s ḍamma is omitted for the same reason.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r1.anchor: «ننسها» عطف على «ننسخ»، وحذفت الياء للجزم. ومن قرأ «ننسأها» حذف الضمة من الهمزة للجزم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r2.claim: نأت is the apodosis of the conditional construction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r2.anchor: { نأت } جواب الشرط، وهذه آية عظمى في الأحكام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi calls this a tremendous verse concerning legal rulings and says knowledge of abrogation is essential for scholars to understand legal cases and distinguish lawful from unlawful.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r3.anchor: معرفة هذا الباب أكيدة وفائدته عظيمة، لا يستغني عن معرفته العلماء، ولا ينكره إلا الجهلة الأغبياء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r4.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r4.claim: When ʿAli found a preacher frightening people, he asked whether the man knew abrogating and abrogated rulings; after the man said no, ʿAli expelled him from the mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r4.anchor: روى أبو البختري قال: دخل علي رضي الله عنه المسجد فإذا رجل يخوف الناس فقال: ما هذا؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r5.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r5.claim: In another version, ʿAli asks whether the preacher knows abrogating and abrogated rulings, then says he has ruined himself and misled others.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r5.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى: أعلمت الناسخ والمنسوخ؟ قال: لا قال: هلكت وأهلكت.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi says a similar report about knowledge of abrogation is also transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r6.anchor: ومثله عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r7.claim: In Arabic naskh can mean transferring or copying, as with a book; the Qur’an was transferred from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, but that sense is not meant here.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r7.anchor: النسخ في كلام العرب على وجهين: أحدهما: النقل كنقل كتاب من آخر. وعلى هذا يكون القرآن كله منسوخا أعني من اللوح المحفوظ

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r8.claim: The expression نستنسخ in 45:29 means that God orders the recording and preservation of deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r8.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى: إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون [الجاثية: 29] أي نأمر بنسخه وإثباته.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r9.claim: The other Arabic sense is cancellation or removal; one kind removes something and installs another in its place, like the sun removing shade, and is the sense intended in the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106/r9.anchor: الثاني: الإبطال والإزالة، وهو المقصود هنا وهو منقسم في اللغة على ضربين: أحدهما: إبطال الشيء وزواله وإقامة آخر مقامه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r1.claim: The Muslim report “no prophethood ever passed except by transformation” uses تناسخت for a community’s transition from one state to another.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r1.anchor: " لم تكن نبوة قط إلا تناسخت " أي تحولت من حال إلى حال يعني أمر الأمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r2.claim: Ibn Faris defines naskh as copying a book and as removing a previously operative ruling and replacing it with another; anything that succeeds another may be called its successor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن فارس: النسخ نسخ الكتاب، والنسخ أن تزيل أمرا كان من قبل يعمل به ثم تنسخه بحاديث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r3.claim: The other kind of removal leaves no replacement, as when wind erases a trace; 22:52 says God removes what Satan casts, leaving it neither recited nor written in the codex.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r3.anchor: إزالة الشيء دون أن يقوم آخر مقامه كقولهم: نسخت الريح الأثر ومن هذا المعنى قوله تعالى: فينسخ الله ما يلقي الشيطان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r4.claim: Abu ʿUbayd says revelation could descend as a surah and then be lifted so it was no longer recited or written.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r4.anchor: وزعم أبو عبيد أن هذا النسخ الثاني قد كان ينزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم السورة فترفع فلا تتلى ولا تكتب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب وعائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r5.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb and ʿAʾisha are reported to have said that al-Ahzab had once been as long as al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r5.anchor: قلت: ومنه ما روي عن أبي بن كعب وعائشة رضي الله عنهما أن سورة «الأحزاب» كانت تعدل سورة البقرة في الطول

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r6.speaker: أبو أمامة بن سهل بن حنيف
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r6.claim: Abu Umama reports that several men could not recite a Qur’anic surah they had known; the Prophet said it was among what God had abrogated the previous night. No grading is stated.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#2/r6.anchor: حدثني أبو أمامة بن سهل ابن حنيف في مجلس سعيد بن المسيب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r1.claim: In one narration, Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib heard Abu Umama relate the report about the lost surah and did not object.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r1.anchor: وفي إحدى الروايات: وسعيد بن المسيب يسمع ما يحدث به أبو أمامة فلا ينكره.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r2.speaker: طوائف من المنتمين للإسلام المتأخرين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r2.claim: Some later Muslim groups deny that abrogation is possible, but al-Qurtubi says the early generations’ consensus that it occurred in the law refutes them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r2.anchor: أنكرت طوائف من المنتمين للإسلام المتأخرين جوازه وهم محجوجون بإجماع السلف السابق على وقوعه في الشريعة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r3.speaker: طوائف من اليهود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r3.claim: Groups of Jews also deny abrogation; al-Qurtubi answers that their own Torah, by their account, describes changed divine commands.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r3.anchor: وأنكرته أيضا طوائف من اليهود وهم محجوجون بما جاء في توراتهم بزعمهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r4.claim: Examples include God permitting Noah and his descendants all animals except blood, later restrictions for Moses and Israel, sibling marriage for Adam’s children but not later generations, Abraham’s son first designated for sacrifice then spared, the command to kill calf-worshippers later lifted, and Moses’ law becoming binding after his commissioning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r4.anchor: قال لنوح عليه السلام عند خروجه من السفينة: إني قد جعلت كل دابة مأكلا لك ولذريتك، وأطلقت ذلك لكم كنبات العشب، ما خلا الدم فلا تأكلوه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r5.claim: Abrogation is not badaʾ; it transfers people from one act of worship or ruling to another for a change in interest, displaying God’s wisdom and sovereignty.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r5.anchor: وليس هذا من باب البداء بل هو نقل العباد من عبادة إلى عبادة، وحكم إلى حكم لضرب من المصلحة، إظهارا لحكمته وكمال مملكته.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r6.claim: All rational people agree that prophetic laws aim at religious and worldly interests; changed commands track changed interests, like a physician adapting treatment to a patient’s state.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r6.anchor: ولا خلاف بين العقلاء أن شرائع الأنبياء قصد بها مصالح الخلق الدينية والدنيوية وإنما كان يلزم البداء لو لم يكن عالما بمآل الأمور

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r7.claim: Badaʾ would imply ignorance of outcomes; God’s address may change with circumstances, but His knowledge and will do not, since change in them is impossible.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r7.anchor: فإنما تتبدل خطاباته بحسب تبدل المصالح كالطبيب المراعي أحوال العليل فراعى ذلك في خليقته بمشيئته وإرادته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r8.claim: Al-Qurtubi says Jews erred by treating abrogation and badaʾ as one thing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#3/r8.anchor: وجعلت اليهود النسخ والبداء شيئا واحدا ولذلك لم يجوزوه فضلوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r1.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r1.claim: Al-Nahhas distinguishes abrogation as transferring a legal obligation from permitted to forbidden or the reverse; badaʾ is abandoning a prior resolve, a human defect caused by imperfection.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r1.anchor: قال النحاس: والفرق بين النسخ والبداء أن النسخ تحويل العبادة من شيء إلى شيء قد كان حلالا فيحرم، أو كان حراما فيحلل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r2.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r2.claim: Al-Nahhas illustrates badaʾ with deciding that someone should visit today, then changing one’s mind and saying not to go, or changing one’s planting plan.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r2.anchor: وأما البداء فهو ترك ما عزم عليه كقولك: امض إلى فلان اليوم ثم تقول لا تمض إليه فيبدو لك العدول عن القول الأول

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r3.claim: God is the true abrogator; the legal address is called abrogating figuratively because abrogation occurs through it, and the ruling being removed can also be called the abrogator by metonymy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r3.anchor: اعلم أن الناسخ على الحقيقة هو الله تعالى، ويسمى الخطاب الشرعي ناسخا تجوزا، إذ به يقع النسخ

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r4.claim: The abrogated item is the removed ruling; the one abrogated from is the person who had been charged with that ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r4.anchor: فالمنسوخ هو المزال، والمنسوخ عنه هو المتعبد بالعبادة المزالة، وهو المكلف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r5.speaker: القاضي عبد الوهاب والقاضي أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r5.claim: The precise Sunni definition is removing an established legal ruling by a later-arriving legal address; absent the later address, the earlier ruling would remain.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r5.anchor: فالذي عليه الحذاق من أهل السنة أنه إزالة ما قد استقر من الحكم الشرعي بخطاب وارد متراخيا هكذا حده القاضي عبد الوهاب والقاضي أبو بكر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r6.claim: The definition’s terms exclude rational judgments, include textual, apparent, and implied forms of evidence, exclude analogy and consensus as abrogating means, and require temporal delay so abrogation is not mere explanation of a ruling’s endpoint.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r6.anchor: وذكر الخطاب ليعم وجوه الدلالة من النص والظاهر والمفهوم وغيره وليخرج القياس والإجماع، إذ لا يتصور النسخ فيهما ولا بهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r7.speaker: أهل السنة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r7.claim: Sunnis hold that the abrogated item is the very ruling previously established, while the Muʿtazila say the earlier address declares that an equivalent future ruling will end.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r7.anchor: المنسوخ عند أئمتنا أهل السنة هو الحكم الثابت نفسه لا مثله كما تقوله المعتزلة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r8.claim: The Muʿtazila define the abrogated matter as an address stating that a future instance of the same ruling is removed, a position al-Qurtubi says follows from their doctrines about divine commands and goodness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r8.anchor: كما تقوله المعتزلة بأنه الخطاب الدال على أن مثل الحكم الثابت فيما يستقبل بالنص المتقدم زائل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r9.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r9.claim: The majority restrict abrogation to commands and prohibitions because a report cannot be abrogated without implying that God’s report was false.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r9.anchor: فالجمهور على أن النسخ إنما هو مختص بالأوامر والنواهي، والخبر لا يدخله النسخ لاستحالة الكذب على الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r10.claim: Another view permits abrogating a report when it contains a legal ruling, with the example from 16:67 continued in the next segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#4/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن الخبر إذا تضمن حكما شرعيا جاز نسخه كقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r1.claim: The example of a report containing a legal ruling is “from the fruits of palms and grapes you take intoxicant,” at 16:67.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r1.anchor: ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r2.claim: Specification from a general expression is not abrogation because the specified item was never included; if it had first been included and later removed, that would be abrogation. Early scholars sometimes called specification abrogation figuratively.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r2.anchor: التخصيص من العموم يوهم أنه نسخ وليس به لأن المخصص لم يتناوله العموم قط

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r3.claim: An apparently universal report may be qualified elsewhere without being abrogated: 2:186 appears to promise every caller an answer, while 6:41 limits it by God’s will.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r3.anchor: كقوله تعالى: وإذا سألك عبادي عني فإني قريب أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان [البقرة: 186].

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r4.claim: The qualification comes in 6:41, so this case is a general statement being restricted, not abrogation of a report.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r4.anchor: كقوله: فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء [الأنعام: 41]. فقد يظن من لا بصيرة عنده أن هذا من باب النسخ في الأخبار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r5.claim: Legal rulings may be abrogated from heavier to lighter, as standing for ten enemies becomes standing for two, or from lighter to heavier, as the fast of ʿAshura and counted days gives way to Ramadan.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r5.anchor: قال علماؤنا رحمهم الله تعالى: جائز نسخ الأثقل إلى الأخف كنسخ الثبوت لعشرة بالثبوت لاثنين. ويجوز نسخ الأخف إلى الأثقل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r6.claim: Like-for-like rulings may replace one another, as with the direction of prayer; a ruling may also be removed without a substitute, as with the alms before private consultation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r6.anchor: وينسخ المثل بمثله ثقلا وخفة، كالقبلة. وينسخ الشيء لا إلى بدل كصدقة النجوى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi lists Qur’an by Qur’an, Sunnah by a definitive mutawatir report, and solitary report by solitary report among valid forms of abrogation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r7.anchor: وينسخ القرآن بالقرآن. والسنة بالعبارة وهذه العبارة يراد بها الخبر المتواتر القطعي. وينسخ خبر الواحد بخبر الواحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r8.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r8.claim: The leading jurists permit the Qur’an to be abrogated by Sunnah, as in “no bequest for an heir”; al-Qurtubi says this is Malik’s apparent position.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r8.anchor: وحذاق الأئمة على أن القرآن ينسخ بالسنة، وذلك موجود في قوله عليه السلام:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r9.speaker: الشافعي وأبو الفرج المالكي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r9.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and Abu al-Faraj al-Maliki reject Qur’an being abrogated by Sunnah; al-Qurtubi prefers the contrary view because both are God’s ruling despite their different names.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r9.anchor: وأبى ذلك الشافعي وأبو الفرج المالكي والأول أصح، بدليل أن الكل حكم الله تعالى ومن عنده وإن اختلفت في الأسماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r10.claim: A further proof is that stoning a married adulterer removes the flogging requirement; only the Prophet’s Sunnah can account for that removal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r10.anchor: فإن الجلد ساقط في حد الزنى عن الثيب الذي يرجم، ولا مسقط لذلك إلا السنة فعل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r11.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r11.claim: The leading jurists also allow Sunnah to be abrogated by Qur’an, as with the qibla, since prayer toward Syria was not prescribed in the Qur’an.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#5/r11.anchor: والحذاق أيضا على أن السنة تنسخ بالقرآن وذلك موجود في القبلة، فإن الصلاة إلى الشام لم تكن في كتاب الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r1.claim: The Qur’anic instruction not to return believing women to unbelievers in 60:10 abrogated their return under the Prophet’s peace agreement with Quraysh.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r1.anchor: فلا ترجعوهن إلى الكفار [الممتحنة: 10] فإن رجوعهن إنما كان بصلح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لقريش.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r2.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r2.claim: The leading jurists allow Qur’an to be abrogated rationally by a solitary report, but disagree whether it happened in law: Abu al-Maʿali and others say the Quba mosque case is an instance; others deny it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r2.anchor: والحذاق على تجويز نسخ القرآن بخبر الواحد عقلا، واختلفوا هل وقع شرعا فذهب أبو المعالي وغيره إلى وقوعه في نازلة مسجد قباء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r3.claim: Analogy cannot abrogate a text because a valid analogy must not conflict with a text.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r3.anchor: ولا يصح نسخ نص بقياس إذ من شروط القياس ألا يخالف نصا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r4.claim: Abrogation applies only during the Prophet’s lifetime; after his death and the stabilization of the law, consensus says there is no abrogation, and consensus itself neither abrogates nor is abrogated.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r4.anchor: وهذا كله في مدة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأما بعد موته واستقرار الشريعة فأجمعت الأمة أنه لا نسخ ولهذا كان الإجماع لا ينسخ ولا ينسخ به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r5.claim: If consensus seems to conflict with a text, it must rest on an unknown abrogating text; the conflicting text has ceased to govern, though its recitation and transmission remain as a Sunnah, as with the verse of a year’s waiting period and the alms before private consultation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r5.anchor: فإذا وجدنا إجماعا يخالف نصا فيعلم أن الإجماع استند إلى نص ناسخ لا نعلمه نحن، وأن ذلك النص المخالف متروك العمل به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r6.claim: Recitation can be abrogated while the ruling remains, as with the stoning verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r6.anchor: وقد تنسخ التلاوة دون الحكم كآية الرجم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r7.speaker: أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r7.claim: Abu Bakr said that Muslims had recited “Do not turn away from your fathers, for that is unbelief”; al-Qurtubi cites it as an example where both recitation and ruling were abrogated.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r7.anchor: ومنه قول الصديق رضي الله عنه: كنا نقرأ «لا ترغبوا عن آبائكم فإنه كفر» ومثله كثير.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r8.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r8.claim: The leading jurists hold that someone who has not yet received the abrogating text remains bound by the earlier ruling, as in the later account of the qibla change.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r8.anchor: والذي عليه الحذاق أن من لم يبلغه الناسخ فهو متعبد بالحكم الأول كما يأتي بيانه في تحويل القبلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r9.speaker: حذاق الأئمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r9.claim: The leading jurists allow a ruling to be abrogated before it is carried out; examples are Abraham’s sacrifice test and the fifty prayers being reduced by five before performance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r9.anchor: والحذاق على جواز نسخ الحكم قبل فعله، وهو موجود في قصة الذبيح، وفي فرض خمسين صلاة قبل فعلها بخمس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r10.claim: One way to identify abrogation is explicit wording such as the Prophet’s statement that he first forbade grave-visiting, then permitted it, or that he initially restricted drinking vessels, then allowed them except for intoxicants.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#6/r10.anchor: أن يكون في اللفظ ما يدل عليه كقوله عليه السلام:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r1.speaker: author
