QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r1.claim: Other signs of abrogation are a narrator’s chronology, an explicit statement that one ruling replaced another, or consensus identifying the abrogating ruling; legal theory treats the subject at length.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r1.anchor: ومنها أن يذكر الراوي التاريخ مثل أن يقول: سمعت عام الخندق، وكان المنسوخ معلوما قبله. أو يقول: نسخ حكم كذا بكذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r2.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r2.claim: The majority read ما ننسخ with an open initial nun, from نسخ: removing a verse’s ruling while leaving its recitation, though it can also mean removing both.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r2.anchor: قرأ الجمهور «ما ننسخ» بفتح النون، من نسخ، وهو الظاهر المستعمل على معنى: ما نرفع من حكم آية ونبقي تلاوتها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r3.speaker: ابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads ننسخ with a ḍamma on the initial nun, deriving it from أنسخت, “found it abrogated”; Abu Hatim calls this wrong, while Abu ʿAli says it works only in that “found” sense and converges in meaning with the majority reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر «ننسخ» بضم النون، من أنسخت الكتاب على معنى وجدته منسوخا. قال أبو حاتم: هو غلط.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r4.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r4.claim: Makkī rejects treating the hamza as causative, since “whatever verse We send down or make you forget, We bring a better one” would make the whole Qur’an abrogated, though only a little was abrogated.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r4.anchor: قال مكي: ولا يجوز أن تكون الهمزة للتعدي لأن المعنى يتغير، ويصير المعنى ما ننسخك من آية يا محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r5.claim: Abu ʿAmr and Ibn Kathir read ننسأها with open nun and sin and hamza, also transmitted from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtaʾ, Mujahid, Ubayy, ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, al-Nakhaʿi, and Ibn Muhaysin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r5.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير بفتح النون والسين والهمز، وبه قرأ عمر وابن عباس وعطاء ومجاهد وأبي بن كعب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r6.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r6.claim: ʿAtaʾ understands ننسأها as postponing the abrogation of the verse’s wording, leaving it in the Mother of the Book so it does not cease to be.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r6.anchor: من التأخير أي نؤخر نسخ لفظها، أي نتركه في آخر أم الكتاب فلا يكون. وهذا قول عطاء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r7.claim: Others take ننسأها to mean deferring the verse from abrogation until a known time; the root نسأ means to delay, as in asking God to extend someone’s life.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#7/r7.anchor: وقال غير عطاء: معنى أو ننسأها: نؤخرها عن النسخ إلى وقت معلوم من قولهم: نسأت هذا الأمر إذا أخرته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r1.claim: A further view takes the hamza reading as removing the verse from people’s memory so it is neither read nor recalled; the wording also allows delaying revelation or abrogation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r1.anchor: فالمعنى نؤخر نزولها أو نسخها على ما ذكرنا. وقيل: نذهبها عنكم حتى لا تقرأ ولا تذكر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r2.claim: The majority read ننسها with a ḍamma on the initial nun, from “leave”: God leaves the verse without replacing or abrogating it; Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Suddi give this meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون «ننسها» بضم النون، من النسيان الذي بمعنى الترك، أي نتركها فلا نبدلها ولا ننسخها قاله ابن عباس والسدى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r3.claim: In 9:67, “they forgot God, so He forgot them” means they abandoned worship and God left them in punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r3.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى: نسوا الله فنسيهم [التوبة: 67] أي تركوا عبادته فتركهم في العذاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r4.claim: Abu ʿUbayd and Abu Hatim prefer the reading with ḍamma, ننسها.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r4.anchor: واختار هذه القراءة أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم، قال أبو عبيد: سمعت أبا نعيم القارىء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r5.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayd says Abu Nuʿaym told of reciting Abu ʿAmr’s reading to the Prophet in a dream; the Prophet corrected two letters, and Abu ʿUbayd guessed one was ننسأها corrected to ننسها.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: سمعت أبا نعيم القارىء يقول: قرأت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المنام بقراءة أبي عمرو

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r6.speaker: الأزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r6.claim: Al-Azhari says ننسها can mean “we command you to leave it,” distinguishing أنسيته, “I ordered him to leave it,” from نسيته, “I left it.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r6.anchor: وحكى الأزهري «ننسها» نأمر بتركها يقال: أنسيته الشيء أي أمرت بتركه ونسيته تركته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r7.claim: A poet’s line uses منسيها for one not commanded to be left behind; it supports the causative sense “make someone leave.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r7.anchor: قال الشاعر: إن علي عقبة أقضيها لست بناسيها ولا منسيها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r8.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects the “leave” sense for the ḍamma reading, saying أنسى is not used to mean ترك; he also rejects the attributed Ibn ʿAbbas explanation as unreliable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r8.anchor: وقال الزجاج: إن القراءة بضم النون لا يتوجه فيها معنى الترك لا يقال: أنسى بمعنى ترك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r9.claim: Al-Qurtubi suggests Ibn ʿAbbas may have meant “leave it without replacing it,” but his wording was not carefully preserved; most linguists and scholars accept “make you leave it.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r9.anchor: ولعل ابن عباس قال: نتركها فلم يضبط. والذي عليه أكثر أهل اللغة والنظر أن معنى «أو ننسها»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r10.speaker: أبو علي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r10.claim: Abu ʿAli and others consider the causative interpretation sound: God makes the Prophet leave the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r10.anchor: وقال أبو علي وغيره: ذلك متجه لأنه بمعنى نجعلك تتركها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes forgetting literally: God makes Muhammad forget the verse; hamza makes the verb take two objects, with the Prophet omitted and the verse explicit.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r11.anchor: وقيل: من النسيان على بابه الذي هو عدم الذكر، على معنى أو ننسكها يا محمد فلا تذكرها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r12.claim: خير is comparative in benefit: a lighter replacement benefits people sooner in this life, a heavier one in the afterlife, and an equal one as much as its predecessor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r12.anchor: لفظة «بخير» هنا صفة تفضيل والمعنى بأنفع لكم أيها الناس في عاجل إن كانت الناسخة أخف، وفي آجل إن كانت أثقل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r13.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r13.claim: Malik explains خير منها as “more firmly established in place of what was abrogated.”

QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r14.claim: Another view says خير is not comparative, since God’s speech does not vary in excellence; as in 27:89, it means a benefit or reward, while “or like it” supports the first interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:106#8/r14.anchor: وقيل: ليس المراد بأخير التفضيل لأن كلام الله لا يتفاضل، وإنما هو مثل قوله: من جاء بالحسنة فله خير منها

QASHANI:2:106-107/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:106-107/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:106-107/r1.claim: Abrogation can cancel a ruling while retaining wording and meaning, or retain wording without meaning, as with the stoning verse.
QASHANI:2:106-107/r1.anchor: بإبطال حكمها وإبقاء لفظها ومعناها، أو لفظها دون معناها، كآية الرجم

QASHANI:2:106-107/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:106-107/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:106-107/r2.claim: A replacement is better when more fitting in its domain, or equal in goodness and benefit.
QASHANI:2:106-107/r2.anchor: بما هو أصلح في بابه منها في بابها أو يساويها في الخير والصلاح

QASHANI:2:106-107/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:106-107/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:106-107/r3.claim: Preserved-Tablet rulings may be specific to persons, lasting while they live, or periods, ending with their era; short periods include abrogated Quran rulings and long ones earlier dispensations. The Tablet records this condition; general rulings endure.
QASHANI:2:106-107/r3.anchor: الأحكام المثبتة في اللوح المحفوظ إما مخصوصة وإما عامة،

RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r1.claim: The verse was revealed after Jews objected that Muhammad ordered his companions to do something, then forbade it and commanded its opposite.
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r1.anchor: فقالوا : ألا ترون إلى محمد يأمر أصحابه بأمر ثم ينهاهم عنه ويأمرهم بخلافه ،

RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r2.claim: Razi takes the basic lexical sense of naskh to be cancellation or removal, rather than transfer.
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r2.anchor: النسخ في أصل اللغة بمعنى إبطال الشيء

RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r3.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r3.claim: Al-Qaffal instead says naskh means transfer and transformation.

RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r4.claim: Arabic says wind erases traces and sun erases shade; 22:52 likewise uses naskh for God’s removal of what Satan casts, supporting removal as the literal sense.
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r4.anchor: لنا أنه يقال : نسخت الريح آثار القوم إذا عدمت ، ونسخت الشمس الظل إذا عدم

RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r5.speaker: معترض
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r5.claim: An objector calls the wind and sun examples metaphorical, since God, not those things, is the true remover.
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r5.anchor: فإن قيل : وصفهم الريح بأنها ناسخة للآثار ، والشمس بأنها ناسخة للظل مجاز

RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r6.claim: Razi replies that God acts through the effective wind and sun, which can also be called agents of removal because of their particular effect.
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r6.anchor: أحدهما : أنه لا يمتنع أن يكون الله هو الناسخ لذلك من حيث إنه فعل الشمس والريح المؤثرتين

RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, even if Arabic speakers mistakenly ascribed removal to wind and sun, their use still attests to the word’s use for removal.
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r7.anchor: والثاني : أن أهل اللغة إنما أخطأوا في إضافة النسخ إلى الشمس والريح

RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r8.speaker: معترض
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r8.claim: The opposing lexical case says naskh is transfer, as in copying a book, transmigration, successive generations, inheritance passing between heirs, and recording deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r8.anchor: بل النسخ هو النقل والتحويل ومنه نسخ الكتاب إلى كتاب آخر كأنه ينقله إليه أو ينقل حكايته

RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r9.claim: Transfer is narrower than cancellation because it entails removing one quality and replacing it; general nonexistence is broader, so the broader sense is likelier to be literal.
RAZI-FULL:v3p204#3/r9.anchor: وعن الثاني : أن النقل أخص من الإبطال لأنه حيث وجد النقل فقد عدمت صفة وحصل عقيبها صفة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAmir reads nansakh with a damma on the nūn and kasra on the sīn; the other readers use fatḥa on both.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر : ( ما ننسخ ) بضم النون وكسر السين والباقون بفتحهما

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r2.claim: Two explanations are offered for Ibn ʿAmir’s form: nasakha and ansakha are synonymous, or ansakha means to make something subject to naskh.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون نسخ وأنسخ بمعنى واحد . والثاني : أنسخته جعتله ذا نسخ

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r3.claim: The second explanation is illustrated by aqbirū fulānan, ‘give him a grave’; the Qur’an says God made Jesus’s mother’s child buried.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r3.anchor: أقبروا فلانا ، أي اجعلوه ذا قبر ، قال تعالى : { ثم أماته فأقبره }

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read nansaʾhā with an initial fatḥa and hamza, a jussive conditional form from the root of postponement.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو : ( ننسأها ) بفتح النون والهمزة وهو جزم بالشرط

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r5.claim: Abu ʿAmr retains the hamza because its sukūn marks the jussive; the root means delay, as in al-nasīʾ and deferred sale, and linguists use it for extending a term.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r5.anchor: ولا يدع أبو عمرو الهمزة في مثل هذا ، لأن سكونها علامة للجزم وهو من النسء وهو التأخير

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r6.claim: A prophetic report says that whoever wishes a longer lifespan and increased provision should maintain kinship ties.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r6.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( من سره النسء في الأجل والزيادة في الرزق فليصل رحمه )

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r7.claim: The remaining readers pronounce nunsihā with a damma on nūn and kasra on sīn, deriving it from forgetting.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r7.anchor: والباقون بضم النون وكسر السين وهو من النسيان

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r8.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r8.claim: Most interpreters take nisyān in its ordinary sense, the opposite of remembering.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r8.anchor: الأكثرون حملوه على النسيان الذي هو ضد الذكر

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r9.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r9.claim: Some interpret nisyān as abandonment, citing Adam’s ‘forgetting’ as leaving the command and God’s leaving people as they left the meeting of the Last Day.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r9.anchor: ومنهم من حمل النسيان على الترك على حد قوله تعالى : { فنسى ولم نجد له عزما }

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r10.claim: Razi prefers ‘abandon’ as a figurative sense: what is forgotten is left behind, so the necessary concomitant is named for the thing that entails it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r10.anchor: والأظهر أن حمل النسيان على الترك مجاز ، لأن المنسي يكون متروكا

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r11.claim: Other reported forms include nunsihā and nunassihā with tashdīd, and tunshihā and tunassihā addressed to the Prophet.

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r12.speaker: عبد الله
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r12.claim: ʿAbd Allah reads: ‘Whatever verse We cause you to forget or abrogate.’
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r12.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله : ما ننسك من آية أو ننسخها

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r13.speaker: حذيفة
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r13.claim: Hudhayfa reads: ‘Whatever verse We abrogate or cause you to forget.’
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r13.anchor: وقرأ حذيفة : ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسكها

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r14.claim: Mā is a conditional particle; nansakh is the condition and naʾti its consequence, and both present-tense verbs are jussive.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r14.anchor: ( ما ) في هذه الآية جزائية كقولك : ما تصنع أصنع وعملها الجزم في الشرط والجزاء

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r15.claim: Technically, abrogation is a revealed legal source indicating that a ruling established by an earlier revealed source ceases after an interval, though otherwise it would have remained.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r15.anchor: طريق شرعي يدل على أن الحكم الذي كان ثابتا بطريق شرعي لا يوجد بعد ذلك مع تراخيه عنه

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r16.claim: A legal source here means a statement from God or His Messenger or an act transmitted from them; consensus, reason, and miracles are not such sources, so they do not abrogate rulings in this technical sense.

RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r17.claim: A ruling’s stated endpoint, condition, or exception is not abrogation because it is not temporally delayed; a later prohibition of the like of a commanded act must count as abrogative for the command not to remain in force.
RAZI-FULL:v3p205/r17.anchor: ولا يلزم تقيد الحكم بغاية أو شرط أو استثناء ، لأن ذلك غير متراخ

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r1.claim: Razi’s position is that abrogation is rationally possible and scripturally established, contrary to Jews who either deny its possibility or accept possibility but deny its scriptural occurrence.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r1.anchor: النسخ عندنا جائز عقلا واقع سمعا خلافا لليهود ، فإن منهم من أنكره عقلا ومنهم من جوزه عقلا

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r2.speaker: بعض المسلمين
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r2.claim: Some Muslims are also reported to deny that abrogation has occurred.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r2.anchor: ويروى عن بعض المسلمين إنكار النسخ

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r3.speaker: جمهور المسلمين
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r3.claim: The Muslim majority argues that Muhammad’s proven prophethood requires accepting that a prior religious law was abrogated.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r3.anchor: واحتج الجمهور من المسلمين على جواز النسخ ووقوعه ، لأن الدلائل دلت على نبوة محمد

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r4.claim: Razi challenges the Jews with the Torah’s report that God permitted Noah and his descendants every animal except blood, while later forbidding many animals to Moses and the Israelites.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r4.anchor: جاء في التوراة أن الله تعالى قال لنوح عليه السلام عند خروجه من الفلك : ( إني جعلت كل دابة مأكلا

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r5.claim: He also cites the early permission for Adam to marry his sister, later forbidden in the law given to Moses.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r5.anchor: كان آدم عليه السلام يزوج الأخت من الأخ وقد حرمه بعد ذلك على موسى عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r6.speaker: منكرو النسخ
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r6.claim: Opponents answer that Moses and Jesus could have commanded their laws only until Muhammad appeared, after which people had a new duty; this would be an expiry, not abrogation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r6.anchor: من الجائز أن يقال : إن موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام أمر الناس بشرعهما إلى زمان ظهور شرع محمد

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r7.speaker: منكرو النسخ
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r7.claim: Muslims denying abrogation likewise point to Torah and Gospel predictions of Muhammad and say the obligation to follow him at his appearance does not prove a prior law was abrogated.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r7.anchor: ثبت في القرآن أن موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام قد بشرا في التوراة والإنجيل بمبعث محمد

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r8.speaker: منكرو النسخ
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r8.claim: They argue that a law’s wording either promises permanence, denies permanence, or says neither; if it promises permanence, its later cessation would make the original statement false and leave no certainty that the current law is permanent.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r8.anchor: إما أن يقال : إنها دالة على دوامها أو لا على دوامها أو ما كان فيها دلالة على الدوام

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r9.claim: Razi rejects pairing a declaration of permanence with a declaration of later abrogation as contradictory, frivolous speech.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r9.anchor: التنصيص على اللفظ الدال على الدوام مع التنصيص على أنه لا يدوم جمع بين كلامين متناقضين

RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r10.claim: If an earlier law was expressly declared abrogable, that qualification should have been transmitted with the law; a major matter would be widely transmitted, and Jews’ and Christians’ united denial shows it was not.
RAZI-FULL:v3p206/r10.anchor: لو أن الله تعالى نص في زمان موسى وعيسى عليهما السلام على أن شرعيهما سيصيران منسوخين لكان ذلك مشهورا

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r1.speaker: منكرو النسخ
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r1.claim: If Moses’s law explicitly indicated a limited duration, opponents say that endpoint should have been universally known; in any case, its expiry would not be abrogation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r1.anchor: وأما القسم الثاني : وهو أن يقال : إن الله تعالى نص على شرع موسى عليه السلام وقرن به ما يدل به على أنه منقطع غير دائم

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r2.speaker: منكرو النسخ
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r2.claim: If the law said neither that it was permanent nor that it was temporary, opponents reason that an ordinary command requires only one performance; a later command therefore does not abrogate it, making abrogation impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r2.anchor: أن مجرد الأمر لا يفيد التكرار وإنما يفيد

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r3.claim: Razi says 2:106 does not prove that abrogation occurred: its conditional wording establishes only that if abrogation occurs, God brings something better or equal.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r3.anchor: فكذا هذه الآية لا تدل على حصول النسخ ، بل على أنه متى حصل النسخ وجب أن يأتي بما هو خير منه

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r4.claim: He instead relies on the verse about replacing one verse with another and the statement that God effaces and confirms what He wills.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وإذا بدلنا ءاية مكان ءاية } ( النحل : 101 ) وقوله : { يمحو الله ما يشاء ويثبت وعنده أم الكتاب }

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r5.speaker: جمهور العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r5.claim: The majority agree that abrogation did occur within the Qur’an; Abu Muslim ibn Bahr denies that it did.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r5.anchor: المسألة السادسة : اتفقوا على وقوع النسخ في القرآن ، وقال أبو مسلم بن بحر : إنه لم يقع

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r6.speaker: جمهور العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r6.claim: The majority first cite this verse for Qur’anic abrogation; Abu Muslim gives three alternative readings of its scope and force.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r6.anchor: واحتج الجمهور على وقوعه في القرآن بوجوه . أحدها : هذه الآية وهي قوله تعالى : { ما ننسخ من ءاية أو ننسها نأت بخير منها أو مثلها }

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r7.claim: Abu Muslim says the abrogated verses are earlier-scripture rules, such as the Sabbath and prayer toward east or west, which God lifted from this community.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r7.anchor: الأول : أن المراد من الآيات المنسوخة هي الشرائع التي في الكتب القديمة من التوراة والإنجيل ، كالسبت والصلاة إلى المشرق والمغرب

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r8.claim: His second reading takes naskh as copying the text from the Preserved Tablet into other books, as in copying a book.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r8.anchor: الوجه الثاني : المراد من النسخ نقله من اللوح المحفوظ وتحويله عنه إلى سائر الكتب

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r9.claim: His third reading is that the conditional verse says only what would follow if abrogation occurred, not that it actually occurred.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r9.anchor: الوجه الثالث : أنا بينا أن هذه الآية لا تدل على وقوع النسخ ، بل على أنه لو وقع النسخ لوقع إلى خير منه

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r10.claim: A response to Abu Muslim says that an unqualified ‘verse’ ordinarily means a Qur’anic verse familiar to the Muslim audience.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r10.anchor: ومن الناس من أجاب عن الاعتراض الأول بأن الآيات إذا أطلقت فالمراد بها آيات القرآن لأنه هو المعهود عندنا

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r11.claim: Another reply says copying the Qur’an from the Preserved Tablet would concern all of it, whereas the verse’s abrogation concerns only some; a critic can object that ‘verse’ need not mean Qur’an alone.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r11.anchor: وعن الثاني : بأن نقل القرآن من اللوح المحفوظ لا يختص ببعض القرآن وهذا النسخ مختص ببعضه

RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r12.speaker: معترض
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r12.claim: A critic counters that āya is general for all signs and that the verse may mean transferring from the Preserved Tablet, then bringing something better afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v3p207/r12.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول على الأول : لا نسلم أن لفظ الآية مختص بالقرآن ، بل هو عام في جميع الدلائل

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r1.speaker: جمهور العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r1.claim: The majority cite the year-long widow’s waiting period, 2:240, as abrogated by the four months and ten days in 2:234.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r1.anchor: الحجة الثانية للقائلين بوقوع النسخ في القرآن : أن الله تعالى أمر المتوفى عنها زوجها بالاعتداد حولا كاملا وذلك في قوله :

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r2.claim: Abu Muslim says the year-long period remains for a pregnant widow whose pregnancy lasts a full year, so the later period merely specifies rather than abrogates the earlier rule.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r2.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : الاعتداد بالحول ما زال بالكلية لأنها لو كانت حاملا ومدة حملها حول كامل لكانت عدتها حولا كاملا

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r3.claim: Razi answers that a pregnant widow’s waiting period ends with childbirth, whether pregnancy lasts one year, less, or more; thus the annual term was wholly removed.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r3.anchor: والجواب : أن مدة عدة الحمل تنقضي بوضع الحمل سواء حصل وضع الحمل بسنة أو أقل أو أكثر

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r4.claim: A second proof is the command to give charity before private consultation with the Messenger, later removed.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r4.anchor: الحجة الثالثة : أمر الله بتقديم الصدقة بين يدي نجوى الرسول بقوله تعالى :

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r5.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r5.claim: Abu Muslim argues the consultation charity duty ended when its purpose—distinguishing hypocrites who would not give from believers—had been achieved.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r5.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : إنما زال ذلك لزوال سببه لأن سبب التعبد بها أن يمتاز المنافقون من حيث لا يتصدقون عن المؤمنين

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r6.claim: Razi reports that no one gave the pre-consultation charity except ʿAli.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r6.anchor: أنه روي أنه لم يتصدق غير علي رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r7.claim: If the purpose were simply identifying hypocrites, everyone who failed to give would be a hypocrite, which Razi rejects; 58:13 says God relented when they did not do it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r7.anchor: لو كان كذلك لكان من لم يتصدق منافقا وهو باطل لأنه روي

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r8.claim: A third proof is that the duty for twenty steadfast believers to defeat two hundred was changed to one hundred defeating two hundred.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r8.anchor: الحجة الرابعة : أنه تعالى أمر بثبات الواحد للعشرة بقوله تعالى : { إن يكن منكم عشرون صابرون يغلبوا مائتين }

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r9.claim: Abu Muslim says the earlier qibla was not wholly removed because it could still be used in uncertainty or under an excuse.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r9.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : حكم تلك القبلة ما زال بالكلية لجواز التوجه إليها عند الإشكال أو مع العلم إذا كان هناك عذر

RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r10.claim: Razi replies that on Abu Muslim’s account Jerusalem has no distinction from other directions; its special status was wholly removed, which is abrogation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208/r10.anchor: الجواب : أن على ما ذكرته لا فرق بين بيت المقدس وسائر الجهات ، فالخصوصية التي بها امتاز بيت المقدس عن سائر الجهات قد زالت بالكلية

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r1.claim: A sixth proof is 16:101: replacing one verse with another entails both removal and establishment, and the removed item may be recitation or a ruling.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r1.anchor: الحجة السادسة : قوله تعالى : { وإذا بدلنا ءاية مكان ءاية والله أعلم بما ينزل قالوا إنما أنت مفتر } ( النحل : 101 ) والتبديل يشتمل على رفع وإثبات ، والمرفوع إما التلاوة وإما الحكم

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r2.claim: Abu Muslim argues that since God says the Book is untouched by falsehood from before or behind, abrogation would mean falsehood entered it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r2.anchor: واحتج أبو مسلم بأن الله تعالى وصف كتابه بأنه لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه ، فلو نسخ لكان قد أتاه الباطل

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r3.claim: Razi explains that no falsehood before or after means no earlier divine book invalidates this Book and no later book will invalidate it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r3.anchor: المراد أن هذا الكتاب لم يتقدمه من كتب الله ما يبطله ولا يأتيه من بعده أيضا ما يبطله

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r4.claim: Abrogation may remove the ruling alone, the recitation alone, or both the ruling and recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r4.anchor: المنسوخ إما أن يكون هو الحكم فقط أو التلاوة فقط أو هما معا

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r5.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r5.claim: ʿUmar reports that they used to recite a stoning verse about the old man and old woman; Razi classifies it as recitation removed while the ruling remained.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r5.anchor: فكما يروى عن عمر أنه قال : كنا نقرأ آية الرجم : ( الشيخ والشيخة إذا زنيا فارجموهما ألبتة

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r6.claim: Another report gives a former recitation saying that if Adam’s son had two valleys of wealth he would seek a third, and only dust fills his belly.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r6.anchor: وروي : ( لو كان لابن آدم واديان من مال لابتغى إليهما ثالثا ولا يملأ جوف ابن آدم إلا التراب

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r7.speaker: عائشة
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r7.claim: ʿAisha reports that ten known sucklings were first revealed, then replaced by five; Razi says the ten lost both recitation and ruling, while the five lost recitation but retained the ruling.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r7.anchor: فهو ما روت عائشة رضي الله عنها أن القرآن قد نزل في الرضاع بعشر معلومات ثم نسخن بخمس معلومات

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r8.claim: A report says Sura al-Ahzab was once as long as the seven long suras or longer, then was reduced.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r8.anchor: ويروى أيضا أن سورة الأحزاب كانت بمنزلة السبع الطوال أو أزيد ثم وقع النقصان فيه

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r9.speaker: عطاء وسعيد بن المسيب
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r9.claim: ʿAta and Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab interpret naskh as copying, like copying a book; other interpreters explain it as removal.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r9.anchor: ومنهم من فسره بالنسخ بمعنى نسخت الكتاب وهو قول عطاء وسعيد بن المسيب

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r10.speaker: الحسن والأصم وأكثر المتكلمين
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r10.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Asamm, and most theologians take the verse to mean a publicly recited Qur’anic verse is abrogated in ruling only, while ‘cause it to be forgotten’ removes both ruling and recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r10.anchor: وهو قول الحسن والأصم وأكثر المتكلمين فحملوه على نسخ الحكم دون التلاوة ، وننسها على نسخ الحكم والتلاوة معا

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r11.speaker: معترض
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r11.claim: An objection says forgetting the Qur’an is impossible rationally, since the Qur’an reaches the mass-transmitted community, and scripturally, given God’s promise to preserve it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r11.anchor: فإن قيل : وقوع هذا النسيان ممنوع عقلا وشرعا . أما العقل فلأن القرآن لا بد من إيصاله إلى أهل التواتر

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r12.claim: Razi answers that God may order a verse removed from recitation, prayer, and use as proof; after its legal force ends and time passes it is forgotten, or remembered only like a solitary report.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r12.anchor: أن يأمر الله تعالى بطرحه من القرآن وإخراجه من جملة ما يتلى ويؤتى به في الصلاة أو يحتج به

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r13.claim: A second answer is that such forgetting could be a miracle of the Prophet; a report says they would recite a sura and wake having forgotten it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r13.anchor: ويروى فيه خبر : أنهم كانوا يقرأون السورة فيصبحون وقد نسوها

RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r14.claim: Razi counters the preservation objection with God’s promise that the Prophet will not forget except what God wills, and the command to remember God after forgetting.
RAZI-FULL:v3p208#2/r14.anchor: سنقرئك فلا تنسى * إلا ما شاء الله

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r1.claim: A second interpretation takes nansakh as replacement, whether of ruling, recitation, or both; nunsiha means leaving the verse as it was, without replacement.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r1.anchor: القول الثاني : ما ننسخ من آية أي نبدلها ، إما بأن نبدل حكمها فقط أو تلاوتها فقط أو نبدلهما

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r2.claim: On that reading, nunsiha means leave it unchanged rather than replace it; the verse promises a better or equal replacement for what is changed.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r2.anchor: أما قوله تعالى : { أو ننسها } فالمراد نتركها كما كانت فلا نبدلها ، وقد بينا أن النسيان بمعنى الترك قد جاء

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r3.claim: A third reading takes nansakh as raising a verse after revelation; with the hamza reading it means delaying revelation from the Preserved Tablet, or postponing its abrogation while revealing a replacement that serves the same interest.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r3.anchor: القول الثالث : ما ننسخ من آية ، أي ما نرفعها بعد إنزالها أو ننسأها على قراءة الهمزة أي نؤخر إنزالها من اللوح المحفوظ

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r4.claim: A fourth reading identifies nansakh with a verse whose ruling and recitation are both abrogated, and nunsiha with one whose ruling is abrogated but whose recitation remains.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r4.anchor: القول الرابع : ما ننسخ من آية ، وهي الآية التي صارت منسوخة في الحكم والتلاوة معا ، أو ننسها ، أي نتركها

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r5.claim: For the reading that takes naskh as transfer from the Preserved Tablet or postponement, nunsiha means leaving a verse un-abrogated.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r5.anchor: وأما قراءة ( ننسها ) فالمعنى نتركها يعني نترك نسخها فلا ننسخها

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r6.speaker: جميع المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r6.claim: All exegetes but Abu Muslim take ‘verse’ here to mean a Qur’anic verse; Abu Muslim takes it to refer to the Torah and Gospel.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r6.anchor: فكل المفسرين حملوه على الآية من القرآن غير أبي مسلم فإنه حمل ذلك على التوراة والإنجيل

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r7.claim: Two explanations of ‘better’ are reported: easier, or more beneficial and fitting (aṣlaḥ).
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r7.anchor: فيه قولان . أحدهما : أنه الأخف ، والثاني : أنه الأصلح

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r8.claim: Razi prefers ‘more beneficial’: God directs accountable people toward their interests, not merely toward what feels lighter to them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r8.anchor: والثاني : أنه الأصلح ، وهذا أولى لأنه تعالى يصرف المكلف على مصالحه لا على ما هو أخف على طباعه

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r9.speaker: معترض
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r9.claim: An objection asks how the later rule can be more beneficial if that would make the earlier rule deficient in benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r9.anchor: فإن قيل : لو كان الثاني أصلح من الأول لكان الأول ناقص الصلاح فكيف أمر الله به ؟

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r10.claim: Razi answers that each rule is more beneficial for its own time: the first for the earlier period and the second for the later one.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r10.anchor: قلنا : الأول أصلح من الثاني بالنسبة إلى الوقت الأول ، والثاني بالعكس منه فزال السؤال

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r11.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r11.claim: Some jurists say abrogation must always supply a replacement, citing the verse’s promise of something better or equal.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r11.anchor: المسألة الأولى : قال قوم : لا يجوز نسخ الحكم إلا إلى بدل ، واحتجوا بأن هذه الآية تدل

RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r12.claim: Razi replies that removing the duty may itself be better than keeping it at that time; the consultation-charity duty was removed without a replacement.
RAZI-FULL:v3p209/r12.anchor: خير من ثبوته في ذلك الوقت

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r1.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r1.claim: Some say a rule cannot be abrogated to one that is more burdensome, since ‘better or equal’ excludes something harder.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r1.anchor: المسألة الثانية : قال قوم : لا يجوز نسخ الشيء إلى ما هو أثقل منه واحتجوا بأن قوله : { نأت بخير منها أو مثلها } ينافي كونه أثقل

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r2.claim: Razi answers that ‘better’ may mean greater reward in the afterlife, which a more burdensome duty can bring.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r2.anchor: والجواب : لم لا يجوز أن يكون المراد بالخير ما يكون أكثر ثوابا في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r3.claim: He lists heavier replacements: confinement for adulterers replaced by flogging and stoning, the ʿAshura fast by Ramadan, and two rakʿas in prayer by four while resident, according to some.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r3.anchor: ثم إن الذي يدل على وقوعه أن الله سبحانه نسخ في حق الزناة الحبس في البيوت إلى الجلد والرجم

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r4.claim: Examples of lighter replacements are the widow’s year-long waiting period reduced to four months and ten days and night prayer changed to an option.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r4.anchor: وكنسخ صلاة الليل إلى التخيير فيها

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r5.claim: The change from Jerusalem to the Kaaba is an example of replacing a rule with an equal one.

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r6.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r6.claim: Al-Shafiʿi holds that the Qur’an cannot be abrogated by a mass-transmitted Sunna, and derives four arguments from this verse.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r6.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : الكتاب لا ينسخ بالسنة المتواترة واستدل عليه بهذه الآية من وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r7.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r7.claim: First, ‘better than it’ implies a replacement of the same kind, as one would replace a reward with a better garment; the Qur’an is replaced by Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r7.anchor: أحدها : أنه تعالى أخبر أن ما ينسخه من الآيات يأت بخير منها وذلك يفيد أنه يأتي بما هو من جنسه

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r8.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r8.claim: Second, the wording attributes the bringing of the replacement to God alone, so it means Qur’an, God’s speech, rather than the Sunna brought by the Messenger.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r8.anchor: وثانيها : أن قوله تعالى : { نأتى * بخير منها } يفيد

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r9.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r9.claim: Third, the replacement must be better than the verse, whereas the Sunna cannot be better than the Qur’an.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r9.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : الكتاب لا ينسخ بالسنة المتواترة

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r10.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r10.claim: Fourth, the closing statement that God can do all things shows that God alone brings this good; the Qur’an is His speech, unlike the Messenger’s Sunna.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r10.anchor: ورابعها : أنه قال : { ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير } دل على أن الآتي بذلك الخير هو المختص بالقدرة

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r11.claim: Razi rejects all four arguments: the verse does not say the good brought is itself the abrogating rule; it may be a distinct thing that comes after abrogation, avoiding a circular sequence.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r11.anchor: والجواب عن الوجوه الأربعة بأسرها : أن قوله تعالى : { نأت بخير منها } ليس فيه أن ذلك الخير يجب أن يكون ناسخا

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r12.speaker: جمهور العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r12.claim: The majority also argue that Qur’anic rulings were abrogated by Sunna: the bequest-to-relatives verse by ‘no bequest for an heir,’ and the flogging verse by the stoning report.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r12.anchor: ثم احتج الجمهور على وقوع نسخ الكتاب بالسنة لأن آية الوصية للأقربين منسوخة بقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( ألا لا وصية لوارث )

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r13.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r13.claim: Al-Shafiʿi rejects the bequest example: an heir’s inheritance right itself prevents diverting that share to a bequest, so the inheritance rule already blocks it.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r13.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : أما الأول : فضعيف لأن كون الميراث حقا للوارث يمنع من صرفه إلى الوصية

RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r14.speaker: عمر
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r14.claim: ʿUmar reports that the stoning wording about the old man and old woman was itself Qur’an, so it may have abrogated the flogging rule as Qur’an rather than Sunna.
RAZI-FULL:v3p210/r14.anchor: لأن عمر رضي الله عنه روى أن قوله : ( الشيخ والشيخة إذا زنيا فارجموهما ألبتة ) كان قرآنا

RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r1.claim: God's power lets Him direct the morally responsible under His will, judgment, and wisdom; none can repel or prevent what He chooses.
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r1.anchor: ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير

RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r2.claim: The Mu'tazila argue that if God's speech were eternal, abrogating and abrogated passages would both be eternal, although abrogation requires succession and the abrogated passage to cease.
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r2.anchor: استدلت المعتزلة بهذه الآية على أن القرآن مخلوق

RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r3.claim: The Mu'tazila infer createdness because the verse describes some Qur'anic passages as better than others, whereas what is differentiated this way is not eternal.
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r3.anchor: أن الآية دلت على أن بعض القرآن خير من بعض

RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r4.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r4.claim: The Mu'tazila argue that God replaces abrogated passages through an act within His power, and any such act is originated.
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r4.anchor: أن المراد أنه تعالى هو القادر على نسخ بعضها

RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r5.speaker: الأصحاب
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r5.claim: Razi's side replies that abrogation belongs to words, expressions, and languages; it does not show that the actual meaning conveyed by them is originated.
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r5.anchor: بأن كونه ناسخا ومنسوخا إنما هو من عوارض الألفاظ

RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r6.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r6.claim: The Mu'tazila answer that divine speech's first relation to a passage ceases and a later relation begins; since eternal things cannot cease, both relations are originated, and speech cannot be apart from them.
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r6.anchor: ذلك المعنى الذي هو مدلول العبارات واللغات لا شك أن تعلقه الأول قد زال

RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r7.speaker: الأصحاب
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r7.claim: Razi's side counters by analogy with God's power and knowledge: their earlier relation to a future world must cease when it exists, or else imply impossible power over an existing world or ignorance; the same answer applies to speech.
RAZI-FULL:v3p211/r7.anchor: أن قدرة الله كانت في الأزل متعلقة بإيجاد العالم

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r1.claim: Naskh can mean conveying or copying from an original; this could make the Quran a copy of its Preserved Tablet origin, or simply a written copy of a text.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r1.anchor: Naskh, usually translated “abrogation,” has the meaning of conveyance or copying from an original, which could extend to the notion that the entire Quran is a naskh, or “copy” in relation to its origin in the Preserved Tablet

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r2.claim: The contextual sense of naskh is erasing or obliterating, compared to the sun erasing shadow, wind erasing dust, or age erasing youth.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r2.anchor: The more relevant sense in this context is “to erase” or “to obliterate,” often described as the action that the sun performs on a shadow, the wind upon dust, or even old age upon youth.

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r3.claim: The root n-s-kh also appears for Moses’ tablets’ inscription, God effacing Satan’s work, and recording human deeds.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r3.anchor: The root n-s-kh appears four times in the Quran: in this verse; in 7:154, referring to the inscription of the tablets of Moses; in 22:52, where God effaces the work of Satan; and in 45:29

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r4.claim: Technical naskh is a major concept in Islamic law, theology, and Quran commentary for understanding the relationship among commands and prohibitions in the Quran and Sunnah and their use in law and practice.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r4.anchor: Naskh (“abrogation”) as a technical term is a key concept in the fully developed form of Islamic jurisprudence, theology, and Quranic commentary

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r5.claim: The mainstream definition is replacing an earlier legal ruling with one revealed later; the original text remains in the Quran but is no longer legally binding.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r5.anchor: the replacement of one legal ruling (ḥukm

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r6.claim: In Islamic legal sciences, abrogation concerns commands and prohibitions, not descriptive matters of metaphysics, ethics, history, God’s nature, or the Hereafter; a ruling determines legal status rather than doctrine.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r6.anchor: As widely understood in the Islamic religious sciences, naskh can occur only in matters of commands and prohibitions, not in descriptive passages relating to metaphysics, ethics, history, the nature of God, or the Hereafter

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r7.claim: Abrogation cannot apply to doctrines such as God’s power or the faithful’s reward, nor to accounts of earlier prophets.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r7.anchor: Thus there can be no abrogation of a passage such as God has power over all things

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r8.claim: The prohibitions of murder, theft, and adultery and the command to treat parents kindly are universal and cannot be abrogated.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r8.anchor: Naskh would not apply to commandments so universal as to be irrevocable

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r9.speaker: ʿĀʾishah
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r9.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet’s wife ʿĀʾishah says Quranic commands about suckling were neither acted upon nor retained in the Quran, an example of abrogating both text and ruling.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r9.anchor: A report attributed to the Prophet’s wife ʿĀʾishah, for example, states that there were commands in the Quran relating to suckling that are now neither acted upon nor part of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r10.speaker: ʿUmar
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r10.claim: A report attributed to ʿUmar says a Quranic stoning command is no longer in the text, though the ruling continues; this is the usual example of abrogating text while retaining its ruling.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r10.anchor: In a report attributed toʿUmar, a verse commanding stoning was part of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r11.speaker: many jurists (IK, R, Ṭ)
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r11.claim: Many, perhaps most, jurists hold that stoning for adultery remains in force despite the verse’s absence from the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r11.anchor: according to many, if not most, jurists; IK, R, Ṭ

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r12.claim: There is general agreement that a later Quranic ruling can abrogate an earlier Quranic ruling, but scholars differ on whether Sunnah can abrogate Quran or vice versa, and whether scholarly consensus can abrogate Quran or hadith.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r12.anchor: Although it is generally agreed that one Quranic ruling may abrogate another Quranic ruling revealed earlier in time, there has been considerable difference of opinion about other kinds of naskh

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r13.claim: Scholars have proposed widely varying counts of abrogated verses: Shah Walī Allāh named five, Ibn al-Jawzī 247, and al-Suyūṭī 21.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r13.anchor: placed the number of abrogated verses at 5

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r14.speaker: Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r14.claim: A minority view, represented by Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī, denies technical abrogation and says apparent conflicts can be reconciled.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r14.anchor: A minority of scholars, such as Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī (d. 934/1527), have gone so far as to say that abrogation, as a technical concept defined by the mainstream legal tradition, does not actually exist

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r15.claim: Naskh must be distinguished from specification, cumulative law, and a ruling’s lost circumstances or effective cause; it matters practically only when legal rulings cannot be reconciled.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r15.anchor: Even among the mainstream upholders of naskh, abrogation must be distinguished from (1) specification, where a verse does not contradict but provides specification regarding the general ruling of another verse

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r16.speaker: Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r16.claim: Abū Muslim’s minority alternatives are that naskh occurs between religions, with Islam replacing Judaism and Christianity, or that āyah here means miracle.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r16.anchor: A small minority of scholars, such as Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r17.speaker: Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r17.claim: On the minority miracle reading, āyah may mean a sign such as the Thamūd she-camel, night and day, the Cave Companions, Zachariah’s silence, Jesus, Moses’ hand, Mary and Jesus, destroyed peoples, miracles, creation, or natural signs.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r17.anchor: A small minority of scholars, such as Abū Muslim al-Iṣfahānī

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r18.claim: Nunsīhā can mean abandon or forsake, as in 9:67; God’s forgetting there does not mean failing to remember.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r18.anchor: can also be understood in the sense of“abandoning,” as in

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r19.claim: With different voweling, nansaʾahā means defer or delay, describing signs or verses abrogated and those left unchanged.

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r20.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r20.claim: Ibn Kathīr and others transmit that two men forgot a surah the Prophet had taught them; he called it abrogated and forgotten, supporting the forgetting reading. No grading is stated.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r20.anchor: Ibn Kathīr and others mention aḥadīth about two men who used to recite a sūrah

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r21.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r21.claim: Some commentators say the replacement is easier in worldly matters but more demanding in matters of the next world: easing the night prayer, but imposing Ramadan fasting for greater reward.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r21.anchor: some interpret better than it as an alleviation when it comes to matters of this world and an intensification when it comes to matters of the next world (Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r22.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r22.claim: Some commentators supply an implied ruling: it is the ruling, not the sign itself, that is better; al-Ṭabarī compares this ellipsis to the omitted love of the calf in 2:93.
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r22.anchor: Thus, for some commentators the verse must mean “No [ruling from a] sign do We abrogate . . . ,” so that it is the ruling, not the sign, that is called “better.” Al-Ṭabarī, for example, compares this implied phrase

STUDYQURAN:2:106/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r23.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:2:106/r23.claim: Because khayr can mean a good, another interpretation takes the phrase as a good from or on account of the sign.

TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r1.claim: Naskh transfers a ruling to its contrary, changing lawful to forbidden, forbidden to lawful, permitted to prohibited, or prohibited to permitted; it applies to commands and rulings, not reports.
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r1.anchor: إذا نسخ حكمها فغير وبدل فرضها ونقل فرض العباد

TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r2.claim: The root sense of naskh is copying a book from one copy into another; in legal usage it is transferring and changing a ruling.
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r2.anchor: وهو نقله من نسخة إلى أخرى غيرها

TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r3.claim: A ruling counts as abrogated whether its wording remains while the ruling changes or its trace is erased; the new ruling transferred to the worshippers is the nāsikh.
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r3.anchor: فعفي ونسي، إذ هي حينئذ في كلتا حالتيها منسوخة. والحكم الحادث المبدل به الحكم الأول والمنقول إليه فرض العباد هو الناسخ

TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet was taught Qur'an and then forgot some of it until it was no longer retained, while some abrogated Qur'an remains recited.
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r4.anchor: عن الحسن، أنه قال: " في قوله: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها نأت بخير منها} [البقرة: 106] قال: إن نبيكم

TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddi interprets abrogating a verse as taking it away.
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r5.anchor: عن السدي: " {ما ننسخ من آية} [البقرة: 106] أما نسخها فقبضها

TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets abrogation as replacing a verse.
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " قوله: {ما ننسخ من آية} [البقرة: 106] يقول: ما نبدل من آية

TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r7.speaker: أصحاب عبد الله بن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r7.claim: The Companions of Ibn Masud say the wording remains while its ruling is changed.
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r7.anchor: عن أصحاب عبد الله بن مسعود، أنهم قالوا: " {ما ننسخ من آية} [البقرة: 106] نثبت خطها ونبدل حكمها

TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد عن أصحاب ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r8.claim: Mujahid transmits from Ibn Masud's Companions that the verse's written wording is retained.
TAB-FULL:v2p388#2/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن أصحاب ابن مسعود: " {ما ننسخ من آية} [البقرة: 106] نثبت خطها

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r1.claim: Al-Tabari reports the Medina and Kufa reading and says the form has two possible interpretations.
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r1.anchor: وبهذا التأويل قال جماعة من أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r2.speaker: جماعة من أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r2.claim: A group of exegetes takes the phrase to mean that God causes the Prophet to forget a verse after changing its ruling.
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r2.anchor: وبهذا التأويل قال جماعة من أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r3.claim: Ibn Abd Allah's codex reads the phrase as 'what We cause you to forget' and adds 'We bring its like,' supporting this sense of forgetting.

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r4.claim: Qatada says one verse could be abrogated by the next, and a verse or more that the Prophet recited could then be forgotten and withdrawn.
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r4.anchor: عن قتادة: " قوله: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها نأت بخير منها أو مثلها} [البقرة: 106] كان ينسخ الآية بالآية بعدها

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r5.claim: Qatada says God makes His Prophet forget whatever He wills and abrogates whatever He wills.
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قوله: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} [البقرة: 106] قال: كان الله تعالى ذكره ينسي نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r6.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r6.claim: Ubayd ibn Umayr interprets nunsiha as raising the verse from people's possession.
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: كان عبيد بن عمير يقول: " {ننسها} [البقرة: 106] نرفعها من عندكم

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r7.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet was taught Qur'an and then forgot it.

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r8.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r8.claim: Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas reads the phrase as aw tansa-hā, addressing the Prophet: 'or you forget it.'
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r8.anchor: سعد بن أبي وقاص يتأول الآية إلا أنه كان يقرؤها : {أو تنسها} بمعنى الخطاب لرسول الله

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r9.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r9.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib is reported to read aw tansa-hā, addressing the Prophet.
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r9.anchor: فإن سعيد بن المسيب يقرؤها: «أو تنسها» قال: فقال سعد

TAB-FULL:v2p391/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r10.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r10.claim: Saʿd rejects that reading as unauthorized, saying the Qur'an was not revealed to al-Musayyib or his family; he cites 87:6 and 18:24.
TAB-FULL:v2p391/r10.anchor: قال سعد: إن القرآن لم ينزل على المسيب ولا على آل المسيب، قال الله: {سنقرئك فلا تنسى} {واذكر ربك إذا نسيت} [الكهف: 24]

TAB-FULL:v2p393/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p393/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
TAB-FULL:v2p393/r1.claim: Saʿd rejected Ibn al-Musayyib’s reading and said the wording was addressed to Muhammad as تنسها.
TAB-FULL:v2p393/r1.anchor: قلت لسعد بن أبي وقاص: إني سمعت ابن المسيب، يقرأ: «ما ننسخ من آية أو تنسها» فقال سعد

TAB-FULL:v2p393/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p393/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v2p393/r2.claim: Al-Rabiʿ explains ننسها as raising or removing a verse; God had revealed Quranic matters and then lifted them.
TAB-FULL:v2p393/r2.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع: " في قوله: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} [البقرة: 106] يقول: ننسها: نرفعها

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r1.claim: Al-Tabari rejects تنسها as a shadh reading outside the authoritative readings transmitted by the community.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r1.anchor: وكذلك قراءة من قرأ «تنسها» (أو تنسها) لشذوذها وخروجها عن القراءة التي جاءت بها الحجة

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r2.claim: He prefers ننسها as “leave it,” since it coherently contrasts changing an abrogated ruling with leaving another unchanged.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r2.anchor: وأولى القراءات في قوله: {أو ننسها} [البقرة: 106] بالصواب من قرأ: {أو ننسها} [البقرة: 106] بمعنى نتركها

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r3.claim: The sequence naturally says that after God describes abrogating a verse, He describes leaving another unaltered; a left verse is also deferred.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r3.anchor: فالخبر الذي يجب أن يكون عقيب قوله: {ما ننسخ من آية} [البقرة: 106] قوله: أو نترك نسخها

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r4.claim: The preferred reading includes both leaving and delaying, since anything left remains deferred.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r4.anchor: فهو يشتمل على معنى الإنساء الذي هو بمعنى الترك، ومعنى النساء الذي هو بمعنى التأخير

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r5.speaker: قوم
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r5.claim: Some reject saying Muhammad forgot Quran that was not abrogated, allowing only forgetting followed by recollection.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r5.anchor: وقد أنكر قوم قراءة من قرأ: «أو تنسها» إذا عني به النسيان، وقالوا: غير جائز أن يكون رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r6.speaker: قوم
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r6.claim: They also argue that if Muhammad forgot a passage, all his companions could not have forgotten it too.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r6.anchor: فإنه لو نسي منه شيئا لم يكن الذين قرءوه وحفظوه من أصحابه بجائز على جميعهم أن ينسوه

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r7.speaker: قوم
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r7.claim: The objectors cite 17:86 as indicating that God did not make His Prophet forget any knowledge He had given him.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r7.anchor: وفي قول الله جل ثناؤه: {ولئن شئنا لنذهبن بالذي أوحينا إليك} [الإسراء: 86] ما ينبئ عن أن الله تعالى ذكره

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r8.claim: Anas reports that the seventy Ansar killed at Biʾr Maʿuna recited a passage that was later lifted from the Quran.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r8.anchor: أنس بن مالك: " أن أولئك السبعين من الأنصار الذين قتلوا ببئر معونة قرأنا بهم وفيهم كتابا

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r9.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r9.claim: Al-Tabari also cites Abu Musa’s report that a saying about Adam’s son having two valleys of wealth was recited and then lifted.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r9.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري أنهم كانوا يقرءون: «لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مال لابتغى لهما ثالثا

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r10.claim: It is neither rationally nor textually impossible for God to cause His Prophet to forget some revelation He had sent down.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r10.anchor: غير مستحيل في فطرة ذي عقل صحيح ولا بحجة خبر أن ينسي الله نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بعض ما قد كان أنزله

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r11.claim: 17:86 says God could remove all revelation if He willed, not that He never removed any; He removed what was no longer needed, namely abrogated material.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r11.anchor: فإنه جل ثناؤه لم يخبر أنه لا يذهب بشيء منه، وإنما أخبر أنه لو شاء لذهب بجميعه

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r12.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r12.claim: Al-Tabari connects the exception in 87:6 to God making the Prophet forget what He willed.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r12.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى ذكره: {سنقرئك فلا تنسى إلا ما شاء الله} فأخبر أنه ينسي نبيه منه ما شاء

TAB-FULL:v2p397/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r13.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r13.claim: His preference for “leave it” rests on coherence, not on denying that God made His Prophet forget some abrogated revelation.
TAB-FULL:v2p397/r13.anchor: طلب اتساق الكلام على نظام في المعنى، لا إنكار أن يكون الله تعالى ذكره قد كان أنسى نبيه بعض ما نسخ

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains “better” as more beneficial and gentler for the believers.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {نأت بخير منها أو مثلها} [البقرة: 106] يقول: خير لكم في المنفعة وأرفق بكم

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r2.claim: Qatada says the replacement verse contains relief, mercy, a command, or a prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: " في قوله: {نأت بخير منها أو مثلها} [البقرة: 106] يقول: آية فيها تخفيف، فيها رحمة، فيها أمر، فيها نهي

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r3.claim: Another view takes “better than it” as better than the verse abrogated or the verse left without abrogation.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: نأت بخير من التي نسخناها، أو بخير من التي تركناها فلم ننسخها

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r4.claim: منها refers to the verse in ما ننسخ من آية, while مثلها refers back to the verse in أو ننسها.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r4.anchor: فالهاء والألف اللتان في قوله: {منها} [البقرة: 106] عائدتان على هذه المقالة على الآية

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r5.claim: Mujahid transmits Ubayd ibn Umayr’s view that ننسها means raising a verse from the people, then bringing a similar or better one.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: كان عبيد بن عمير يقول: " {ننسها} [البقرة: 106] نرفعها من عندكم، نأت بمثلها أو خير منها

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r6.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r6.claim: Al-Rabiʿ likewise glosses ننسها as raising the verse and replacing it with something better or similar.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r6.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع: " {أو ننسها} [البقرة: 106] نرفعها نأت بخير منها أو بمثلها

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r7.claim: Mujahid reports the same interpretation from the followers of Ibn Masʿud.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد، عن أصحاب ابن مسعود، مثله

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r8.claim: A replacement is better either in this life because it is lighter, or in the afterlife because its greater burden earns greater reward.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r8.anchor: إما في العاجل لخفته عليكم، من أجل أنه وضع فرض كان عليكم فأسقط ثقله عنكم

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r9.claim: The annual fast of a full month was heavier than a few prescribed days but better in the afterlife through greater reward.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r9.anchor: فكان فرض صوم شهر كامل كل سنة أثقل على الأبدان من صيام أيام معدودات

TAB-FULL:v2p399/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r10.claim: Similar means equal bodily burden and reward, as when prayer direction changed from Jerusalem to the Kaaba without changing the effort of facing it.
TAB-FULL:v2p399/r10.anchor: نظير نسخ الله تعالى ذكره فرض الصلاة شطر بيت المقدس إلى فرضها شطر المسجد الحرام

TAB-FULL:v2p402/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r1.claim: The qibla change illustrates equal burden: facing either sanctuary required the same effort, which is the sense of “similar.”
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r1.anchor: شطره واحدة؛ لأن الذي على المتوجه شطر البيت المقدس من مؤنة توجهه شطره، نظير الذي على بدنه مؤنة توجهه شطر الكعبة سواء

TAB-FULL:v2p402/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r2.claim: “Verse” stands for the ruling of a verse, an understood ellipsis, as in 2:93 where drinking the calf means taking its love into the heart.
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r2.anchor: كقوله: {وأشربوا في قلوبهم العجل} [البقرة: 93] بمعنى حب العجل ونحو ذلك

TAB-FULL:v2p402/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r3.claim: The verse means that God changes or leaves unchanged a ruling and brings believers a ruling better or equal in lightness, burden, reward, and recompense.
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r3.anchor: فتأويل الآية إذا: ما نغير من حكم آية فنبدله أو نتركه فلا نبدله، نأت بخير لكم أيها المؤمنون حكما منها

TAB-FULL:v2p402/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r4.claim: No part of Quran can be better than another, since all is God’s speech; therefore the verse concerns rulings rather than Quranic passages themselves.
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r4.anchor: وغير جائز أن يكون من القرآن شيء خير من شيء؛ لأن جميعه كلام الله، ولا يجوز في صفات الله تعالى ذكره

TAB-FULL:v2p402/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r5.claim: The phrase means abrogating or leaving unchanged the ruling of a verse; listeners understand the omitted word “ruling.”
TAB-FULL:v2p402/r5.anchor: وإنما عنى جل ثناؤه بقوله: {ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها} [البقرة: 106] ما ننسخ من حكم آية أو ننسه

TAB-FULL:v2p403/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p403/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p403/r1.claim: The replacement can benefit Muhammad and the believers now or in the afterlife, or be equally beneficial in both terms.
TAB-FULL:v2p403/r1.anchor: وأنفع لك ولهم، إما عاجلا في الدنيا وإما آجلا في الآخرة

TAB-FULL:v2p403/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p403/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p403/r2.claim: Here قدير means strong or powerful, from ability; al-Tabari distinguishes it from قدر meaning measuring or determining.
TAB-FULL:v2p403/r2.anchor: ومعنى قوله: {قدير} [البقرة: 20] في هذا الموضع: قوي، يقال منه: قد قدرت على كذا وكذا

TAB-FULL:v2p403/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p403/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p403/r3.claim: Banu Murra of Ghatafan pronounce قدرت عليه with a kasra on the dāl; the measurement sense is قدرته أقدره قدرا.
TAB-FULL:v2p403/r3.anchor: وبنو مرة من غطفان تقول: قدرت عليه بكسر الدال. فأما من التقدير من قول القائل

TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r1.claim: Some say the question tells Muhammad that he already knows God is powerful and sovereign, like an Arab rhetorical question meaning “is it not so?”
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r1.anchor: كان بعضهم يقول: إنما ذلك من الله جل ثناؤه خبر عن أن محمدا قد علم ذلك

TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari rejects that analysis: ألم تعلم means “did you not know”; a negative with an interrogative requests confirmation or denies, not affirms.
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r2.anchor: قال: وهذا لا وجه له عندنا؛ وذلك أن قوله جل ثناؤه {ألم تعلم} [البقرة: 106] إنما معناه: أما علمت. وهو حرف جحد أدخل عليه حرف استفهام

TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r3.claim: Although phrased to Muhammad, the address is aimed at his companions, the people warned in 2:104; the plural wording at 2:107 confirms this.
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r3.anchor: فإنما هو معنى به أصحابه الذين قال الله جل ثناؤه: {لا تقولوا راعنا وقولوا انظرنا واسمعوا} [البقرة: 104]

TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r4.claim: Arabic can address one person while intending a group, or address a group while intending one; the shift from singular to plural is an established usage.
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r4.anchor: أن يخرج المتكلم كلامه على وجه الخطاب منه لبعض الناس وهو قاصد به غيره، وعلى وجه الخطاب لواحد وهو يقصد به جماعة

TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r5.claim: The return to plural address in 2:107 after the singular opening helps identify the companions as the intended audience.
TAB-FULL:v2p403#2/r5.anchor: والذي يدل على أن ذلك كذلك قوله جل ثناؤه: {وما لكم من دون الله من ولي ولا نصير} [البقرة: 107] فعاد بالخطاب في آخر الآية إلى جميعهم

TAB-FULL:v2p405/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r1.claim: Al-Tabari cites al-Kumayt’s praise poem, which addresses Ahmad while aiming its words at the Prophet’s household and the Umayyad critics.
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r1.anchor: إلى السراج المنير أحمد لا … يعدلني رغبة ولا رهب

TAB-FULL:v2p405/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r2.speaker: جميل بن معمر
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r2.claim: Jamil begins by speaking of his neighbors as a group, then uses a singular predicate because he means one of them.
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r2.anchor: وكما قال جميل بن معمر: [البحر الطويل] ألا إن جيراني العشية رائح …

TAB-FULL:v2p405/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r3.speaker: جميل بن معمر
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r3.claim: In another poem Jamil uses the masculine قاتل for the woman he loves, demonstrating reference to a woman through a masculine form.
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r3.anchor: وكما قال جميل أيضا في كلمته الأخرى: خليلي فيما عشتما هل رأيتما … قتيلا بكى من حب قاتله قبلي

TAB-FULL:v2p405/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r4.claim: Likewise, the singular address to Muhammad in 2:106–107 is intended for his companions, as the plural address and 2:108 show.
TAB-FULL:v2p405/r4.anchor: فكذلك قوله: {ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير} [البقرة: 106] {ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السموات والأرض}

SULAMI:v1p63/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p63/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p63/r1.claim: Every change of state brings a person to a higher station, until the states end in intimate companionship and direct address without an intermediary.
SULAMI:v1p63/r1.anchor: ما نقلتك من حالة إلا أوصلناك إلى مقام أشرف منها وأعلى إلى أن تنتهى بك الأحوال إلى محل الندامى

TABATABAI:2:106-107/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r1.speaker: author
