TABATABAI:2:106-107/r1.claim: The jurists' technical definition of naskh as clarifying that a ruling's term has ended is derived from this verse and is one instance of its broader apparent meaning.
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r1.anchor: النسخ بالمعنى المعروف عند الفقهاء وهو الإبانة عن انتهاء أمد الحكم وانقضاء أجله اصطلاح متفرع على الآية

TABATABAI:2:106-107/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r2.claim: Naskh means removal; Arabic says the sun removes the shadow, and the Qur'an uses the verb for God's removal of what Satan casts into a prophet's recitation.
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r2.anchor: النسخ هو الإزالة، يقال نسخت الشمس الظل إذا أزالته وذهبت به

TABATABAI:2:106-107/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r3.claim: Naskh can also describe copying a book from one copy to another, as though the first were replaced; the Qur'an likewise uses tabdīl for replacing a verse.
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r3.anchor: ومنه أيضا قولهم نسخت الكتاب إذا نقل من نسخة إلى أخرى

TABATABAI:2:106-107/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r4.claim: Naskh does not annihilate the verse itself; it removes its effect as a sign, such as a legal obligation, while preserving its underlying existence, whereas insāʾ removes it from knowledge.
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r4.anchor: والإنساء إفعال من النسيان وهو الإذهاب عن العلم كما أن النسخ هو الإذهاب عن العين

TABATABAI:2:106-107/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r5.claim: An āyah can be a Qur'anic passage through its inimitability, a divine ruling through its benefit for piety and closeness, an existent through its disclosure of its maker, or a prophet or saint through the call in word and deed.
TABATABAI:2:106-107/r5.anchor: فالبعض من القرآن آية لله سبحانه باعتبار عجز البشر عن إتيان مثله، والأحكام والتكاليف الإلهية آيات له تعالى

TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r1.claim: The Qur'an describes signs as differing in degree, as in the verse saying the Prophet saw some of his Lord's greatest signs.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r1.anchor: لقد رأى من آيات ربه الكبرى

TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r2.claim: A sign can have one aspect or many; naskh may remove the whole sign or only one aspect, as when a Qur'anic ruling is abrogated while its eloquence and inimitability remain.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r2.anchor: كالآية من القرآن تنسخ من حيث حكمها الشرعي وتبقى من حيث بلاغتها وإعجازها

TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r3.speaker: اليهود
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r3.claim: The passage notes the Jewish objection to abrogation as an objection transmitted among reports on the verse's occasion of revelation.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r3.anchor: الإنكار الواقع من اليهود على ما نقل في شأن نزول الآية بالنسبة إلى معنى النسخ

TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r4.speaker: اليهود
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r4.claim: One objection says a divinely revealed sign protects a real interest that nothing can replace, so removing it loses a benefit; unlike humans, God cannot revise a ruling because His knowledge changes.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r4.anchor: أحدهما من جهة أن الآية إذا كانت من عند الله تعالى كانت حافظة لمصلحة من المصالح الحقيقية لا تحفظها شيء دونها

TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r5.claim: The reply is that God is capable of bringing something better or equal to replace what is removed; this objection effectively denies His unrestricted power.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#2/r5.anchor: فأشار سبحانه إلى الجواب عن الأول بقوله { ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير } أي فلا يعجز عن إقامة ما هو خير من الفائت

TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r1.claim: The two divine questions answer the two objections in order; their separation without a conjunction indicates two distinct objections.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r1.anchor: فقوله تعالى { ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير ألم تعلم أن الله له ملك السماوات والأرض } ، مرتب على ترتيب ما يتوهم من الاعتراضين

TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r4.claim: Naskh is not limited to religious rulings; it also applies to created things and events.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r4.anchor: أن النسخ لا يختص بالأحكام الشرعية بل يعم التكوينيات أيضا

TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r5.claim: Abrogation always involves two sides: the abrogating sign or ruling and the one abrogated.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r5.anchor: أن النسخ لا يتحقق من غير طرفين ناسخ ومنسوخ

TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r6.claim: The abrogating replacement contains the perfection or interest present in what it abrogates.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r6.anchor: أن الناسخ يشتمل على ما في المنسوخ من كمال أو مصلحة

TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r7.claim: Although abrogating and abrogated rulings appear opposed, both share an interest that resolves the contradiction; each ruling fits the needs of its time.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r7.anchor: يرتفع التناقض بينهما من جهة اشتمال كليهما على المصلحة المشتركة

TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r8.claim: A prophet's death and a later prophet's mission follow the natural order of life and mortality and changing needs as people and eras develop.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r8.anchor: فإذا توفي نبي وبعث نبي آخر وهما آيتان من آيات الله تعالى أحدهما ناسخ للآخر

TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r9.claim: Religious rulings can change with circumstances: early leniency suited a weak community without resources, while later jihad suited a stronger Islam with forces prepared.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r9.anchor: كحكم العفو في أول الدعوة وليس للمسلمين بعد عدة ولا عدة. وحكم الجهاد بعد ذلك حينما قوي الإسلام

TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r10.claim: Abrogated verses can hint at their coming replacement; the author introduces 2:109 and 4:15 as examples.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#3/r10.anchor: والآيات المنسوخة مع ذلك لا تخلو من إيماء وتلويح إلى النسخ كما في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r1.claim: Naskh differs from general-specific, unqualified-qualified, and ambiguous-explained relations: the former pair is reconciled by shared wisdom or interest, while the others are resolved by the wording's stronger indication.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r1.anchor: فإن الرافع للتنافي بين الناسخ والمنسوخ بعد استقراره بينهما بحسب الظهور اللفظي هو الحكمة والمصلحة الموجودة بينهما

TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r2.claim: One reading has nunsihā with ḍamma on the nūn and kasra on the sīn, from insāʾ, meaning to remove from knowledge or memory.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r2.anchor: قرىء بضم النون وكسر السين من الانساء بمعنى الإذهاب عن العلم والذكر

TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r3.claim: This wording is general and does not refer to the Prophet; indeed the author says it excludes him, since the earlier Meccan promise says he will not forget.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r3.anchor: وهو كلام مطلق أو عام غير مختص برسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بل غير شامل له أصلا

TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r4.claim: The exception in this verse is like the exception in 11:108.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#4/r4.anchor: وأما اشتماله على الاستثناء بقوله { إلا ما شاء الله } فهو على حد الاستثناء الواقع في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r1.claim: A variant reads nansāhā with a fatḥa on the nūn and hamza, from nasʾ meaning to delay; the verse then means removing a sign or delaying its manifestation.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r1.anchor: وقرىء قوله ننسأها بفتح النون والهمزة من نسئ نسيئا إذا أخر تأخيرا

TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r2.claim: Whether God removes or delays a sign, no perfection or interest is lost; 'better or equal' concerns the perfection of an existent or the interest of a prescribed ruling.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r2.anchor: والدليل على أن المراد بيان أن التصرف الإلهي يكون دائما على الكمال والمصلحة هو قوله بخير منها أو مثلها

TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r3.speaker: النبي والصحابة وأئمة أهل البيت
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r3.claim: Numerous reports from the Prophet, Companions, and the Imams of the Prophet's household state that the Qur'an includes abrogating and abrogated passages.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r3.anchor: قد تكاثرت روايات الفريقين عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم والصحابة وعن أئمة أهل البيت عليه السلام ان في القرآن ناسخا ومنسوخا

TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r4.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r4.claim: Al-Nuʿmānī transmits from ʿAlī that 51:56, saying jinn and humans were created to worship, was abrogated by 11:118: God created them for mercy.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#5/r4.anchor: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام بعد ذكر عدة آيات من الناسخ والمنسوخ قال عليه السلام ونسخ قوله تعالى { وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون }

TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i reads abrogation here more broadly than legislative repeal: the verses’ purposes can be qualified, with worship the universal end and mercy the realized end for those guided.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r1.anchor: وفيها دلالة على أخذه عليه السلام النسخ في الآية أعم من النسخ الواقع في التشريع

TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r2.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r2.claim: A report in al-Nu'mani attributes to the Imam the reading of 21:101–102 as abrogating the universal statement that all will come to Hell in 19:71: the people promised good are kept away.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r2.anchor: وفي تفسير النعماني أيضا عنه عليه السلام قال ونسخ قوله تعالى { وإن منكم إلا واردها

TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r3.claim: He rejects treating 19:71 and 21:101–102 as a general verse qualified by a particular one: an irrevocable divine decree cannot be lifted or invalidated.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r3.anchor: أقول وليست الآيتان من قبيل العام والخاص لقوله تعالى { كان على ربك حتما مقضيا }

TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r4.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r4.claim: Al-Baqir is reported to include badaʾ among forms of abrogation, citing God's erasing and confirming what He wills, and the deliverance of Jonah's people.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r4.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن الباقر عليه السلام إن من النسخ البداء المشتمل عليه قوله تعالى { يمحوا الله ما يشاء

TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r5.speaker: أئمة أهل البيت
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r5.claim: Some reports from the Imams count the death of one Imam and the succession of another as abrogation; al-Tabataba'i says he explained this earlier and that reports on such meanings are abundant.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r5.anchor: وفي بعض الأخبار عن أئمة أهل البيت عد عليه السلام موت إمام وقيام إمام آخر مقامه من النسخ

TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r6.speaker: قتادة
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r6.claim: Qatada reports that God lifted verses and caused the Prophet to forget them; he glosses the replacement as bringing something lighter, a concession, a command, or a prohibition.
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r6.anchor: عن قتادة قال كانت الآية تنسخ الآية وكان نبي الله يقرأ الآية والسورة

TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r7.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects the reports that explain the verse as God making the Prophet forget recited material because they contradict the Qur'an, as discussed under “or cause it to be forgotten.”
TABATABAI:2:106-107#6/r7.anchor: وجميعها مطروحة بمخالفة الكتاب كما مر في بيان قوله أو ننسها

TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r1.claim: The segment continues a report attributed to Ibn Abbas: revelation came to the Prophet at night and was deferred or made to disappear by day, linked to 2:106.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r1.anchor: ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها

TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r2.claim: Abu Umama reports that an Ansari and others could recall only the basmala of a sura; the Prophet said it had been abrogated the previous night and erased from memory and writing.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r2.anchor: عن أبي أمامة أن رهطا من الأنصار من أصحاب النبي

TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r3.claim: Saad ibn Abi Waqqas read the variant nansa'ha, rejected Ibn al-Musayyib's nunsiha reading, and said the Quran had not been revealed to Ibn al-Musayyib or his family; al-Hakim graded the report sound.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r3.anchor: عن سعد بن أبي وقاص أنه قرأ

TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r4.claim: Saad appeals to 87:6 and 18:24 to argue that God protected the Prophet from forgetting, so nansa'ha means defer or leave rather than cause him to forget.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r4.anchor: أقول يريد بالتمسك بالآيتين أن الله رفع النسيان

TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r5.claim: On Saad's reading, nasakh removes a verse's legal force while preserving recitation, as with the charity consultation verse; nansa'ha removes legal force and recitation, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada interpret it.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r5.anchor: إزالة الآية عن العمل دون التلاوة كآية صدقة النجوى

TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel reviewed the Quran with the Prophet annually and twice in his final year; Abdullah witnessed what had been abrogated or changed.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r6.anchor: عن أبي ظبيان قال قال لنا ابن عباس

TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r7.claim: Related reports convey the same account through Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masud, and other Companions and Successors.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r7.anchor: وهذا المعنى مروي بطرق أخرى عن ابن عباس وعبد الله بن مسعود

TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r8.claim: Abrogation may affect a ruling while the verse remains in the codex, or affect recitation with or without also abrogating its ruling.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#27/r8.anchor: محصل ما استفيد منها أن النسخ قد يكون في الحكم

TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r1.claim: Al-Tabatabai says 2:106 and 16:101 do not concern abrogation of recitation; he explained this under 2:106 and will discuss it under 16:101.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r1.anchor: أن الآيتين أجنبيتان عن الإنساء بمعنى نسخ التلاوة

TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r2.claim: Because these reports conflict with the Quran's clear wording, the author rejects both the reports of forgetting and those of textual alteration.
TABATABAI:15:1-9#28/r2.anchor: أن هذه الروايات مخالفة لصريح الكتاب فالوجه عطفها على روايات التحريف

AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r1.claim: Some read ننسأها, meaning that God delays the verse, as al-nasīʾ in 9:37 means postponement.
AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم {ننسأها} أي نؤخرها، وهو مثل {إنما النسيء زيادة في الكفر} لأنه تأخير

AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r2.claim: The delay sense comes from أنسأت: أنسأتك الدين means I deferred the debt for you; النسيء is its verbal noun, and intercalation delays a month.
AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r2.anchor: "أنسأتك الدين" أي: جعلتك تؤخره. كأنه قال: "أنسأتك" ف"نسأت" و "النسيء" أنهم كانوا يدخلون الشهر في الشهر

AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r3.claim: The reading ننسها is also sound, and the conditional verb is jussive as the answer to the condition.
AKHFASH:v1p149#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم {أو ننسها} كل ذلك صواب. وجزمه بالمجازاة

TABRISI:2:106/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106/r1.speaker: ابن عامر
TABRISI:2:106/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads nunsikh with a damma on nūn and kasra on sīn; the other readers open both vowels.
TABRISI:2:106/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر ما ننسخ بضم النون وكسر السين والباقون بفتحها

TABRISI:2:106/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
TABRISI:2:106/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read nansaʾhā with both vowels open and a hamza; the rest read nunshihā with a damma, kasra, and no hamza.
TABRISI:2:106/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ننساها بفتح النون والسين وإثبات الهمزة والباقون بضم النون وكسر السين بلا همز

TABRISI:2:106/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106/r3.claim: The best explanation of Ibn ʿĀmir’s form is that nasakha and ansakha are two synonymous dialect forms; the ordinary open-vowel reading is clearer.
TABRISI:2:106/r3.anchor: لغتين متفقتين في المعنى وإن اختلفتا في اللفظ

TABRISI:2:106/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106/r4.claim: In Arabic, naskh means removing something and putting another thing in its place, as the sun removes and replaces the shade.
TABRISI:2:106/r4.anchor: النسخ في اللغة إبطال شيء وإقامة آخر مقامه يقال نسخت الشمس الظل أي أذهبته وحلت محله

TABRISI:2:106/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106/r5.speaker: ابن دريد
TABRISI:2:106/r5.claim: Ibn Durayd generalizes the root: anything that replaces another thing has superseded it.
TABRISI:2:106/r5.anchor: وقال ابن دريد كل شيء خلف شيئا فقد انتسخه وانتسخ الشيب الشباب

TABRISI:2:106/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106/r6.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:2:106/r6.claim: Alī ibn ʿĪsā defines abrogation as lifting an obligation and replacing it, but the author rejects this as too broad, giving inability to pray standing and a ruling against reason as counterexamples.
TABRISI:2:106/r6.anchor: وهذا ليس بصحيح لأنه ينتقض بمن يلزمه الصلاة

TABRISI:2:106/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106/r7.claim: Abrogation is a later legal proof that a ruling established by an earlier text will not apply in the future, though absent the later proof the earlier text would still govern.
TABRISI:2:106/r7.anchor: وأولى ما يجد به النسخ أن يقال هو كل دليل شرعي دل على أن مثل الحكم الثابت بالنص الأول غير ثابت في المستقبل

TABRISI:2:106/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106/r8.speaker: أبو بكر
TABRISI:2:106/r8.claim: The first kind of Qurʾanic abrogation lifts both a verse’s ruling and its recitation; Abū Bakr is reported to have cited a formerly recited warning about disowning fathers.
TABRISI:2:106/r8.anchor: أن يرفع حكم الآية وتلاوتها كما روي عن أبي بكر أنه قال كنا نقرأ لا ترغبوا عن آبائكم

TABRISI:2:106#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#2/r1.claim: A second form of Qurʾanic abrogation leaves a verse written in the muṣḥaf while removing its legal force; 60:11 is the example.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r1.anchor: هذه ثابتة اللفظ في الخط مرتفعة الحكم

TABRISI:2:106#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#2/r2.claim: A third form removes the wording while retaining the ruling, as with the stoning verse; the author notes many reports of recitations once present in the Qurʾan being lifted.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r2.anchor: ومنها ما يرتفع اللفظ ويثبت الحكم كآية الرجم فقد قيل كانت منزلة فرفع لفظها

TABRISI:2:106#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r3.speaker: أبو موسى
TABRISI:2:106#2/r3.claim: Abū Mūsā reports a recitation that a person with two valleys of wealth would seek a third, that only dust fills his stomach, and that God accepts the repentance of the repentant; it was later lifted.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r3.anchor: ما روي عن أبي موسى أنهم كانوا يقرأون لو أن لابن آدم واديين من مال

TABRISI:2:106#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r4.speaker: أنس
TABRISI:2:106#2/r4.claim: Anas reports that a recitation honoring the seventy Anṣār killed at Biʾr Maʿūna was later lifted.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r4.anchor: وعن أنس أن السبعين من الأنصار الذين قتلوا ببئر معونة قرأنا فيهم كتابا

TABRISI:2:106#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
TABRISI:2:106#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets nansaʾhā as letting the verse proceed without abrogating it; Ṭarafa’s line uses the root for driving something along.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة معنى ننسأها أي نمضيها فلا ننسخها

TABRISI:2:106#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#2/r6.claim: The root n-s-ʾ means delay: camels can be kept from the watering place or their watering interval extended; it also describes fattening livestock and urging a mount onward.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r6.anchor: نسأت الإبل في ظمئها أنسأها نسأ إذا زدتها

TABRISI:2:106#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#2/r7.claim: Mā is a conditional noun standing in place of an, accusative as the object of nansakh but fronted because it represents a sentence-initial conditional particle; the verbs are jussive.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r7.anchor: ما اسم ناب مناب أن وهو في موضع نصب بننسخ وإنما لزمه التقديم وإن كان مفعولا

TABRISI:2:106#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#2/r8.claim: Min in min āya is either partitive or redundant.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r8.anchor: ومن في قوله من آية للتبعيض وقيل هي مزيدة

TABRISI:2:106#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#2/r9.claim: Alam is formally interrogative but functions as confirmation, and taʿlam remains jussive under lam because the interrogative does not change the governing particle’s effect.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r9.anchor: ولفظ ألم ها هنا لفظ الاستفهام ومعناه التقرير وتعلم مجزوم بلم

TABRISI:2:106#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r10.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:2:106#2/r10.claim: One coherence reading sees the verse assuring believers that God will still send them good despite disbelievers’ wish that no good be revealed to them.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r10.anchor: دل بهذه الآية على أنه سبحانه لا يخليهم من إنزال خير إليهم

TABRISI:2:106#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r11.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:2:106#2/r11.claim: Abū Muslim reads the verse as a reply to Jews who criticized Muhammad for abrogating previous religious laws.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r11.anchor: وقيل إنه سبحانه لما عاب اليهود بأشياء ورد عليهم ما راموا به الطعن في أمر نبينا

TABRISI:2:106#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#2/r12.claim: The verse may mean whatever verse or ruling God removes, or whatever verse He replaces, as reported from Ibn ʿAbbās.
TABRISI:2:106#2/r12.anchor: قد ذكرنا حقيقة النسخ عند المحققين وقيل معناه ما نرفع من آية

TABRISI:2:106#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#3/r1.claim: The reading nunsihā has two possible senses: forgetting, the opposite of remembering, or leaving and abandoning.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r1.anchor: فالوجه الأول في الآية مروي عن قتادة

TABRISI:2:106#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#3/r2.claim: The forgetfulness sense is illustrated by the command to remember God if one forgets, while abandonment is illustrated by God abandoning those who abandon Him.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r2.anchor: أي تركوا طاعة الله فترك رحمتهم أو ترك تخليصهم

TABRISI:2:106#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:106#3/r3.claim: Qatāda applies forgetfulness to the community: they may be told to leave off reciting a verse until they forget it; Abū Jaʿfar says this should not apply to the Prophet lest it repel people.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r3.anchor: الوجه الأول في الآية مروي عن قتادة وهو أن يكون محمولا على النسيان

TABRISI:2:106#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r4.speaker: جماعة من المحققين
TABRISI:2:106#3/r4.claim: Other scholars allow God to make even the Prophet forget a verse when public interest requires it, including by miraculously causing a large group to forget together.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r4.anchor: وقد جوز جماعة من المحققين ذلك على النبي

TABRISI:2:106#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:106#3/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the Prophet was taught the Qurʾan and then forgot it, citing God’s promise to make him recite without forgetting except what God wills.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r5.anchor: ذهب الحسن فقال: إن نبيكم أقرىء القرآن

TABRISI:2:106#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:106#3/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj rejects interpreting the word as forgetting because 17:73 and 17:86 say God would not will to remove what He revealed to the Prophet.

TABRISI:2:106#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
TABRISI:2:106#3/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī answers that the cited verses concern reports and histories that cannot be abrogated, whereas the Prophet could forget commands whose ruling depends on changing circumstances.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي هذا الذي احتج به على من ذهب إلى أن ننسها من النسيان لا يدل على فساد ما ذهبوا إليه

TABRISI:2:106#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r8.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وسالم مولى أبي حذيفة وسعد بن مالك
TABRISI:2:106#3/r8.claim: Variants from Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ, Sālim, and Saʿd ibn Mālik read the form as making someone forget; their wording supports the forgetfulness interpretation.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r8.anchor: قراءة سعد بن أبي وقاص وقراءة من قرأ أو ننسكها وهو المروي عن سالم مولى أبي حذيفة

TABRISI:2:106#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r9.speaker: الضحاك وابن مسعود والأعمش ومجاهد عن أبي
TABRISI:2:106#3/r9.claim: Readings attributed to al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ibn Masʿūd, al-Aʿmash, and Ubayy render the omitted object as the Prophet or someone being made to forget the verse.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r9.anchor: ما روي عن الضحاك أنه قرأ ننسها ويؤكد ذلك أيضا ما روي من قراءة ابن مسعود

TABRISI:2:106#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#3/r10.claim: In the reading nunsihā the intended object is omitted; the explicit object in nunsikhā makes the meaning of causing someone to forget clear.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r10.anchor: فالمفعول المراد المحذوف في قراءة من قرأ أو ننسها مظهر في قراءة من قرأ ننسكها

TABRISI:2:106#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r11.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:106#3/r11.claim: Qatāda also says verses used to be abrogated by other verses and that God caused His Prophet to forget some of them.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r11.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قال كانت الآية تنسخ بالآية

TABRISI:2:106#3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#3/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:106#3/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes nunsihā to mean abandonment: God commands people to leave off acting on the verse.
TABRISI:2:106#3/r12.anchor: والوجه الثاني وهو أن المراد بالنسيان الترك في الآية مروي عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:106#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r1.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:106#4/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the sense ‘abandon’ is expressed with nasītu, not ansaytu; the verse means God commands people to leave the verse.
TABRISI:2:106#4/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج إنما يقال في هذا نسيت إذا تركت ولا يقال فيه أنسيت تركت

TABRISI:2:106#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r2.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:106#4/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī says interpreting ansaytu as ‘left’ is not wrong, since a person commanded to leave something has in effect left it.
TABRISI:2:106#4/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي من فسر أنسيت بتركت لا يكون مخطئا لأنك إذا أنسيت فقد نسيت

TABRISI:2:106#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r3.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:2:106#4/r3.claim: Alī ibn ʿĪsā explains that commentators describe the resulting meaning: one commanded to leave the verse has left it.
TABRISI:2:106#4/r3.anchor: ومن هذا قال علي بن عيسى إنما فسره المفسرون على ما يؤول إليه المعنى

TABRISI:2:106#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:106#4/r4.claim: Leaving the verse means preserving it without abrogation, as Ibn ʿAbbās explains: leave it and do not replace it; God’s ‘leaving’ is an expansive expression for letting something be.
TABRISI:2:106#4/r4.anchor: وإنما معناه اقرارها فلا ترفع كما قال ابن عباس نتركها فلا نبدلها

TABRISI:2:106#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#4/r5.claim: For readers who vocalize the word as nansaʾhā, with the sense of delay, the author lays out four interpretations.
TABRISI:2:106#4/r5.anchor: وأما من قرأ أو ننسأها على معنى التأخير فقيل فيه وجوه

TABRISI:2:106#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:106#4/r6.claim: One view means delaying a verse’s revelation and sending a replacement that serves the same interest or is better for people.
TABRISI:2:106#4/r6.anchor: أن معناه أو نؤخرها فلا ننزلها وننزل بدلا منها مما يقوم مقامها في المصلحة

TABRISI:2:106#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:106#4/r7.claim: Another view delays the verse to a later time and supplies an equivalent replacement at the earlier time; the author considers this the strongest account.
TABRISI:2:106#4/r7.anchor: أن معناه نؤخرها إلى وقت ثان ونأتي بدلا منها في الوقت المتقدم بما يقوم مقامها

TABRISI:2:106#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r8.speaker: أبي
TABRISI:2:106#4/r8.claim: A third view treats delay as a verse’s recitation being lifted after revelation and practice; Ubayy reports that al-Aḥzāb once had more than seventy verses and exceeded al-Baqara in length.

TABRISI:2:106#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:2:106#4/r9.claim: Mujāhid’s fourth view leaves the written wording and recitation in place while abrogating the ruling.
TABRISI:2:106#4/r9.anchor: وهو ما حكي عن مجاهد يثبت خطها ويبدل حكمها

TABRISI:2:106#4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#4/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#4/r10.claim: The author favors the second view; the first has little purpose if people never knew or heard the delayed verse, while the last two simply amount to abrogation.
TABRISI:2:106#4/r10.anchor: والوجهان الأولان عليهما الاعتماد لأن الوجهين الأخرين يرجع معناهما إلى معنى النسخ

TABRISI:2:106#5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:106#5/r1.claim: One interpretation takes ‘better’ as easier for people, such as the eased fighting command, and ‘equal’ as equally easy, such as changing the prayer direction to the Kaaba; this is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās.
TABRISI:2:106#5/r1.anchor: في السهولة كالعبادة بالتوجه إلى الكعبة بعد أن كان إلى بيت المقدس

TABRISI:2:106#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#5/r2.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:106#5/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a replacement is better or equal in the later period because it better serves the public interest of that time.
TABRISI:2:106#5/r2.anchor: نأت بخير منها في الوقت الثاني أي هي لكم في الوقت الثاني خير لكم من الأولى في الوقت الأول

TABRISI:2:106#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#5/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:106#5/r3.claim: Some take the address as directed to the Prophet; others take it to all morally responsible people, meaning any listener or person.
TABRISI:2:106#5/r3.anchor: قيل هو خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقيل هو خطاب لجميع المكلفين والمراد ألم تعلم أيها السامع

TABRISI:2:106#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#5/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#5/r4.claim: On one reading, God can produce verses and sūras like the Qurʾan to replace an abrogated command with something equally beneficial.
TABRISI:2:106#5/r4.anchor: أن الله تعالى قادر على آيات وسور مثل القرآن ينسخ بها ما أمر فيقوم في النفع مقام المنسوخ

TABRISI:2:106#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#5/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:106#5/r5.claim: If addressed to Muhammad, the question means God can help him and defeat his enemies; another view makes it general to everything.
TABRISI:2:106#5/r5.anchor: وعلى القول الأول معناه ألم تعلم يا محمد أنه سبحانه قادر على نصرك والانتصار لك من أعدائك

TABRISI:2:106#5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#5/r6.speaker: من زعم أنه لا يجوز نسخ القرآن بالسنة المعلومة
TABRISI:2:106#5/r6.claim: Those denying abrogation of Qurʾan by definitive Sunna argue that the verse attributes the replacement to God, while Sunna is not literally attributed to Him, and that the verse concerns God’s unique power over the miraculous Qurʾan.
TABRISI:2:106#5/r6.anchor: واستدل من زعم أنه لا يجوز نسخ القرآن بالسنة المعلومة بهذه الآية قال أضاف الإتيان بخير منها إلى نفسه

TABRISI:2:106#5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#5/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#5/r7.claim: The author holds that definitive Sunna may abrogate Qurʾan: it comes by God’s revelation and command, and ‘better’ means more beneficial for faith and reward, whether delivered by Qurʾan or Sunna.
TABRISI:2:106#5/r7.anchor: والصحيح أن القرآن يجوز أن ينسخ بالسنة المقطوع عليها ومعنى خير منها أي أصلح لنا منها في ديننا

TABRISI:2:106#5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:106#5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:106#5/r8.claim: The verse shows the Qurʾan is created and distinct from God: an eternal thing cannot be abrogated, and anything under God’s power is an originated act.
TABRISI:2:106#5/r8.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن القرآن محدث وأنه غير الله تعالى لأن القديم لا يصح نسخه

FARRA:v1p64/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p64/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p64/r1.claim: In “they forgot God, so He forgot them,” forgot means abandoned; a second possible sense is literal forgetting, as in “remember your Lord when you forget.”

FARRA:v1p64/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p64/r2.speaker: بعضهم
FARRA:v1p64/r2.claim: Some read ننسأها with hamza, deriving it from postponement and meaning “defer it”; al-Farrāʾ accepts both readings.

FARRA:v1p64/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p64/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
FARRA:v1p64/r3.claim: A report says the Prophet heard a man recite and prayed for him because he had reminded him of verses he had been made to forget.
FARRA:v1p64/r3.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة بإسناد برفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سمع

THALABI:v1p253/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p253/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes naskh as copying from an earlier original: in that sense the entire Qurʾan is a copy of the Preserved Tablet sent down to the Prophet.
THALABI:v1p253/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في هذه الآية: ألستم قوما عربا هل يكون نسخة إلا من أصل كان قبل ذلك؟

THALABI:v1p253/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p253/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Qurʾan descended together from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven, then Gabriel delivered it to Muhammad verse by verse.
THALABI:v1p253/r2.anchor: روى عبد الوهاب بن عطاء عن داود عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس: أنزل الله تعالى القرآن جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ إلى السماء الدنيا

THALABI:v1p253/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p253/r3.claim: Naskh also means removal or annulment, as when the sun removes a shadow; this sense makes some Qurʾanic rulings abrogate others.
THALABI:v1p253/r3.anchor: والوجه الثاني: بمعنى رفع الشيء وإبطاله يقال: نسخت الشمس الظل: أي ذهبت به وأبطلته

THALABI:v1p253/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p253/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes one abrogation type: the verse remains written while its ruling is replaced.
THALABI:v1p253/r4.anchor: كقول ابن عباس في قوله ما ننسخ من آية قال: ثبت خطها وتبدل حكمها.

THALABI:v1p253/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p253/r5.claim: One type removes recitation but leaves the ruling, as with the stoning verse.
THALABI:v1p253/r5.anchor: ومنها رفع تلاوتها وبقاء حكمها مثل آية الرجم.

THALABI:v1p253/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p253/r6.claim: Another type removes both recitation and ruling, so the verse leaves the written Qurʾan and people’s memory.
THALABI:v1p253/r6.anchor: أن ترفع الآية أصلا أي تلاوتها وحكمها معا فتكون خارجة من خط الكتاب

THALABI:v1p253/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r7.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v1p253/r7.claim: At Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab’s gathering, several people found a sura they knew impossible to recite; the Prophet said it had been abrogated the previous night.
THALABI:v1p253/r7.anchor: والشاهد له ما روي أبو أمامة سهل بن حنيف في مجلس سعيد ابن المسيب: إن رجلا كانت معه سور

THALABI:v1p253/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p253/r8.claim: Abrogation applies to commands and prohibitions, not reports, since abrogating a report would make the informant a liar.
THALABI:v1p253/r8.anchor: ثم اعلم أن النسخ إنما يعترض على الأوامر والنواهي دون الأخبار إذا نسخ صار المخبر كذابا،

THALABI:v1p253/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p253/r9.claim: The Jews say abrogating laws implies a change of mind in God; Thaʿlabī answers that some laws were first permitted and later forbidden.
THALABI:v1p253/r9.anchor: وإن اليهود حاولوا نسخ الشرائع وزعموا إنه بداء فيقال لهم: أليس قد أباح الله تزويج الاخت من الأخ ثم حظره

THALABI:v1p253/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p253/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p253/r10.claim: The author adds Abraham as an example of a command first given and then withdrawn: he was told to sacrifice his son and then not to.
THALABI:v1p253/r10.anchor: براهيم عليه السلام بذبح ابنه، ثم قال له لا تذبحه؟

THALABI:v1p254/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p254/r1.claim: Further examples answer the claim that abrogation entails a change of mind: God ordered Abraham to sacrifice his son, then told him not to; Moses ordered calf worshippers killed and then spared.
THALABI:v1p254/r1.anchor: أليس قد أمر موسى بني إسرائيل أن يقتلوا من عبد العجل منهم وأمرهم برفع السيف عنهم؟

THALABI:v1p254/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p254/r2.claim: Moses later withdrew the order to kill them, and Ezekiel was ordered to circumcise and then forbidden; neither case implies divine change of mind.
THALABI:v1p254/r2.anchor: وأمرهم برفع السيف عنهم؟ أليست نبوة موسى غير متعبد بها، ثم تعبد بذلك؟ أليس قد أمر حزقيل النبي بالختان

THALABI:v1p254/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p254/r3.claim: Abrogation is a transfer from one worship and ruling to another for a benefit, manifesting God’s wisdom and complete sovereignty, not a change of mind.
THALABI:v1p254/r3.anchor: فكذلك في نسخ الشرائع لم يلحقه بداء بل هو نقل العباد من عبادة إلى عبادة، وحكم إلى حكم

THALABI:v1p254/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p254/r4.claim: Abrogation is a major Qurʾanic science that anyone setting out to interpret the Qurʾan must know.
THALABI:v1p254/r4.anchor: فهذه من علم النسخ وهو نوع كثير من علوم القرآن، لا يسع جهله لمن شرع إلى التفسير.

THALABI:v1p254/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r5.speaker: علي
THALABI:v1p254/r5.claim: ʿAlī asked a preacher at the Kufa mosque whether he knew abrogating from abrogated verses; when he said no, ʿAlī warned that he had ruined himself and others.
THALABI:v1p254/r5.anchor: وعن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي: إن عليا عليه السلام مر بقاص يقص في جامع الكوفة بباب كندة

THALABI:v1p254/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r6.speaker: ابن عامر
THALABI:v1p254/r6.claim: The common reading opens nūn and sīn in nansakh; Ibn ʿĀmir reads nunsikh with ḍamma on nūn and kasra on sīn, which Abū Ḥātim calls an error.
THALABI:v1p254/r6.anchor:
قرأت العامة بفتح النون والسين من النسخ.
وقرأ ابن عامر: بضم النون وكسر السين.
قال أبو حاتم: هو غلط

THALABI:v1p254/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p254/r7.claim: Some defend Ibn ʿĀmir’s form in two ways: make something a copy of another, or place it among the abrogated, as making a man an exile.
THALABI:v1p254/r7.anchor: وقال: بعضهم له وجهان، أحدهما نجعله نسخه من قولك نسخت الكتاب إذا كتبته

THALABI:v1p254/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p254/r8.claim: The second proposed sense for nunsikh is to make a verse among the abrogated; a cited poem illustrates the form.
THALABI:v1p254/r8.anchor: والوجه الثاني: تجعله في جملة المنسوخ كقولك: طردت الرجل إذا نفيته وأطردته جعلته طريدا.

THALABI:v1p254/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r9.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وأبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب
THALABI:v1p254/r9.claim: These readers pronounce nunsihā with ḍamma on nūn and kasra on sīn; Abū ʿUbayd and Abū Ḥātim choose it, meaning “we cause it to be forgotten,” as most exegetes explain.
THALABI:v1p254/r9.anchor: قرأ سعيد بن المسيب وأبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي ويعقوب: ننسها بضم النون وكسر السين

THALABI:v1p254/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r10.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p254/r10.claim: Al-Hasan explains the reading as what God caused His Messenger to forget.
THALABI:v1p254/r10.anchor: قال الحسن: هو ما أنسى الله رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم.

THALABI:v1p254/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v1p254/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as leaving a verse without replacing it, linking the sense to 9:67 and 20:126.
THALABI:v1p254/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي نتركها ولا نبدلها قال الله: نسوا الله فأنساهم

THALABI:v1p254/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p254/r12.claim: In these citations, ansā and nasī are treated as equivalent in the sense of leaving or neglecting.
THALABI:v1p254/r12.anchor: كل هذا من الترك كانه جعل أنسى ونسي بمعنى واحد.

THALABI:v1p254/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p254/r13.speaker: أبو منصور الأزهري
THALABI:v1p254/r13.claim: Al-Azharī explains it as God commanding that a verse be left; ansaytu can mean that I ordered something to be left.
THALABI:v1p254/r13.anchor: سمعت أبا منصور الأزهري يقول: معناه أو نأمر بتركها يقال أنسيت الشيء

THALABI:v1p255/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r1.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v1p255/r1.claim: An anonymous poet’s line supports the sense of commanding that a story be left out of memory.
THALABI:v1p255/r1.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
جرت علي قصة أقصيتها … لست بناسيها مجمع ولا منسيها

THALABI:v1p255/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
THALABI:v1p255/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reads the phrase as “or We cause you to forget.”
THALABI:v1p255/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبي بن كعب: أو ننسيك.

THALABI:v1p255/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r3.speaker: عبد الله
THALABI:v1p255/r3.claim: ʿAbd Allāh reads “We cause you to forget an āya” or “We abrogate it.”
THALABI:v1p255/r3.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: ننسيك من آية أو ننسخها.

THALABI:v1p255/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r4.speaker: سالم مولى حذيفة
THALABI:v1p255/r4.claim: Sālim, the client of Ḥudhayfa, reads the phrase as “or We make it forgotten.”
THALABI:v1p255/r4.anchor: قرأ سالم مولى حذيفة: أو ننسكها.

THALABI:v1p255/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r5.speaker: أبو رجاء
THALABI:v1p255/r5.claim: Abū Rajāʾ reads nunsihā with a doubled sīn.
THALABI:v1p255/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو رجاء: أو ننسها بالتشديد، وقرأ الضحاك:

THALABI:v1p255/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r6.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v1p255/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk reads the form passively, with ḍamma on tāʾ and fatḥa on sīn.
THALABI:v1p255/r6.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك: أو ننسها بضم التاء وفتح السين على مجهول

THALABI:v1p255/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r7.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
THALABI:v1p255/r7.claim: Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ reads tansahā with an open tāʾ, from the verb “to forget.”
THALABI:v1p255/r7.anchor: وقرأ سعد بن أبي وقاص: أو تنسها بتاء المفتوحة من النسيان

THALABI:v1p255/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r8.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
THALABI:v1p255/r8.claim: Qāsim ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn Fāʾiq reports Saʿd’s reading and his retort that the Qurʾan was not revealed to the family of al-Musayyab.
THALABI:v1p255/r8.anchor:
سمعت سعد بن أبي وقاص يقول: بالنسخ من آية أو ننسها.
قال: فقلت له: إن سعيد بن المسيب يقرأ: ننسها.

THALABI:v1p255/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p255/r9.claim: Thaʿlabī links forgetting to God’s promise to make the Prophet recite without forgetting and the instruction to remember God when he forgets.
THALABI:v1p255/r9.anchor: قال الله تعالى لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم: سنقرئك فلا تنسى واذكر ربك إذا نسيت .

THALABI:v1p255/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r10.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v1p255/r10.claim: Mujāhid reads nunsahā with an open, ungeminated nūn, meaning “or We leave it.”
THALABI:v1p255/r10.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد: (أو ننسها) بفتح النون مخففة أي نتركها

THALABI:v1p255/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r11.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس وعبيد بن عمير وعطاء وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والنخعي
THALABI:v1p255/r11.claim: These readers pronounce nansāʾahā with open nūn and hamza, meaning defer it without replacing or abrogating it.
THALABI:v1p255/r11.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس وعبيد بن عمير وعطاء وابن كثير وأبو عمرو والنخعي: أو ننساها بفتح النون الأول

THALABI:v1p255/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r12.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v1p255/r12.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says nansāʾahā means to carry it forward, retaining the remembrance of what it contains.
THALABI:v1p255/r12.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد: ننسأها مجازه نمضيها لذكر ما فيه

THALABI:v1p255/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r13.speaker: طرفة
THALABI:v1p255/r13.claim: Ṭarafa’s line uses nasʾ for carrying a thing forward or adhering it, supporting Abū ʿUbayd’s gloss.
THALABI:v1p255/r13.anchor:
قال طرفة:
أمون كألواح الاران نسأتها … على لاحب كأنه ظهر برجد

THALABI:v1p255/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r14.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وعطاء
THALABI:v1p255/r14.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and ʿAṭāʾ distinguish the phrases: nansakh concerns revealed Qurʾan as a copy, while nansāʾahā defers a verse not yet revealed.
THALABI:v1p255/r14.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب وعطاء: أما ما ننسخ من آية فهو ما قد نزل من القرآن

THALABI:v1p255/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p255/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p255/r15.claim: “Better” means more useful, easier, and more rewarding; no verse is inherently better than another, since God’s speech is one and the difference lies in benefit and reward.
THALABI:v1p255/r15.anchor: نأت بخير منها أي بما هو أجدى وأنفع لكم وأسهل عليكم وأكثر لأجركم

THALABI:v1p275/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p275/r3.speaker: شجاع بن أبي نصر
THALABI:v1p275/r3.claim: Shuja, whom Qasim ibn Sallam calls reliable and truthful, says he saw the Prophet in a dream approve Abu Amr’s readings except this one and the hamzated reading of 2:106.
THALABI:v1p275/r3.anchor: وأخبر القاسم بن سلام عن شجاع بن أبي نصر قال، وكان أمينا صدوقا: إنه رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في المنام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines naskh linguistically as canceling one thing and putting another in its place, as the sun removes the shade and takes its place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: النسخ في اللغة: إبطال شيء وإقامة آخر مقامه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r2.speaker: غيره
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r2.claim: Another authority explains succession as the passing of one age or generation and the arrival of another to take its place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r2.anchor: وقال غيره: تناسخ الأزمنة والقرن بعد القرن: هو مضي الأول ومجيء الثاني بعده يخلفه في محله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r3.speaker: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r3.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī distinguishes replacing one thing with another from transferring a thing to a new place while it remains the same.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r3.anchor: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي: النسخ: تبديل الشيء من الشيء، وهو غيره، والنسخ: نقل شيء من مكان إلى مكان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r4.speaker: الفراء وأبو سعيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and Abū Saʿīd use masakha and nasakha for turning someone into an ape as equivalent expressions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r4.anchor: وروى أبو تراب (¬4) عن الفراء وأبي سعيد: مسخه الله قردا، ونسخه قردا، بمعنى واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r5.speaker: العلماء من أهل اللغة والتفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r5.claim: Linguists and exegetes give naskh two senses, the first being to copy a book into another copy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r5.anchor: وقال العلماء من أهل اللغة والتفسير (¬1): النسخ له معنيان:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r6.claim: In the copying sense, istinsākh in 45:29 may mean making a copy, like istaskhara meaning sakhira, or summoning the angels to write; both mean writing without copying from a physical exemplar.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r6.anchor: ومن هذا قوله عز وجل {إنا كنا نستنسخ ما كنتم تعملون} [الجاثية: 29]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r7.claim: On the copying sense, the entire Qurʾan is a transcription from the Mother of the Book to the Prophet before being sent down to him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r7.anchor: فعلى هذا المعنى: القرآن كله منسوخ،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r8.speaker: العلماء من أهل اللغة والتفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r8.claim: The second sense is lifting and nullifying a ruling, either with a replacement or without one; the verse intends this sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r8.anchor: والثاني: هو رفع الحكم وإبطاله، ثم يجوز النسخ إلى بدل وإلى غير بدل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r9.claim: Abrogation in the Qurʾan includes a ruling that is lifted while its wording remains written and recited but is no longer acted upon; this is the familiar form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p220/r9.anchor: منها: ما يكون حكمه مرفوعا، وخطه مثبت يتلى ويقرأ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p234/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p234/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p234/r1.claim: God has power over everything, including abrogation, substitution, and all else.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p234#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p234#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p234#2/r1.claim: The question is an admonitory affirmation: it expects agreement, as in the poetic question, You are the best riders of camels.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r1.claim: The reading nunsihā means “or cause you to forget it,” with the omitted object understood as you.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r2.speaker: قارئ بالهمز
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r2.claim: A hamzated reading, nunsāʾhā, means to defer the verse rather than abrogate it until a later term; sale on credit and postponing Muḥarram's sanctity illustrate the sense of delay.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r2.anchor: ومن قرأها: "أو ننسأها". بالهمز (1) . أراد: نؤخرها فلا ننسخها إلى مدة.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r3.claim: “Better” means more excellent; its advantage lies in being easier and lighter.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p60#3/r3.anchor: نأت بخير منها} أي: بأفضل منها. ومعنى فضلها: سهولتها وخفتها

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#2/r1.claim: The sūrahs called al-miʾūn follow the seven long sūrahs; each has more than, or nearly, one hundred verses.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p35#2/r1.anchor: و (السور التي تعرف بالمئين) هي ما ولي السبع الطوال، سميت بمئين لأن كل سور منها تزيد على مائة آية أو تقاربها.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r1.claim: Abrogating a verse means removing it by invalidating its ruling.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r1.anchor: ما نرفع آية من جهة النسخ بأن نبطل حكمها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r2.claim: Causing a verse to be forgotten means erasing it from people’s hearts.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r2.anchor: أو بالإنساء لها بأن نمحوها عن القلوب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r3.claim: A better replacement is more suitable and useful for those charged with it, easier for them, and greater in reward.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r3.anchor: أصلح لمن تعبد بها، وأنفع لهم وأسهل عليهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r4.claim: An equivalent replacement matches it in benefit and reward.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r5.claim: The verse was revealed after polytheists alleged that Muhammad gave his Companions a command and then reversed it, proving the Quran was his own speech.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r5.anchor: حين قال المشركون: إن محمدا يأمر أصحابه بأمر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r6.claim: The commentary links the abrogation discussion to the statement about replacing one verse with another.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:106-107/r6.anchor: وقوله: وإذا بدلنا آية مكان آية

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r1.speaker: İbn Âmir
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r1.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads with a damma on the nūn and kasra on the sīn, deriving the form from insākh.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r1.anchor: İbn Âmir kıraatinde “nûn”un zammı ve “sin”in kesriyle مَا نَنسَخْ okunur ki “insâh”tandır

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r2.speaker: İbn Kesîr ve Ebû Amr
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read with fatḥa on the first nūn and sīn followed by a hamza sākin, from neseʾ/nesīʾ, meaning to delay.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r2.anchor: İbn Kesîr ve Ebû Amr kıraatlerinde birinci “nûn”un ve “sin”in fethaları ve bundan sonra bir hemze-i sâkine ile أَوْ نُنسِهَا okunur ki tehir mânasına “nese’” ve “nesîe”dendir

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r3.claim: The verse establishes the permissibility of abrogation in revealed law, explicitly including the earlier scriptures.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r3.anchor: âyetin sevki kütüb-i sâlifenin cevâz-ı neshi hakkında nas ise de

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r4.claim: Because “any verse” is general in wording, the verse also apparently covers Qur'anic verses; denying abrogation in the Qur'an denies the plain text.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r4.anchor: mantûku itibariyle مِنْ ءَايَةٍ âm olduğundan bazı Kur’ân âyetlerine de zâhir olarak şâmildir. Binâen‘aleyh âyât-ı Kur’âniyede de nâsih ve mensuh vardır

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r5.claim: Lexically, naskh means substitution, putting something else in the place of a thing; the Qur'an uses tabdīl for it.

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r6.claim: Naskh can mean removal or annulment, as when the sun replaces and removes the shade; 22:52 uses it this way.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r6.anchor: “Güneş gölgeyi nesh etti” demek, “onun yerine geçti” demektir ki buna “izâle ve ibtal etti” denilir

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r7.claim: Naskh also means transferring something in place of another, as in copying a book; 45:29 uses the verb for recording deeds.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r7.anchor: إِنَّا كُنَّا نَسْتَنسِخُ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r8.claim: In legal usage, abrogation is later revealed legal evidence indicating an earlier ruling's opposite: to God it discloses the ruling's endpoint, while to us it lifts the apparently continuing ruling.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r8.anchor: Istılâh-ı şer‘de de nesh herhangi bir hükm-i şer‘înin hilâfına sonradan diğer bir delîl-i şer‘înin delâlet etmesidir ki ilm-i ilâhîye nazaran evvelki hükmün müntehâ-yı müddetini beyan

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r9.claim: Abrogation is explanatory change, never divine reconsideration or ignorance; it applies to non-eternal commands and prohibitions, not reports or rulings expressly made eternal.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r9.anchor: ebediyetle takyid edilmiş olan hükümlerde nesh cereyan edemez, kezâlik haberlerde de nesh cereyan edemez. Nesh ancak evâmir ü nevâhî gibi inşâî bir mânayı tazammun eden

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r10.claim: Changing created things over time and changing rulings across eras diminish neither divine knowledge, will, nor power; each change manifests wise decree, not reconsideration.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r10.anchor: âlem-i tekvînde bugün yarattığını yarın ifnâ ederek diğer bir şeye tebdil etmekle ilmine, kudretine, iradesine hiçbir nakīsa ârız olmayacağı gibi, âlem-i teşrî‘de de başka başka zamanlarda başka başka hükm-i şer‘î inşa etmekle

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r11.claim: Creedal and informational truths cannot be abrogated; even a report about a time-bound event remains eternally true and cannot be denied for that time.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r11.anchor: Hâsılı hakāik-i îmâniye, i‘tikādiye gibi ihbârî olan esâsât-ı ilmiye kābil-i nesh değildir. Bunların bir an için zamânî olanları bile hakāik-i ezeliye hükmündedir.

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r12.claim: Commands such as drinking water, avoiding wine, marrying, and avoiding adultery can change status over time unless explicitly eternal; abrogation discloses their term.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r12.anchor: “su iç, şarab içme, nikâh yap, zina etme” gibi inşâî olan teşrî‘ât sarâhaten ebediyetle takyid edilmedikçe kābil-i neshdirler

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r13.claim: The Qur'an confirms and further explains the Torah and earlier scriptures, while replacing some of their rulings with a complete, accessible law suited to every era.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r13.anchor: Kur’an, Tevrat’ı ve sâir kütüb-i sâlife-i ilâhiyeyi musaddıktır, müeyyiddir, daha ziyadesiyle müfessir ve mübeyyindir. İkinci kısımda ise Kur’an onlardaki birtakım ahkâmı nesh ederek

ELMALILI:2:106-113/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r14.claim: By the principle of divine unity, creation and legislation belong solely to God; people may act only within His revealed laws and evidence, never abrogating them by human will.
ELMALILI:2:106-113/r14.anchor: ‘İbâd nihâyet O’nun inşââtı içinde ve O’nun gösterdiği âyât ve edillenin delâlet-i ilmiyesine göre bir tasarrufa me’zundur

ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r1.claim: The claim that God cannot abrogate and therefore cannot send this revelation is false; abrogation involves wisdom and no deficiency.
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r1.anchor: yalan söylüyorlar ve yanlış biliyorlar. Yapabilir ve yapar ve yapmasında hiçbir nakīsa

ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r2.claim: An abrogated verse may be partly or wholly replaced, including its legal meaning, the ruling on its recitation, or both.
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r2.anchor: mânasındaki bir hükmünü veya lafzının hükmü olan tilâvetini veya her ikisini bizzat kitabımızla nesh edersek

ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r3.claim: Under another reading, God can have the Prophet abrogate a verse through his Sunnah.
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r3.anchor: diğer kıraate göre- Resûlümüze sünnetiyle nesh ettirirsek

ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r4.claim: The phrase can mean making a verse forgotten and erasing it from memory, or, in another reading, delaying the implementation of its rulings.

ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r5.claim: God brings something better or at least equal; these forms of legal abrogation are purposeful, never absurd, sheer neglect, or deficiency.
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r5.anchor: İşte nesh-i şer‘î bu aksâm tahtında cereyan eder ve hiçbiri abes değildir.

ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r6.claim: The Prophet knows God's omnipotence, and this knowledge has grounds rather than resting without proof.
ELMALILI:2:106-113#2/r6.anchor: Bilirsin ve bu ilim burhansız, beyyinesiz de değildir.

MAJAZ:v1p49/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p49/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p49/r2.claim: Naskh here means replacing the abrogated verse with another verse.
MAJAZ:v1p49/r2.anchor: ما ننسخ من آية» (106) أي: ننسخها بآية أخرى

MAJAZ:v1p49/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p49/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p49/r3.claim: Without hamza, nunsihā is from forgetting and means removing the verse; with hamza, nunsiʾhā is from postponement.
MAJAZ:v1p49/r3.anchor: «أو ننسها» من النسيان: [نذهب بها] ، ومن همزها جعلها من نؤخرها

MAJAZ:v1p49/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p49/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p49/r4.claim: A form read nansūhā means to let the verse pass or proceed; Jarīr’s ansaʾtukum and Ṭarafa’s saqtu camel-driving usage support postponing or sending onward.
MAJAZ:v1p49/r4.anchor: ومن قال: ننسوها كان مجازها تمضيها، وقال جرير: ولا أنسأتكم غضبى ونسأت الناقة: سقتها، وقال طرفة:

MAJAZ:v1p49/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p49/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p49/r5.claim: The promise means that God brings you something better than the abrogated verse.
MAJAZ:v1p49/r5.anchor: نأت بخير منها» (106) أي نأتيك منها بخير.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r1.claim: Naskh lexically means annul, remove, eliminate, or transfer; as a religious term it is repeal or replacement of a ruling by a later ruling.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r1.anchor: Sözlükte “iptal etmek, gidermek, yok etmek, nakletmek” gibi anlamlara gelen nesh (nesih), İslâmî bir terim olarak “dinî bir hükmün yürürlükten kaldırılması veya daha sonra gelen bir hükümle değiştirilmesi” anlamında kullanılır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r2.claim: Abrogation applies only to commands and prohibitions; the repealed ruling is mansukh and the repealing ruling is nasikh.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r2.anchor: Sadece buyruk ve yasaklarda nesih söz konusu olabilir. Ortadan kaldırılan hükme mensuh, onu ortadan kaldırana da nâsih denir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r3.claim: Scholars agree abrogation is rationally possible and occurred in earlier religions: the Gospel repealed some Torah rules, and the Qur'an changed or removed some rulings in both earlier scriptures.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r3.anchor: Prensip olarak neshin aklen mümkün olduğu, ayrıca diğer dinlerde de fiilen meydana geldiği hususunda görüşbirliği vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r4.claim: Some earlier Islamic rulings also changed as Islam developed; the commentary gives the Prophet's hadiths on visiting graves as an example.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r4.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in kabir ziyaretiyle ilgili hadislerinde olduğu gibi İslâm’ın gelişme sürecine bağlı olarak önceki bazı hükümler sonradan değiştirilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r5.claim: Whether the Qur'an contains abrogated verses is disputed: most scholars accept abrogation by later verses or hadiths, some reject it, and proposed counts range from five to two hundred.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r5.anchor: İslâm bilginlerinin çoğunluğu bâzı âyetlerin sonradan gelen başka âyetler veya hadislerle neshedildiğini savunurken bazı âlimler de bu görüşü reddetmişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r6.claim: The author favors the later scholars' view: unless final replacement is explicit, both differing rulings remain valid in their own circumstances and the applicable circumstance determines which governs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r6.anchor: Daha çok son dönem İslâm bilginlerinin tercih ettiği ve bizce de isabetli olan anlayışa göre bir konuda iki farklı hüküm içeren iki âyetten

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r7.claim: On this view, if the circumstances for one ruling never recur, it becomes impossible to apply it in practice, without requiring that its text or ruling was wholly annulled.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r7.anchor: eğer birinin şartları artık sonsuz olarak tekrar doğmazsa pratikte o hükmü uygulamaya da imkân bulunmayacağını düşünmek daha isabetli görülmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r8.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r8.claim: Shawkani reports that those reading the verb as nansa(hā) understand it to mean delaying the abrogation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r8.anchor: Şevkânî’nin özetlediği bilgilere göre söz konusu fiili “nense (hâ)” şeklinde okuyanlara göre âyette bu fiil, “(neshedilmesini) ertelersek” anlamında kullanılmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r9.claim: The authors prefer the nunsi(hā) reading, which they explain as leaving the verse unchanged and unabrogated or allowing it to be abrogated.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r9.anchor: Bizim de tercih ettiğimiz “nünsi(hâ)” şeklindeki okunuşa göre bu ifade, “... o âyeti (değiştirmeden, neshetmeden) olduğu gibi bırakırsak” veya “o âyetin yürürlükten kaldırılmasına izin verirsek” şeklinde açıklanmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r10.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r10.claim: Shawkani says the second interpretation, allowing repeal, is the one most scholars of language and rational inquiry accept.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r10.anchor: Şevkânî, son yorumun, “lugat ve nazar ehlinin çoğunluğunun üzerinde birleştiği yorum” olduğunu söyler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r11.claim: The phrase may also refer to divine messages in earlier scriptures being made to be forgotten, so they did not pass into later books and reports.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:106/r11.anchor: Buradaki “unutturma” ifadesiyle, geçmiş dinlere ait kitaplarda bulunan ilâhî mesajların unutturulması, yani sonraki kitaplara ve rivayetlere hiç intikal etmemesi de kastedilmiş olabilir.

NAHHAS:v1p253/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p253/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p253/r10.claim: The clause is conditional and «نأت» is its response.

NAHHAS:v1p253/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p253/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p253/r11.claim: «أو ننسها» is coordinated to «ننسخ»; its final yāʾ is dropped because the verb is jussive.
NAHHAS:v1p253/r11.anchor: وقوله ( أو ننسها ) عطف على ننسخ وحذفت الياء للجزم

NAHHAS:v1p253/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p253/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p253/r12.claim: The alternate «أو ننسأها» drops the hamza's ḍamma under the jussive.
NAHHAS:v1p253/r12.anchor: ومن قرأ ( أو ننسأها ) حذف الضمة من الهمزة للجزم

NAHHAS:v1p253/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p253/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p253/r13.claim: «لم» makes the verb jussive; the interrogative does not alter the governing particle, and «أن» is fatḥa because it occupies a noun position.
NAHHAS:v1p253/r13.anchor: ( ألم تعلم أن ) جزم بلم وحرف الاستفهام لا يغير عمل العامل وفتحت أن لأنها في موضع اسم

BURHAN:v2p30/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r1.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p30/r1.claim: One view defines abrogation as lifting both the recitation of a revealed text and its practical force.
BURHAN:v2p30/r1.anchor: فقيل المنسوخ ما رفع تلاوة تنزيله كما رفع العمل به

BURHAN:v2p30/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p30/r2.claim: The author rebuts that definition by noting that the Qurʾan abrogated the Torah while the Torah and Gospel remain recited.
BURHAN:v2p30/r2.anchor: ورد بما نسخ الله من التوراة بالقرآن والإنجيل وهما متلوان

BURHAN:v2p30/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r3.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p30/r3.claim: Another view denies abrogation in revealed Qurʾan that is recited, and regards abrogation as a divinely granted easing for this community.
BURHAN:v2p30/r3.anchor: وقيل لا يقع النسخ في قرآن يتلى وينزل والنسخ مما خص الله به هذه الأمة

BURHAN:v2p30/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p30/r4.claim: The author rejects the claim that post-revelation abrogation entails a change of mind, calling it a mistaken Jewish assumption.
BURHAN:v2p30/r4.anchor: منهم أنه بداء كالذي يرى الرأي ثم يبدو له وهو باطل

BURHAN:v2p30/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p30/r5.claim: Abrogation clarifies a ruling’s duration, as changing life, health, or wealth does not imply a change of mind; the same applies to commands and prohibitions.
BURHAN:v2p30/r5.anchor: لأنه بيان مدة الحكم ألا ترى الإحياء بعد الإماتة وعكسه والمرض بعد الصحة وعكسه والفقر بعد الغنى

BURHAN:v2p30/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r6.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p30/r6.claim: A further view says God copied the Qurʾan from the Preserved Tablet, the Mother of the Book, since abrogation comes only from an original.
BURHAN:v2p30/r6.anchor: وقيل إن الله تعالى نسخ القرآن من اللوح المحفوظ الذي هو أم الكتاب

BURHAN:v2p30/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p30/r7.claim: The author’s preferred position is that abrogation is both legally permitted and actually established by transmitted evidence and reason.
BURHAN:v2p30/r7.anchor: والصحيح جواز النسخ ووقوعه سمعا وعقلا

BURHAN:v2p30/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r8.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p30/r8.claim: One position allows Qurʾan to be abrogated only by Qurʾan, reasoning that nothing but Qurʾan can be equal or better than it.
BURHAN:v2p30/r8.anchor: فقيل لا ينسخ قرآن إلا بقرآن

BURHAN:v2p30/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r9.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p30/r9.claim: Another position says the Sunna does not abrogate the Sunna.
BURHAN:v2p30/r9.anchor: وقيل بل السنة لا تنسخ السنة

BURHAN:v2p30/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r10.speaker: ابن حبيب النيسابوري
BURHAN:v2p30/r10.claim: Ibn Habib al-Nisaburi says Sunna revealed by God can abrogate, whereas Sunna based on independent reasoning cannot.
BURHAN:v2p30/r10.anchor: وقيل السنة إذا كانت بأمر الله من طريق الوحي نسخت وإن كانت باجتهاد فلا تنسخه حكاه ابن حبيب النيسابوري في تفسيره

BURHAN:v2p30/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r11.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p30/r11.claim: A further position allows either the Qurʾan or Sunna to abrogate the other.

BURHAN:v2p30/r14.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p30/r14.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p30/r14.claim: Another view holds that revelation sent down in Medina abrogates what was revealed in Mecca.
BURHAN:v2p30/r14.anchor: وقيل ما نزل بالمدينة ناسخ لما نزل بمكة

BURHAN:v2p32/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p32/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p32/r1.claim: There is no disagreement that Qurʾan abrogates Qurʾan; the author cites both 2:106 and 16:101.
BURHAN:v2p32/r1.anchor: لا خلاف في جواز نسخ الكتاب بالكتاب

BURHAN:v2p32/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p32/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p32/r2.claim: The Qurʾan can also abrogate Sunna, as the fast of ʿAshura was displaced by Ramadan fasting.
BURHAN:v2p32/r2.anchor: ولذلك نسخ السنة بالكتاب كالقصة في صوم عاشوراء برمضان وغيره

BURHAN:v2p32/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p32/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
BURHAN:v2p32/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya says leading scholars permit the Qurʾan to abrogate Sunna, citing the report “No bequest to an heir.”
BURHAN:v2p32/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية حذاق الأمة على الجواز

BURHAN:v2p32/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p32/r4.speaker: الشافعي
BURHAN:v2p32/r4.claim: Al-Shafiʿi rejects Qurʾan abrogating Sunna; Ibn ʿAtiyya argues that only the Prophet’s Sunna removed flogging from the stoning punishment for a married adulterer.
BURHAN:v2p32/r4.anchor: والحجة عليه من قوله في إسقاط الجلد في حد الزنا عن الثيب الذي رجم

BURHAN:v2p32/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p32/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p32/r6.claim: The author says al-Shafiʿi’s apparent wording was misunderstood: Qurʾan and Sunna never conflict without a like-kind text abrogating one, which shows their mutual support.
BURHAN:v2p32/r6.anchor: وإنما مراد الشافعي أن الكتاب والسنة لا يوجدان مختلفين إلا ومع أحدهما مثله ناسخ له

BURHAN:v2p32/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p32/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p32/r7.claim: The author calls the alleged Sunna abrogation of the stoning verse specification, supported by a Qurʾanic text whose recitation was abrogated.
BURHAN:v2p32/r7.anchor: وأما النسخ بالآية فليس بنسخ بل تخصيص ثم إنه ثابت بالقرآن الذي نسخت تلاوته

BURHAN:v2p32/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p32/r8.speaker: الجمهور
BURHAN:v2p32/r8.claim: The majority restricts abrogation to commands and prohibitions; some add reports, while others limit those reports to ones intended as commands or prohibitions.
BURHAN:v2p32/r8.anchor: الجمهور على أنه لا يقع النسخ إلا في الأمر والنهي وزاد بعضهم الأخبار وأطلق وقيدها آخرون

BURHAN:v2p32/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p32/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p32/r9.claim: The author’s first category in a classification contains 43 surahs with neither abrogating nor abrogated passages, beginning with al-Fatiha and including Yusuf and Ya Sin.
BURHAN:v2p32/r9.anchor: أحدهما ما ليس فيه ناسخ ولا منسوخ وهي ثلاث وأربعون سورة وهي الفاتحة ثم يوسف ثم يس

BURHAN:v2p43/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p43/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p43/r1.claim: Rules of restraint in weakness and fighting when strong both return when their causes recur; neither abrogates the other, and each applies in its proper time.
BURHAN:v2p43/r1.anchor: وليس حكم المسايفة ناسخا لحكم المسالمة بل كل منهما يجب امتثاله في وقته

BURHAN:v2p43/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p43/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p43/r2.claim: One explanation for saying “any verse” rather than “the Qurʾan” is that the Qurʾan supersedes all earlier books and has no later abrogator.
BURHAN:v2p43/r2.anchor: ولم يقل ( من القرآن ) لأن القرآن ناسخ مهيمن

BURHAN:v2p43/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p43/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p43/r3.claim: The author says actual Qurʾanic abrogation is rare and explicitly identified, citing alms before private counsel, waiting periods, and retreat in battle.
BURHAN:v2p43/r3.anchor: وما فيه من ناسخ ومنسوخ فمعلوم وهو قليل بين الله ناسخه عند منسوخه كنسخ الصدقة عند مناجاة الرسول والعدة والفرار في الجهاد

BURHAN:v2p43/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p43/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p43/r4.claim: Many supposed cases are postponement, or explanation of a general ruling; the Sunna explains the Qurʾan, as stated in 16:44.
BURHAN:v2p43/r4.anchor: وأما غير ذلك فمن تحقق علما بالنسخ علم أن غالب ذلك من المنسأ ومنه ما يرجع لبيان الحكم المجمل

BURHAN:v2p43/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p43/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p43/r5.claim: Claims of Qurʾanic abrogation often mistake postponement, delayed clarification, intervening discourse, specification, or general and particular rulings for abrogation.
BURHAN:v2p43/r5.anchor: فليس بنسخ وإنما هو نسأ وتأخير أو مجمل أخر بيانه لوقت الحاجة أو خطاب قد حال بينه وبين أوله خطاب غيره

BURHAN:v4p418/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p418/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p418/r7.claim: After “ma” and “mahما,” “min” often heightens their extreme indefiniteness; the preposition and its complement function circumstantially.
BURHAN:v4p418/r7.anchor: وكثيرا ما تقع بعد ما ومهما لإفراط إبهامهما

BURHAN:v2p42/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p42/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p42/r1.claim: Commands tied to a temporary cause, such as patience during weakness, are deferred when the cause changes; this is “nasʾ,” not abrogation.
BURHAN:v2p42/r1.anchor: الثالث ما أمر به لسبب ثم يزول السبب

BURHAN:v2p42/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p42/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p42/r2.claim: Verses enjoining leniency are not abrogated by the sword verse: each command applies while its cause lasts, whereas abrogation permanently removes a ruling.
BURHAN:v2p42/r2.anchor: تبين ضعف ما لهج به كثير من المفسرين في الآيات الآمرة بالتخفيف أنها منسوخة بآية السيف وليست كذلك بل هي من المنسأ

BURHAN:v2p42/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p42/r3.speaker: الشافعي
