BURHAN:v2p42/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi’s example is the ban on storing sacrificial meat from compassion, later lifted; it can return if needy people again require it.
BURHAN:v2p42/r3.anchor: أشار الشافعي في ( الرسالة ) إلى النهي عن ادخار لحوم الأضاحي

BURHAN:v1p440/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p440/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p440/r1.claim: As God’s speech, no part of the Qurʾan is inherently superior; talk of parts is figurative, while its varied discourse meets hearers’ needs through interpretation and understanding.
BURHAN:v1p440/r1.anchor: من حيث أنه كلام الله لا مزية لشىء منه على شىء ثم قولنا شىء منه يوهم التبعيض وليس لكلام الله الذى هو صفته بعض

BURHAN:v1p440/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p440/r2.speaker: الحليمي
BURHAN:v1p440/r2.claim: Al-Halimi allows preference among surahs and verses, interpreting “better” as the later operative verse when one of two recited rulings abrogates the other.
BURHAN:v1p440/r2.anchor: وقال الحليمي قد ذكرنا أخبار تدل على جوار المفاضلة

BURHAN:v1p440/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p440/r3.speaker: الحليمي
BURHAN:v1p440/r3.claim: Al-Halimi says commands, prohibitions, promises, and warnings benefit people more than narratives, which support those essential teachings and can be dispensed with.
BURHAN:v1p440/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا فيقال آيات الأمر والنهى والوعد والوعيد خير من آيات القصص لأن القصص إنما أريد بها تأكيد الأمر والنهى

BURHAN:v1p440/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p440/r4.speaker: الحليمي
BURHAN:v1p440/r4.claim: Al-Halimi also calls verses naming God and describing His attributes better in the sense that their subject matter is more exalted.
BURHAN:v1p440/r4.anchor: والثانى أن يقال إن الآيات التى تشتمل على تعديد أسماء الله تعالى وبيان صفاته والدلالة على عظمته وقدسيته أفضل

BURHAN:v1p440/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p440/r5.speaker: الحليمي
BURHAN:v1p440/r5.claim: Al-Halimi’s third sense is immediate benefit beyond future reward: Ayat al-Kursi, al-Ikhlas, and the Muʿawwidhatayn provide protection and worship through divine names and attributes.
BURHAN:v1p440/r5.anchor: والثالث أن يقال سورة خير من سورة أو آية خير من آية بمعنى أن القارىء يتعجل بقراءتها فائدة سوى الثواب الآجل

ITQAN:v3p71/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p71/r1.speaker: ابن الحصار
ITQAN:v3p71/r1.claim: Ibn al-Hassar answers that nothing is abrogated without replacement: extant Qur'anic material replaces recitation that was abrogated, and what God abrogated from the Qur'an was replaced by wording and meaning transmitted to us mutawatir.
ITQAN:v3p71/r1.anchor: قال ابن الحصار في هذا النوع إن قيل كيف يقع النسخ إلى غير بدل

ITQAN:v1p173/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r1.speaker: جماعة
ITQAN:v1p173/r1.claim: Some define the seven long surahs as beginning with al-Baqara and ending with Bara'a.
ITQAN:v1p173/r1.anchor: السبع الطوال أولها البقرة وآخرها براءة كذا قال جماعة

ITQAN:v1p173/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p173/r2.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas lists al-Baqara, Al Imran, al-Nisa, al-Ma'ida, al-An'am, and al-A'raf; its narrator forgot the seventh.
ITQAN:v1p173/r2.anchor: لكن أخرج الحاكم والنسائي وغيرهما عن ابن عباس قال السبع الطوال

ITQAN:v1p173/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v1p173/r3.claim: A sound report from Sa'id ibn Jubayr identifies Yunus as the seventh long surah; an earlier report from Ibn Abbas agrees.
ITQAN:v1p173/r3.anchor: وفي رواية صحيحة عن ابن أبي حاتم وغيره عن سعيد بن جبير أنها يونس وتقدم عن ابن عباس مثله

ITQAN:v1p173/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r4.speaker: الحاكم
ITQAN:v1p173/r4.claim: Another report recorded by al-Hakim gives al-Kahf as the seventh long surah.
ITQAN:v1p173/r4.anchor: وفي رواية عند الحاكم أنها الكهف

ITQAN:v1p173/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p173/r5.claim: The mi'un are the surahs after the seven long ones, named because each exceeds or approaches one hundred verses.
ITQAN:v1p173/r5.anchor: والمئون ما وليها سميت بذلك لأن كل سورة منها تزيد على مائة آية أو تقاربها

ITQAN:v1p173/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p173/r6.claim: The mathani follow the mi'un; the name can mean they come second to the mi'un, which precede them.
ITQAN:v1p173/r6.anchor: والمثاني ما ولي المئين لأنها ثنتها أي كانت بعدها فهي لها ثوان والمئون لها أوائل

ITQAN:v1p173/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r7.speaker: الفراء
ITQAN:v1p173/r7.claim: Al-Farra defines the mathani as surahs under one hundred verses because they are recited more often than the long and hundred-verse groups.
ITQAN:v1p173/r7.anchor: وقال الفراء هي السورة التي آيها أقل من مائة لأنها تثنى أكثر مما يثنى الطوال والمئون

ITQAN:v1p173/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r8.speaker: النكزاوي
ITQAN:v1p173/r8.claim: Another explanation for mathani is that their examples repeat lessons and reports.
ITQAN:v1p173/r8.anchor: وقيل لتثنية الأمثال فيها بالعبر والخبر حكاه النكزاوي

ITQAN:v1p173/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r9.speaker: جمال القراء
ITQAN:v1p173/r9.claim: Jamal al-Qurra defines mathani as surahs in which stories are repeated; the term can also refer to the whole Qur'an or to al-Fatiha.
ITQAN:v1p173/r9.anchor: وقال في جمال القراء هي السور التي ثنيت فيها القصص وقد تطلق على القرآن كله وعلى الفاتحة

ITQAN:v1p173/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p173/r10.claim: The mufassal follows the mathani and consists of short surahs; its name is attributed to the many basmala divisions between surahs or to its small amount of abrogated material.
ITQAN:v1p173/r10.anchor: والمفصل ما ولي المثاني من قصار السور سمي بذلك لكثرة الفصول التي بين السور بالبسملة وقيل لقلة المنسوخ منه

ITQAN:v1p173/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v1p173/r11.claim: A Bukhari report from Sa'id ibn Jubayr calls the mufassal the muhkam, and its ending at Surat al-Nas is undisputed.
ITQAN:v1p173/r11.anchor: كما روى البخاري عن سعيد بن جبير قال إن الذي تدعونه المفصل هو المحكم وآخره سورة الناس بلا نزاع

ITQAN:v1p173/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r12.speaker: أوس
ITQAN:v1p173/r12.claim: One reported view begins the mufassal at Qaf, based on an earlier hadith from Aws.
ITQAN:v1p173/r12.anchor: أحدها ق لحديث أوس السابق قريبا

ITQAN:v1p173/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r13.speaker: النووي
ITQAN:v1p173/r13.claim: Al-Nawawi authenticates the view that al-Hujurat begins the mufassal.

ITQAN:v1p173/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r14.speaker: الأكثرون
ITQAN:v1p173/r14.claim: Al-Mawardi attributes to most scholars the view that Surat al-Qital (Muhammad) begins the mufassal.

ITQAN:v1p173/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r15.speaker: القاضي عياض
ITQAN:v1p173/r15.claim: Al-Qadi Iyad reports a view that al-Jathiya begins the mufassal.

ITQAN:v1p173/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r16.speaker: ابن أبي الصيف اليمني
ITQAN:v1p173/r16.claim: Ibn Abi al-Sayf al-Yamani reports the views that al-Saffat, al-Saff, or Tabarak begins the mufassal.
ITQAN:v1p173/r16.anchor: حكى الثلاثة ابن أبي الصيف اليمني

ITQAN:v1p173/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r17.speaker: الكمال الذماري
ITQAN:v1p173/r17.claim: Al-Kamal al-Dhimari reports that Surat al-Fath begins the mufassal.
ITQAN:v1p173/r17.anchor: الثامن الفتح حكاه الكمال الذماري في شرح التنبيه

ITQAN:v1p173/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r18.speaker: ابن السيد
ITQAN:v1p173/r18.claim: Ibn al-Sayyid reports that Surat al-Rahman begins the mufassal.
ITQAN:v1p173/r18.anchor: التاسع الرحمن حكاه ابن السيد في أمياله على الموطأ

ITQAN:v1p173/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r19.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p173/r19.claim: Another listed view begins the mufassal at al-Insan.

ITQAN:v1p173/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r20.speaker: ابن الفركاح
ITQAN:v1p173/r20.claim: Ibn al-Firkah reports from al-Marzuki the view that Surat Sabbih begins the mufassal.
ITQAN:v1p173/r20.anchor: الحادي عشر سبح حكاه ابن الفركاح في تعليقه عن المرزوقي

ITQAN:v1p173/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r21.speaker: الخطابي
ITQAN:v1p173/r21.claim: Al-Khattabi argues for al-Duha as the start because reciters separate these surahs with takbir; al-Raghib instead calls the final seven surahs the mufassal.
ITQAN:v1p173/r21.anchor: الثاني عشر الضحى حكاه الخطابي ووجهه بأن القارئ يفصل بين هذه السور بالتكبير

ITQAN:v1p173/r22.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p173/r22.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v1p173/r22.claim: Al-Raghib uses mufassal for the final seven surahs of the Qur'an.
ITQAN:v1p173/r22.anchor: وعبارة الراغب في مفرداته المفصل من القرآن السبع الأخير

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p24/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p24/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p24/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that revelation sometimes came to the Prophet at night and he forgot it by day; this verse was then revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p24/r3.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال كان ربما ينزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم الوحي بالليل ونسيه بالنهار

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p34/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p34/r2.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p34/r2.claim: Commentators report that polytheists accused Muhammad of contradicting himself by issuing and then reversing commands, and called the Quran his own contradictory speech; this verse and 16:101 answered them.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p34/r2.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن المشركين قالوا: أترون إلى محمد يأمر أصحابه، بأمر ثم ينهاهم عنه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r1.claim: In Arabic, āya means a sign; it can also denote a group of Qur’anic letters.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r1.anchor: الآية في اللغة : العلامة . وقد يقال : الآية ويراد بها : جماعة حروف من القرآن

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines an āya as a group of letters.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r2.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الآية : جماعة حروف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r3.speaker: الشيباني
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r3.claim: Al-Shaybānī’s usage خرج القوم بآيتهم means that the group went out together.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r3.anchor: وقد حكي عن الشيباني ، أنه قال : خرج القوم بآيتهم ، أي : بجماعتهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj gives the forms āya, āy, and āyāt.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج : يقال آية وآي ، وآيات

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r10.claim: Āya can mean a bounded unit of Qur’anic text called a verse.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r10.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الآية في القرآن على ستة أوجه : -

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r16.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r16.claim: Khayr can mean more beneficial, describing a replacement verse.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p285/r16.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الخير في القرآن على اثنين وعشرين وجها : -

TABATABAI:2:21-25#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#9/r2.speaker: المعترض
TABATABAI:2:21-25#9/r2.claim: The objection asks whether Qur'anic abrogation, which the Qur'an itself acknowledges, constitutes a change in judgment and therefore inconsistency.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#9/r2.anchor: فإن قلت فما تقول في النسخ الواقع في القرآن وقد نص عليه القرآن نفسه في قوله ما ننسخ من آية أو ننسها

BURHAN:v4p400/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p400/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p400/r8.claim: Conditional ma takes the front of the clause and is governed by the following verb, as in the cited conditions about abrogation and good deeds.
BURHAN:v4p400/r8.anchor: الثاني الشرطية ولها صدر الكلام ويعمل فيها ما بعدها من الفعل

BURHAN:v2p159/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p159/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p159/r4.claim: An exegete's illustrative application of a verse should not be mistaken for restricting the verse to that example; the author mentions a rebuke over al-Shadhili's application.
BURHAN:v2p159/r4.anchor: ولقد بلغني عن شخص انه انكر على الشيخ أبي الحسن الشاذلي

BURHAN:v2p28/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p28/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p28/r6.claim: Naskh can mean removal, as in God's removing what Satan casts.
BURHAN:v2p28/r6.anchor: والنسخ يأتي بمعنى الإزالة ومنه قوله تعالى

BURHAN:v2p337/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p337/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p337/r12.claim: Some also classify ‘do you not know that God is capable of all things?’ as an interrogative that commands belief or recognition.

BURHAN:v2p331/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p331/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p331/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير as a report question.
BURHAN:v2p331/r11.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري منه ﴿ ألم تعلم أن الله على كل شيء قدير ﴾ 5

BURHAN:v2p331/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p331/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p331/r12.claim: The author prefers reading the question as a rebuke to the denier of abrogation, rather than as a report based on the clause after the negative.
BURHAN:v2p331/r12.anchor: والاولى ان يجعل على الانكار أي الم تعلم ايها المنكر للنسخ

BURHAN:v2p331/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p331/r13.speaker: ابن السراج
BURHAN:v2p331/r13.claim: Ibn al-Sarrāj says putting the interrogative hamza on ليس gives an affirmative report; this is why أحد, which suits genuine negation, is awkward in أليس أحد في الدار.
BURHAN:v2p331/r13.anchor: قول ابن السراج فاذا ادخلت على ليس الف الاستفهام كانت تقريرا ودخلها معنى الايجاب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p579#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p579#2/r2.speaker: من لم يهمز
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p579#2/r2.claim: The form nunsihā in 2:106 is cited on the reading of those who do not hamza.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r1.speaker: مجاهد
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r1.claim: A third account of abrogation keeps an earlier verse written and recited while changing its ruling; Mujāhid is reported to say its wording remains and its ruling is replaced, like 60:11.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r1.anchor: وهو ما حكي عن مجاهد أنه قال: يثبت خطها ويبدل حكمها

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r2.claim: For the reading ننسها from forgetting, the verb can mean either leaving something or forgetting it in the opposite-of-remembering sense.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p188/r2.anchor: وأما من قرأ ننسها من النسيان فإن لفظ (نسي) المنقول منه أنسي على ضربين

JISHUMI:v1p646/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p646/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p646/r1.claim: The statement that God abrogates verses refutes the denial of abrogation, while the qibla question itself shows a community was turned from one qibla to another.
JISHUMI:v1p646/r1.anchor: أما الكتاب فقوله تعالى: (ما ننسخ من آية) يدل على بطلان قوله، وقوله: سيقول السفهاء

JISHUMI:v1p538/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p538/r1.claim: The hamzated reading nunsaʾhā means delaying revelation, either not sending the verse and replacing its benefit or deferring it so another verse serves in its place.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r1.anchor: قراءة وننسأها على قراءة الهمز أي نؤخرها فلا ننزلها أصلا

JISHUMI:v1p538/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p538/r2.claim: Nansakh means removing a verse after its revelation.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r2.anchor: الثالث: ما ننسخ من آية أي نرفعها، وننسخها بعد إنزالها.

JISHUMI:v1p538/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p538/r3.claim: On nunsihā, God leaves a verse in place rather than abrogating it, so people continue to act by it.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r3.anchor: وعلى قراءة ننسها نتركها فلا نرفعها، بل نبقيها على حالها

JISHUMI:v1p538/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r4.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p538/r4.claim: Al-Aṣamm takes abrogation as abrogating by a book and nunsihā as ordering people to stop acting on a verse whose ruling was abrogated.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r4.anchor: ما ننسخ من آية بكتاب أو ننسها نأمر بترك العمل بها

JISHUMI:v1p538/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r5.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v1p538/r5.anchor: وننسها: قيل: من النسيان، عن قتادة، وقيل:

JISHUMI:v1p538/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p538/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās understands nunsihā as leaving or abandoning.

JISHUMI:v1p538/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r7.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p538/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī says a community can forget recitation over time after being instructed to stop reciting it.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r7.anchor: إذا أمر بترك تلاوته نسي على مرور الأيام، عن أبي علي،

JISHUMI:v1p538/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p538/r8.claim: An unnamed report says the forgotten recitation was a miracle for the Prophet: people read a sūra, then awoke having forgotten it.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r8.anchor: وقيل: يكون ذلك معجزا للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ورووا في ذلك خبرا أنهم كانوا

JISHUMI:v1p538/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p538/r9.claim: A second approach reads abrogation as removing a verse from the Preserved Tablet or delaying it, and nunsihā as leaving it unabrogated.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r9.anchor: فأما من قال بالقول الثاني ما ننسخ من آية أي ما ننسخها من اللوح المحفوظ

JISHUMI:v1p538/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p538/r10.claim: Abū Muslim applies “verse” to Torah and Gospel laws and denies Qur’anic abrogation; the author says consensus refutes that denial.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r10.anchor: غير أبي مسلم فإنه حمل ذلك على التوراة والإنجيل وأحكامها، والشرائع التي فيها

JISHUMI:v1p538/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p538/r11.claim: “Better” may mean easier, as in the relaxation of battle obligations, or equally easy, as with turning toward the Kaʿba.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r11.anchor: قيل: في التسهيل وفي التيسير نحو قوله: (الآن خفف الله عنكم) في الجهاد، أو مثلها في السهولة كالتوجه إلى الكعبة، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p538/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r12.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p538/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan understands better or equivalent as having the same beneficial quality at the earlier time.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r12.anchor: وقيل: بخير منها في الوقت الأول في الصلاح أو مثلها في ذلك، عن الحسن،

JISHUMI:v1p538/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r13.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p538/r13.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the address may be to the Prophet while meaning all accountable people, or to any hearer or human being.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r13.anchor: قيل: خطاب للرسول، والمراد جميع المكلفين، وقيل: أراد ألم تعلم أيها السامع

JISHUMI:v1p538/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p538/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p538/r14.claim: The phrase may be general or mean that God can support the Prophet and take vengeance on his enemies.
JISHUMI:v1p538/r14.anchor: وقيل: هو عام في كل شيء، وقيل: ألم تعلم أنه تكفل بنصرك
